title: ABCD Reads Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***Yesteryear*** by Caro Claire Burke.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/4849281772290048) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"A traditional American woman, a beautiful wife and mother who sells her pioneer lifestyle of raw milk and farm-fresh eggs to her millions of social media followers, suddenly awakens cold, filthy, and terrified in the brutal reality of 1855—where she must unravel whether this living nightmare is an elaborate hoax, a twisted reality show, or something far more sinister." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/yesteryear/))

"The chasm between social media and reality runs deep and dark in Caro Claire Burke’s debut novel, “Yesteryear,” which crawls into the psyche of a tradwife influencer so maddening and mesmerizing that Anne Hathaway has already signed on to play her in the movie adaptation.
“Sometimes it actually made me sick,” Natalie Heller Mills narrates, “how perfect my life was, and how good I was at living it.” Note her use of the past tense." (from [New York Times Book Review](https://archive.ph/WHSQ6#selection-753.0-764.0))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). title: Civic Meetup #570: "Invaders,” “Polluters,” and “Predators”: Anti-South Asian Racism in Canadian Far-Right Digital Networks
location: Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom
description:
Topic: "Invaders,” “Polluters,” and “Predators”: Anti-South Asian Racism in Canadian Far-Right Digital Networks

How do Canadian far-right groups portray South Asians on social media? Drawing on data collected from Canadian far-right networks on X (formerly Twitter), the analysis focuses on depictions of South Asians as “invaders,” “polluters,” and “predators,” and explores how emotions like fear and disgust are used​​ to frame South Asians as outsiders and perceived threats to Canada.

‎

Speaker: Dr. Zeinab Farokhi (in-person)

Dr. Zeinab Farokhi is an Assistant Professor of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies at the University of Toronto Mississauga. Her upcoming book, Digital Islamophobia,  explores the gendered and affective dimensions of anti-Muslim sentiments across Canada, the United States, and India.

title: Jeff Chang: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents award-winning author Jeff Chang in conversation with Vinh Nguyen at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon, celebrating what would have been Bruce Lee's birthday.
More than half a century after his death, Bruce Lee remains as towering a figure as ever, the man who popularized martial arts in the West, became a bridge between Eastern and Western culture, and was poised to conquer Hollywood when he died suddenly at age thirty-two. But in the decades since, his legend has eclipsed the man. Forgotten is the immigrant, the fighter, the seeker, the teacher, the father grappling with exile and belonging in a country that questioned his right to simply exist.
In his epic new cultural biography
Water Mirror Echo: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
, acclaimed author Jeff Chang recovers the man behind the icon. Drawing on in-depth interviews with Lee's closest intimates, thousands of newly available personal documents, and dozens of rare photographs from the family archive, Chang traces Lee's remarkable journey: a charismatic child star turned delinquent teen fighter in Hong Kong, exiled alone to America, who transformed personal struggle into a philosophy of movement and being. Chang reveals how Lee's rise didn't just create a Hollywood legend, it helped birth something even more enduring: the very concept of Asian America.
Join Jeff Chang for a special evening honouring Bruce Lee's birthday, offering a stirringly human portrait of the icon, the immigrant, and the movement he unknowingly ignited.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre, 50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: [In]Security: Military Portraiture of Gertrude Kearns
location: Joan Goldfarb Study Centre, 275 Joan & Martin Goldfarb Centre for Fine Arts @ 86 Fine Arts Road, Toronto
description: [In] Security, evokes the tensions between protection and vulnerability, certainty and instability. Made between 2002 and 2026, these works are portraits of real people: Canadian Armed Forces senior officers at critical moments in Canada’s military history. They are also records of the systems around them. Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

description:
This presentation introduces an innovative approach to experiential education and planetary learning, developed within a long-standing research partnership between the University of Antioquia in Medellín, Colombia, and the University of Education in Bern, Switzerland. The approach draws on Latin American critical theory and on the experience of Colombia’s Movimiento Pedagógico Nacional, a large-scale social movement of the 1980s and 1990s which organized so-called National Educational Expeditions: researchers and university professors, activists, school teachers and students explored together the relation between neoliberal educational restructuring and the sharpening sociospatial inequality and violence in the country.
Transnational Educational Expeditions formed the core of our approach to experiential education. In these expeditions, a binational team of practitioners, researchers and students, made up of equal numbers from both partner universities, jointly carried out ethnographic research, first in Switzerland and then in Colombia. Through these expeditions, we explored how public schooling contributes both to reproducing and to transforming urban inequality in contexts of migration in the two countries.
The approach is innovative in that it examines social fields in Colombia and Switzerland through each other, making the systematic contrast of nationally situated perspectives a productive resource in the co-production of knowledge.

Join us for an engaging Industry Talk featuring Scott Hendershot, Senior Manager of the Sustainability Office at the University of Toronto’s St. George Campus.
Wednesday, November 25. 2026
5 – 7 p.m.
BA2155
Pizza provided – All students welcome 
Register here 
Scott leads U of T’s Sustainability Office, driving initiatives that embed sustainability into campus operations, decision-making, and the student experience. With over 30 years of professional experience and more than a decade of leadership in sustainability strategy, Scott brings a wealth of practical insight on creating meaningful and lasting change. 
As a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) and Sustainability Excellence Associate (SEA), Scott will share his perspectives on advancing sustainability in complex organizations, lessons from industry, and the role future engineers and leaders can play in building a more resilient future. 
Don’t miss this opportunity to learn from a sustainability leader and connect with fellow students over pizza! 
Speaker
Scott Hendershot
Senior Manager – Sustainability Office
University of Toronto – St. George Campus 
Scott Hendershot leads the Sustainability Office at the University of Toronto’s St. George Campus, providing strategic oversight and championing initiatives that advance sustainable change across the university and beyond. 
Working with a team of five Project Managers, Scott is focused on embedding sustainability into the fabric of campus operations, decision-making, and the student experience. His team collaborates across the institution to drive innovative solutions that support U of T’s sustainability goals and long-term resilience. 
Joining the University of Toronto in 2021, Scott brought with him more than 30 years of diverse professional experience from the private sector. Prior to U of T, he spent over a decade helping to develop and integrate sustainability strategies within the aviation industry, playing a leadership role in advancing sustainability and organizational change. 
Scott is a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) and Sustainability Excellence Associate (SEA) with a deep commitment to creating practical, lasting solutions for a more sustainable future.

title: Vibe Coding: Make Your Own Interactive Story with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if you could write a story where the reader chooses what happens, like a branching adventure, a mystery, or a game, and have AI build it with you?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll learn "vibe-coding": using an AI coding assistant to build your own interactive story or simple game. You'll design the branches, describe the rules in plain language, test for the tricky edge cases (what if the player picks the weird option?), and end up with a single file you can share with anyone. Just a story you want to tell. This is the playful sibling of the practical vibe-coding workshop.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.

title: Rédiger son testament avec l’Association du Barreau de l’Ontario
description:
Novembre est le Mois de la rédaction d’un testament (Make a Will Month), et la Bibliothèque publique de Toronto est heureuse d’accueillir l’Association du Barreau de l’Ontario pour une séance d’information sur l’importance de la planification successorale. Venez découvrir pourquoi il est essentiel de préparer un testament et des procurations afin de protéger vos intérêts et ceux de vos proches.
Un avocat spécialisé en droit des successions et des fiducies présentera les éléments clés d’un testament, expliquera les conséquences d’un décès sans testament, décrira les différents types de procurations et leur rôle, et abordera les points importants à considérer lors de la préparation de votre planification successorale et de vos directives en matière de soins.
Veuillez noter que cette séance a un caractère informatif et éducatif. Elle ne vise pas à fournir des conseils juridiques personnalisés, mais plutôt à offrir un aperçu général du droit et à vous aider à mieux comprendre comment un avocat peut vous accompagner afin que vos volontés soient respectées et mises en œuvre conformément à vos intentions.
Accessibilité:
Le sous-titrage en direct ou automatique, l’interprétation en langue des signes, les services d’intervenant, ou les services d’accompagnement sont disponibles sur demande. Veuillez soumettre votre demande au moins deux semaines à l’avance à : tpl.ca/accessibility-events

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesdays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: VCP presents LADY AUDLEY’S SECRET
location: Fred Thury Studio Theatre, 258 Vanier College
description:
An Original Version of Miss Braddon’s popular Novel,
In Two Acts
By C. H. Hazelwood
Adapted from the 1862 novel of the same name, Lady Audley’s Secret is a classic example of Victorian melodrama. Concerning the ambitious, unscrupulous Lady Audley who, in order to preserve her present situation is prepared, when an unwanted husband returns, to attempt to get rid of him in the garden well. But she is observed – and struggle and twist as she may, neither bribery nor attempted arson avail her. Nemesis overtakes her and tragedy ensues.
Find out what she is hiding and the lengths to which she will go to in order to protect Lady Audley’s Secret.
Directed by Jean-Paul Yovanoff
Stage Managed by Nicole Lisov

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Recovery College: YU & Balance Week 6 | Managing academic stress and exam anxiety
location: Virtual Event
description:
This session is open to students from York’s Markham and Glendon campuses.
Sometimes, a single grade can get inside your head and make you question your ability to succeed in your program. The pressure to earn high marks, often called “academic perfectionism”, is something many post-secondary students experience.
In this week’s session of YU & Balance, participants will explore how stress affects academic performance and learn practical strategies to manage it as you prepare for exam season. By the end of the session, participants will have tools to recognize stress, respond to it effectively, and protect your confidence during exams.
This session is part of a 6-week Recovery College series. For each session attended, participants will receive $5 on their YU-card. To receive the gift card, you must attend the full session (approximately 45–60 minutes). Unfortunately, we’re not able to provide gift cards for partial attendance. title: [In]Security: Military Portraiture of Gertrude Kearns
location: Joan Goldfarb Study Centre, 275 Joan & Martin Goldfarb Centre for Fine Arts @ 86 Fine Arts Road, Toronto
description: [In] Security, evokes the tensions between protection and vulnerability, certainty and instability. Made between 2002 and 2026, these works are portraits of real people: Canadian Armed Forces senior officers at critical moments in Canada’s military history. They are also records of the systems around them. Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Tubman Talks Roundtable: Decolonizing Knowledge Production in Ituri, North and South Kivu Provinces of the Democratic Republic of Congo: Extractivism, Environmental Governance, Gender Justice, and Community Knowledge
description:
Date: Thursday, November 26, 2026
Time: 2:00-3:30pm EST
Location: Virtual
Register here: https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/z7joamFfT3aKIAIwCsVaEw
Title: Decolonizing Knowledge Production in Ituri, North and South Kivu Provinces of the Democratic Republic of Congo: Extractivism, Environmental Governance, Gender Justice, and Community Knowledge
Abstract
The provinces of Ituri, North and South Kivu in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are shaped by complex intersections of resource extraction, environmental governance, armed conflict, gendered violence, and community resistance. Yet dominant institutional and external frameworks often produce knowledge about these realities in ways that marginalize local experiences, Indigenous and community-based knowledge, and the intellectual contributions of Congolese women. This presentation examines the possibilities and challenges of decolonizing knowledge production by centering locally grounded research, lived experiences, and community perspectives in understanding the political, environmental, and gendered dimensions of conflict in eastern DRC.
Bringing together complementary perspectives on extractivism and resource-related dynamics in Ituri, environmental governance and women’s agency in North Kivu, and gender justice, sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), as well as peacebuilding in the Kivus, the presentation explores how dominant knowledge systems shape understandings of conflict and whose voices are recognized as legitimate sources of knowledge. It further considers how community-based research, feminist and decolonial approaches, and survivor-centered practices can challenge extractive research relationships and support more accountable, inclusive, and transformative forms of knowledge production.
Rather than positioning Congolese communities only as research subjects or victims of conflict, the discussion recognizes them as knowledge holders, analysts, and active participants in shaping responses to violence, environmental harm, and social injustice. The session will conclude with an extended community dialogue, inviting participants to reflect on research ethics, representation, power, and the possibilities of building more reciprocal relationships between universities, researchers, and communities in the DRC and its diaspora.
The session will include 45 minutes of speaker presentations, followed by 45 minutes of community discussion and exchange. Creating space for collective reflection, the event aims to foster dialogue on how knowledge can help us understand the realities of eastern DRC and advance gender justice, environmental accountability, and locally grounded peacebuilding.
Keywords: Decolonizing knowledge; eastern Democratic Republic of Congo; Ituri; North and South Kivu; extractivism; environmental governance; feminist research; SGBV; community knowledge; peacebuilding.
 
Speakers: Rose Ukeci Uwodha, Borauzima Feza Esther and Kashoro Nyenyezi (All Congolese Scholars)
Bio of Presenters
Rose Ukeci Uwodha is a PhD candidate in sociology and anthropology at the University of Mons (Belgium). She will speak about Who Found the Gold? Extractivism and Community Knowledge in Kilo-Moto, Ituri. Her doctoral research examines discourse, power and resistance in the gold mining territory of Kilo-Moto, in north-eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. She studies how religious movements, artisanal miners, customary authorities and former combatants contest or reshapes the extractive order. Her work starts from the official history of the mine, which dates the “discovery” of gold to 1903, and the arrival of prospectors sent by the Congo Free State. This narrative erased the knowledge of the Ukebu people, who knew and worked the metal long before Europeans arrived, and it still shapes how the state, mining companies and donors speak about the mine. Against this background, she shows that the knowledge of local communities is political. For some religious movements, gold is alive and certain places are sacred. Artisanal miners create their own rules and techniques, and women miners organize in cooperatives to defend their place in a male-dominated sector. Her research also shows that “the local” is not homogeneous, since some customary authorities adopt the language of good governance to capture mining revenues. Taking community knowledge seriously without romanticizing it is at the heart of her approach.
 
Bora will be talking about Producing Knowledge with Women Working in and around Virunga National Park: A Global South Researcher’s Perspective on Armed Conflict Dynamics in Eastern DRC (Dissertation title?)
Borauzima Feza Esther is a Congolese (DRC) researcher with a Master’s degree in Political Science and a Specialized Master’s degree in Gender Studies. She teaches at the Official University of Bukavu and is a researcher with the Research Group on Conflict and Human Security. A PhD candidate in Sociology and Anthropology at the University of Mons, she conducts research on armed conflicts, gender, and natural resource governance around Virunga National Park in eastern DRC.
Her work examines how female agency is exercised or constrained in contexts of extreme precarity and vulnerability. In particular, she investigates the trajectories of women combatants involved in caregiving and the mystical-military practices of armed groups, former female combatants imprisoned on espionage charges, and women reselling forest resources in collaboration with armed groups. Her research draws on Afro-feminist, decolonial, and critical approaches. She also engages critically with the production of knowledge, North–South relations, and the ethical challenges of conducting research in sensitive contexts.
 
Dr. Kashoro’s contribution will focus on how sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), women’s experiences, and community knowledge can help us decolonize research and advance peacebuilding in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
Kashoro Nyenyezi is a scholar and community-based researcher whose work focuses on social justice, sexual and gender-based violence, feminist research, and peacebuilding in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and its diaspora. She holds a PhD in Social Justice Education from the Ontario Institute for Studies in Education (OISE), University of Toronto, and is an independent research fellow at York University’s Harriet Tubman Institute. Her research examines the intersections of land, gendered violence, power, and colonial legacies, with particular attention to the experiences and knowledge of women in conflict-affected communities. Through her research and community engagement with Helping Hand for Survivors, she advances survivor-centred, feminist, and decolonial approaches to understanding sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), promoting women’s agency, and strengthening community-led peacebuilding. Her work challenges approaches that position Congolese women and communities merely as subjects of research, instead recognizing them as knowledge producers whose experiences and perspectives are essential to understanding violence, advancing gender justice, and building sustainable peace. For this presentation, she brings an interdisciplinary perspective on how research can become more accountable to the communities whose lives and struggles it seeks to understand.

title: Book Launch: That Directionless Light of the Future, Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald
location: Art Metropole, 896 College Street, Toronto, ON M6H 1A4, Canada
description:
Please join us for a book launch of That Directionless Light of the Future: Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald with editor Jon Davies. Stop by to pick up a copy of the publication and enjoy refreshments and a drop-in signing with the editor. Join us for brief remarks at 6pm.

That Directionless Light of the Future: Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald is the first major publication devoted to artist Russell FitzGerald. Bringing together newly commissioned scholarship and more than 90 reproductions of paintings, drawings, illustrations, archival material the book offers the first comprehensive account of an artist whose ambitious vision has remained hidden for decades.

Edited by Canadian art historian and curator Jon Davies, this handsome volume brings together reproductions of the artist’s work and other material with new texts by Davies, Dodie Bellamy, and Jamie Parra to return FitzGerald to art history and consider his relevance to the present.

For further information, visit our website. https://artmetropole.com/events/book-launch-that-directionless-light-of-the-future-rediscovering

title: 2026 Mulan International Film Festival
location: Innis Town Hall, 2 Sussex Ave, Toronto, ON M5S 1J5, Canada
description:
From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen.


Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song.


Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame.


Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale.


Screening times vary by day.

location: Alderwood
description:
In November we will be discussing the non-fiction book
Clara at the Door With a Revolver
by Carolyn Whitzman.
“In the autumnal darkness of October 6, 1894, an unseen figure rang the doorbell at the Parkdale home of a well-to-do Toronto family and then shot eighteen-year-old Frank Westwood in his doorway, murdering him in cold blood.
Six weeks later, Clara Ford, a Black tailor and single mother, was arrested. Known for her impeccable work ethic and her resolute personality - and for her predilection for wearing men’s attire – she confessed to the murder.
But as the details of her arrest and her complex connection to the Westwood family emerged, Clara recanted, testifying that she had been coerced by police into a false confession.”

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre, 50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.
Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle.

n a Learning Circle:

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Journée pédagogique: Explorum - Bombes à bain
location: S. Walter Stewart, Auditorium
description:
L’expérience des bombes à bain est une expérience simple qui illustre une des réactions chimiques les plus communes : la neutralisation acidobasique qui forme un sel et de l'eau. Cette activité relaxante permet aux enfants de faire leur propre bombe à bain et de comprendre que cette réaction produit du gaz (des bulles) ; ils apprennent que l’acide contient du cations H+ et que la base contient des anions OH- qui réagissent ensemble pour former du sel et de l'eau. Chaque participant combine ses ingrédients et confectionne sa propre bombe à bain qu’il emporte avec lui emballée dans un petit sac en cellophane.
The bath bomb experience is a simple activity that illustrates one of the most common chemical reactions: acid-base neutralization, which forms a salt and water. This relaxing activity allows children to create their own bath bomb and understand that this reaction produces gas (bubbles). They learn that the acid contains H+ ions and the base contains OH- ions, which react together to form salt and water. Each participant combines their ingredients and crafts their own bath bomb to take home, packaged in a small cellophane bag.
Accessibilité:
Le sous-titrage en direct ou automatique, l’interprétation en langue des signes, les services d’intervenant, ou les services d’accompagnement sont disponibles sur demande. Veuillez soumettre votre demande au moins deux semaines à l’avance à : tpl.ca/accessibility-events

In this third instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series Internet Horror Classics on Film, crime writer Kathleen Hale and film critic Willow Maclay discuss Jane Schoenbrun's coming-of-age psychological horror film, We're All Going to the World's Fair alongside host Adam Nayman.
About this event's guests:
Kathleen Hale
is a crime writer based in Los Angeles. Her reporting has been featured in Vanity Fair, among other outlets. Slenderman is her first true crime book.
Willow Maclay
is a freelance film critic stationed in St. John's, Newfoundland. She has written for outlets such as The Village Voice, Ebert Voices, Cinemascope Magazine, and more. She is also the co-author of Corpses, Fools and Monsters: An Examination of Transgender Cinema.
Adam Nayman
is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. He is a regular contributor to The Ringer, a lecturer at the University of Toronto's Cinema Studies Institute, and he has written on film for The New Yorker and The New York Times.
Read more:
Corpses, Fools and Monsters

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Robotics Institute Seminar: Steven Waslander, “TankerVision: Turning Firefighting Flights into a Wildfire Behaviour Dataset”
location: Bahen Centre for Information Technology, Room 1190, or on Zoom, 40 St George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5S 2E4, Canada
description:
Join in-person (BA1190) or online (Zoom) 
TankerVision: Turning Firefighting Flights into a Wildfire Behaviour Dataset
Abstract
Models of wildfire rate of spread, intensity and spotting still rely mostly on small experimental burns from decades ago. Fires are hardest to observe exactly when it matters most, during rapid, intense spread. Satellites are too coarse in space and time, and drones and research aircraft are kept out of fire airspace. The only platforms reliably overhead during a major run are the aircraft fighting the fire. 
TankerVision turns these operational flights into a continuous, automated source of fire behaviour data. Working with Conair Aerial Firefighting, the BC Wildfire Service and Alberta Wildfire, we developed a self-contained imaging unit for the bird-dog aircraft that direct airtanker operations. It records georeferenced colour and thermal infrared imagery whenever the aircraft is near a fire, with no action required from the crew. A prototype flew roughly 50 missions over 30 fires from Kamloops in 2025. 
With support from DRDC and NRCan, three upgraded aircraft flew fires across five provinces and territories in 2026. An automated pipeline segments fire and smoke, reconstructs georeferenced 3D fire fronts and derives rate-of-spread observations from successive passes. The result is the first large multi-pass, multi-fire dataset of active wildfire behaviour, a foundation for data-driven fire prediction models, with an initial public release planned for December 2026. 
About Steven Waslander
Prof. Steven Waslander is a leading authority on autonomous vehicles, including multirotor drones and autonomous driving vehicles.  He received his B.Sc.E.in 1998 from Queen’s University, his M.S. in 2002 and his Ph.D. in 2007, both from Stanford University in Aeronautics and Astronautics, where as a graduate student he created the Stanford Testbed of Autonomous Rotorcraft for Multi-Agent Control (STARMAC), the world’s most capable outdoor multi-vehicle quadrotor platform at the time. He was recruited to Waterloo from Stanford in 2008, where he founded and directed the Waterloo Autonomous Vehicle Laboratory (WAVELab), extending the state of the art in autonomous drones and autonomous driving through advances in localization and mapping, object detection and tracking, integrated planning and control methods and multi-robot coordination. His work on autonomous vehicles has resulted in the Autonomoose, the first autonomous vehicle created at a Canadian University to drive on public roads. In 2018, he joined the University of Toronto Institute for Aerospace Studies (UTIAS), and founded the Toronto Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (TRAILab). Starting in July of 2026, he became the director of the University of Toronto Robotics Institute. 
Join in-person (BA1190) or online (Zoom)

Experience Toronto
On **Friday November 25th,** **join us for La Boheme at The Terminal Theatre in Queen's Quay Terminal.** This will be our first time seeing The Toronto City Opera perform. When the seamstress Mimì meets the poet Rodolfo, their romance blossoms amid friendship, laughter, and the harsh realities of poverty. Inspiring the hit broadway musical *Rent*, *La bohème* features unforgettable melodies and captures the beauty and fragility of love.

title: The Myth of “Samshu”: Smell, Race, and the Making of Chinatown in North America, 1880s–1920s
location: North York Central Library, Room 101
description:
What did Chinatown smell like to outsiders a century ago? How could an unfamiliar distilled drink
become a symbol of racial and cultural difference? Between the 1880s and the 1920s, Chinese
immigrant communities in North America encountered growing scrutiny of their businesses,
customs, and everyday lives. Among the objects attracting attention was “samshu,” a term found in
English-language descriptions of Chinese distilled spirits. Its reputation became entangled with
accounts of Chinatown, unfamiliar odours, drinking practices, illicit alcohol, and anxieties about
immigration.
This lecture investigates how descriptions of samshu circulated within the cultural imagination of
North American society. Moving among sensory impressions, racialized representations, and the
history of bootlegging and alcohol regulation, it asks how ordinary experiences of smell and taste
could become markers of inclusion and exclusion. The lecture also asks audiences to distinguish
claims made about Chinese communities from the more complicated realities of their lives. In doing
so, it explores how historical encounters produce durable ideas about “us” and “them.”
Presenter: Dr. Jackson Yue Bin Guo | Sessional Lecturer II, Global Asia Studies / History,
University of Toronto Scarborough | Founder, Aprilum Lyceum
Jackson Yue Bin Guo received his Ph.D. in History from the University of Toronto in 2023. He
researches food and drink, law, sensory experience, material culture, and everyday life in late
imperial and modern China. His current book manuscript, Governing Intoxication: Alcohol and the
Convergence of Sensory Life in Late Imperial and Modern China, explores the social, cultural, and
regulatory histories of distilled alcohol. His scholarship has appeared in Global Food History and
the Asian Journal of Law and Society. He is the founder of Aprilum Lyceum.

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

location: Naturlandia, 2237 Dundas Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1X6, Canada
description:
Since 2021, the Fusion Festival has brought together writers, directors and actors to workshop and develop new works by Canadian playwrights & screenwriters. Building on this tradition, we’re proud to introduce The Fusion Lab, a new initiative dedicated to supporting Canadian artists through year-round workshops designed to facilitate the creation of new Canadian works. The program will provide opportunities for artists to develop their work, with selected scripts showcase at our annual Fusion Festival!

This season, we’re excited to present staged readings of two original Canadian plays written by Brandon Nicoletti.

SPOTTER

Featuring: Patrick S. McEwen & Blake Pyne

When Kai nearly injures himself during a bench press, Tyler steps in and offers to be his spotter. The two men form an unlikely connection that sparks conversations about body image, modern dating, and the way gay men see each other.

KILL TEST

Featuring: Marisa Roggeveen, Andy Kalirai, & Scott Clark

A rookie operative must extract information from a captive while her mentor tests her resolve.

Join us at Naturlandia on November 27 th at 8:30pm for an evening of new Canadian theatre.

Come experience original storytelling, support emerging Canadian artists, and help us continue our tradition of bringing bold new orks to the stage and screen!

title: [Hike - Intermediate] Seaton Trail & 3rd Concession
description:
GTA Hiking & Stuff
Valley Farm Dog Park @ Seaton Trail & 3rd Concession -

PLEASE NOTE: This hike starts a the Southern end of the Seaton Trail and heads north for about an hour before we turn around. Please note the parking location
\*\*\*
Seaton Trail is another beautiful hiking area up near the Pickering area.

This time, we are going to start at the south end of Seaton Trail and head north. This is an intermediate hike.

We will strive for between 7-10 kms. There are some sections with hills that will get your heart rate up.

Bring a water bottle and dress for the weather.

The hike leaves at 9:35am sharp.

We will be meeting at the Seaton Trail Parking Lot off Concession 3 (Rossland Road) ([https://goo.gl/maps/575kQzkHLJP1tx198](https://goo.gl/maps/575kQzkHLJP1tx198)). There is a small parking lot. It is a very busy parking lot, so please arrive early or share ride where possible.

We will hike at a medium pace (4 - 5 km/h) for the approx 8 kms.

Bring 1L of water and good hiking shoes or boots.

**Parking Address:**
Valley Farm Rd. & 3rd Concession · Pickering, ON

NOTE: Due to construction you can’t take Brock to 3rd concession, you MUST take valley farm road which you can reach from Brock via Dellbrook Ave, or alternatively via Kingston or Finch Ave.

There are signs warning of construction, the trail and parking are open so just follow the construction signs. At the end of valley farm turn LEFT - The parking lot is not far and on your left.

***Hike starts at 9:35-am SHARP.***

Please note that as we get into winter hiking with snow and slippery trails, we consider proper Crampons to be mandatory.

title: Holiday Succulent Workshop

description:
Join us this holiday season and create a one-of-a-kind succulent!
Celebrate the festive season with a delightful holiday-inspired succulent arranging workshop! In this creative and relaxing session, you’ll design a beautiful succulent arrangement in a charming snowflake tin planter—perfect for adding a touch of natural elegance to your holiday décor or gifting to someone special.
 
Guided by a succulent expert, you’ll learn tips and tricks for arranging succulents with a seasonal flair, including techniques for layering textures, balancing colours, and incorporating winter-inspired accents.
 
All materials are provided, including a snowflake tin planter, premium succulents, specialty soil, and care instruction cards to ensure your arrangement stays vibrant through the holiday season and beyond.
 
Join us for this festive workshop and leave with a stunning centrepiece that captures the warmth and beauty of the holidays!
 
Saturday, November 28, 10 to 11 a.m.
Public $55, TBG Members $50 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Canadian Succulents
Molly is the owner and operator of the small business Canadian Succulents. Canadian Succulents creates floral arrangements using entirely succulents and cacti plants. They not only arrange and design all of the creations, but also grow all the plants that can be found in them as well. They operate out of a greenhouse just northeast of the city, where they grow over 300 varieties of succulents and cacti. They grow and create these designs for wedding centrepieces and favours, corporate events and gifting, and hotel and office greenery.

Each attendee will receive one 6″ white pillar candle, a full selection of pressed flowers to choose from, and step-by-step guidance on using heated palette knives safely to melt your design into the wax.

Epiphanie Belanger is the founder of HobbyHub, a community-driven platform designed to help people try new hobbies in a relaxed environment. What started as a personal curiosity for creative pursuits quickly turned into a mission to make hobbies more accessible, social, and fun for beginners.

title: 2026 Mulan International Film Festival

description:
From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen.


Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song.


Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame.


Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale.


Screening times vary by day.

**Scheduling details:**
\- If you have a specific game that you would like to post for\, feel free to do so in comments\. In your post\, include the name of the game\, number of players needed for the game\, whether you are offering a teach or not\, and the start time \(please try to start before noon if possible\)\.

title: 🍁🌿 Fall Hike: East Don Trail Adventure 🍪🥾
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 15 Years!
# **Toronto’s Newest Ravine Trail, Autumn Scenery & Fresh-Baked Cookies!**

Did you join us for our last East Don Trail adventure? People had such a great time, and there was plenty to talk about afterward! Now that fall is here, we’re heading back to enjoy the trail in autumn.
Join us as we explore the **East Don Trail**, one of Toronto’s newest additions to its incredible ravine system.

This beautiful route follows the East Don River through peaceful forests, wetlands, and scenic valley landscapes, connecting communities that were once separated.
If you’ve walked the Lower Don Trail, this is a different experience.

Expect quieter pathways, river views, new bridges, and the feeling of discovering another corner of Toronto that many people have yet to explore.

Most of the route is paved and relatively easy to walk. Just one warning: what goes down must come up! 😄

The final section includes a fairly steep hill, so you should be comfortable tackling a good climb near the end.
And the best part? We’ll finish with a couple of optional stops for coffee, baked goods, and cookies!

## 🚶‍♂️ What We’ll Do

We’ll meet outside Broadview Subway Station before making our way into the Don Valley to explore the East Don Trail.

Along the way, we’ll:
🌿 Walk beside the East Don River
🌉 Cross bridges and follow scenic pathways
🍂 Enjoy the ravine scenery and fall colours
📸 Stop for photos and conversation
☕ Visit Circles & Squares Bakery Café near the end of the trail
🍪 Continue to the Peak Freans Cookie Outlet for discounted cookies and treats

**Both stops afterward are optional.** At Circles & Squares Bakery Café, you can grab a quick coffee or something baked, or stay a little longer if you’d like. You’re welcome to join us for the cookie outlet afterward, or make your own plans.

We’ll finish at **Coxwell Subway Station via TTC bus**. This is a one-way walk, so we will not be returning to Broadview Station.

## 🍁 Weather & Expectations

This walk happens rain or shine unless severe weather makes it unsafe.
The trail is mostly paved and relatively easy, but there is one fairly steep hill near the end. Please come prepared for that final climb and wear comfortable walking shoes.

This is a social walk, not a guided historical tour. We’re here to enjoy the scenery, have conversations, and explore one of Toronto’s newest green spaces together.

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meeting location:** Outside Broadview Subway Station
🦌 **Look for:** My Moose Hat!
⏰ **Meeting time:** 11:00 AM
🚶 **Departure:** 11:05 AM sharp. I’ll wait a maximum of five minutes.
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
Please arrive on time, as we’ll leave promptly.

🏁 **End point:** Coxwell Subway Station, via TTC bus.

## ☕🍪 After the Walk

### First stop: Circles & Squares Bakery Café

We’ll stop at **Circles & Squares Bakery Café** near the end of the trail. If you’d like, grab a coffee, a pastry, or something else from the bakery. This is a casual stop, so there’s no obligation to buy anything or stay for long.

### Next stop: Peak Freans Cookie Outlet

Then we’ll head to the **Peak Freans Cookie Outlet**, where you can browse their selection of cookies, crackers, and other treats at outlet prices.
You’re welcome to join us for both stops, just one, or head home after the hike. The choice is yours!

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or by e-transfer to [mathewmaclean@hotmail.com](mailto:mathewmaclean@hotmail.com).**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing events like this. Thank you for supporting our community! 💛

## 🎒 What to Bring

* 💧 Water
* 👟 Comfortable walking shoes
* 🧥 Weather-appropriate clothing
* 📱 A phone or camera for photos
* 💵 Spending money if you’d like coffee, baked goods, or cookies

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This group is open to anyone who wants to be social and make friends, whether single or partnered.
We also organize movies, walks and hikes, arts and culture outings, restaurant gatherings, and plenty more. There’s always something happening!

## ⚠️ A Few Reminders

* You’re welcome to RSVP ahead of time or show up on the day if you’re unsure about your schedule.
* Please keep an eye on the event page for updates in case plans change or the event needs to be cancelled.
* Remember that this is a one-way walk ending at Coxwell Subway Station, not Broadview.

👤 **Organized by Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **[torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com](mailto:torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com)**.

**Stay for the coffee and cookies.**
**Leave having discovered another hidden corner of the city.** 🍁🌿🍪

title: Author Talk: Steven Biggs
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Grow Figs Where You Think You Can’t: Stories, Ingenuity, and Homegrown Figs
What makes someone build a “figatorium,” collect hundreds of varieties, or tuck fig trees into bed for a Canadian winter? 
 
Join Toronto horticulturist and author Steven Biggs for a mix of storytelling and practical fig-growing advice celebrating the revised and expanded edition of Grow Figs Where You Think You Can’t. 
 
Meet some of the fascinating growers featured in the book—from a generous mentor in an Ontario backyard to a California fig hunter—and discover the family traditions, curiosity, and ingenuity behind their gardens. Along the way, Steven shares ideas for growing figs here in the Toronto area, getting ripe fruit, and finding room for a little Mediterranean flavour at home. 
 
Whether you already grow figs or are simply curious, come for the stories, bring your questions, and stay for the book signing. 
 
Saturday, November 28, 11:30 a.m. to 1 p.m.
Free to attend. Please register beforehand so we know you’re coming!
 
About Steven Biggs
Recognized by Garden Making magazine as one of the “Green Gang” of Canadians making a difference in horticulture, Steven Biggs is a Toronto-based horticulturist, author, and host of the award-winning Food Garden Life Show. A former horticulture instructor with George Brown College and Durham College, he has spent decades helping gardeners grow edible plants in unlikely places. In his own Toronto garden, his experiments have included driveway straw-bale gardens, a rooftop kitchen garden, wicking beds, fruit plantings, an edible-themed front yard, and a fig collection that got slightly out of hand.  
 
Steven’s fascination with figs took off in 1993, when he spent a summer working at a nursery with the UK National Collection of figs. Since 2009, he has been teaching, writing, speaking, and interviewing growers about figs in cold climates. His first fig book, Grow Figs Where You Think You Can’t, won a Silver Award of Achievement from the Garden Writers Association. Steven’s fig writing has appeared in Fine Gardening, Garden Making, The Gardener, and Edible Toronto.  
 
Steven continues the fig conversation through his Fig Culture podcast and newsletter, where he shares stories, interviews, and practical ideas for growing figs in cold climates and containers. Find his fig tips and other food-gardening ideas at foodgardenlife.com.

title: Christmas in Old York! 1833 (RETURN FOR 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

**If you plan on attending, please get your tickets for this event early as this tour has run for the last 3 years, and does sell out rather quickly.**

So what was it like in York in 1833 at Christmas time?

The prices of various food items and gifts on display, the gas lights creating a glow as the snow begins, places to gather, places to get a drink, like the Steamboat Hotel on Front Street, or maybe one might decide to take their best girl or guy on a stagecoach trip to High Park to watch kids speed down the hills on their skids.

What were the traditions in old York? Maybe the residents went down to the lake and watched the nighttime fishermen spear fish for Christmas dinner. Let's take a trip around old York and see what it was like back in 1833, three months before we changed our name to Toronto in 1834.

Or take a holiday trip to Kingston or Montreal to buy gifts directly from New York or London stores, fancy hats for the ladies and cigars for the men. Books and wooden toys for the kids. What about that goose in the little grocery store on King Street West of Jarvis? Candies from Britain, real home made gingerbread in the store windows.

On Christmas Eve everyone walked to St. James Cathedral for the ringing of the bells, singing, and skating over the frozen Toronto Bay to the Peninsula.

This tour explores old York. This walking tour is for all walking levels. The tour begins and ends at St. James Cathedral on King Street East at Church Street. A great way to kick off the season.

This tour has a ticketed price of $15.00.

location: Palmerston, Theatre
description:
Meet
Andrea Gunraj
, acclaimed essayist and author of
Go-between Girl: My Indentured Roots as Reclaimed Present
, The Lost Sister and The Sudden Disappearance of Seetha. Based out of Toronto, Gunraj writes about underseen stories and connections. She will discuss her latest work, Go-Between Girl, through storytelling and personal reflection, exploring themes of family, migration, belonging, and the complex intersections of Caribbean, Indian, and Canadian identities.
Gunraj will be in conversation with
Victoria Kuketz
, a public policy leader, journalist (IG @victoriakuketz), global social inclusion leader, and 2026 Obama Foundation Scholar. The discussion will be followed by an audience Q&A and book signing.
Presented by the
Caribbean Canadian Indian Cultural Collective (CCICC)
and
Indo Caribbean Educators Network (ICEN)
, this event offers a unique opportunity to engage with one of the most compelling voices in contemporary Indo-Caribbean literature. Attendees will gain insight into Gunraj's personal journey as a professional civic leader and Indo-Caribbean woman, and how historical and cultural experiences have shaped Indo-Caribbean people. Discover the power of storytelling as memory, community building, and cross-cultural understanding.
Whether you are familiar with Andrea's work or discovering it for the first time, this event promises an inspiring and thought-provoking evening celebrating literature, heritage, and the diverse narratives that enrich Canada's multicultural landscape.
Free program. Please register. Doors open at 12:45 pm. At 1:00 pm, seating becomes first-come, first-served until capacity is reached.
Organization Info:
The
Canadian Caribbean Indian Cultural Collective (CCICC)
is a community organization representing Indians (currently referred to as South Asians) of various ethnicities, regions, and faiths, who are the descendants of the indentured labourers taken by the British to their colonies in the Caribbean and around the world. Their mission is to share their stories of struggle, resilience and contributions across the Caribbean and here in Canada.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

title: Painting Botanical Cast Ornaments from Garden Blooms
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Learn how to create your own plant-based pigments and paint one-of-a-kind botanical cast ornaments!
Want to give a holiday gift that is not mass produced in a factory? Looking for a calming experience that beats the hustle and bustle? Join botanical artist Rebecca Fortin for an afternoon of natural paint-making and ornament painting.
 
Under Rebecca’s guidance, you’ll explore how to create colour pigments from local botanicals, such as goldenrod, nettle, berries, and more.
 
Test your plant-based pigments on watercolour paper, including creating a holiday card. Participants will choose two plaster miniature botanical casts to paint and take home or gift for the holiday season. These ornaments are created by Rebecca, each made using impressions of live botanicals. This workshop features botanical casts made with flowers directly from Toronto Botanical Garden, capturing the garden’s beauty in artwork that lasts long after the blossoms fade.
 
All materials will be provided. No prior experience required.
 
This workshop is intended for ages 16+. Mature youth aged 12+ are welcome, but must be accompanied and supervised by an adult.
 
Please note: Please wear practical clothes and footwear that you don’t mind getting a little messy. As with all handmade processes using real plants: results will vary, pigments may shift in colour over time, and each piece will have perfect imperfections that contribute to its unique character.
 
Saturday, November 28, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $115, TBG Members $110 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Rebecca Fortin
Rebecca Fortin is a visual artist based in rural Whitby, Ontario, where she creates botanical artwork rooted in the textures, colours, and quiet beauty of the plants around her. After a 20-year career in public health administration, Rebecca pivoted to focus on her art practice, completing the Drawing and Painting program at the Haliburton School of Art + Design in 2022. She now works full-time as an artist, bringing together her background in community health promotion with her passion for connecting people to nature through art.
 
Rebecca’s work has been shown across Ontario and is held in private and corporate collections in Canada and internationally. Her hands-on workshops invite participants to explore botanicals and natural art materials — offering memorable, calming experiences and the opportunity to create beautiful, one-of-a-kind pieces to take home.

title: Double Contra Dance with Jacob deGroot-Magetti, Áine Schryer-O'Gorman & Adam Iredale-Gray
location: St. Barnabas Church Hall, 175 Hampton Ave, Toronto, M4K 2Z3
description:
November 28th – Double Contra Dance on the Danforth! 
Wondering whether you should join us for the advanced dance? At this dance, it is assumed that you are comfortable with all the common moves and can dance them on the fly (even if called without the caller walking the dance through beforehand). A hey should feel fun (not scary or disorienting) and it should be rare that anyone would need to help you get reoriented during a dance. If that sounds like you, please come! 
If you’re thinking of bringing a beginner that day, we’d love to see them at the evening dance. Make sure they attend the intro to contra lesson at 7pm so that they have the most fun possible during the dance (and get free entry to the next regular evening dance). 
✨ On stage:
Caller Jacob deGroot-Magetti guiding the dances, with Áine Schryer-O’Gorman & Adam Iredale-Gray – setting the groove and keeping the floor in motion all day long. 
🕖 Evening timeline:
Afternoon – Advanced dance (2pm to 5pm) 
Evening – Regular dance (Intro lesson 7pm, dance 7:30 to 10:30pm) 
😷 Mask-Optional
💧 Bring a refillable water bottle
🥟 Samosas will be ready (arrive early if you want one!) 
Afternoon & Evening dances are priced separately.
Sliding scale: $10–$35 (kids 16 & under free)
It costs about $22 per dancer to make these nights happen—your support, generosity, and word-of-mouth keep the community strong. 
📍 St. Barnabas Church Hall
175 Hampton Ave (near Chester Station)

title: Lost Libraries of the Ancient World (LECTURES - 5TH ANNIVERSARY 2ND DATE)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

**A second date has been added as there are 9 on the waitlist for the Saturday October 24 lecture! If you are planning to take in this lecture, get your spots early. See you then!**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2026/2027. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join me, and uncover the world and keep active, warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life. The first Lecture on the Go was **Walking North America** and that was in October of 2021. Hard to believe it's been 5 years of lectures. So I wanted to do something special to celebrate 5 years of exploration.

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

Let's get started.

What if some of humanity's greatest discoveries were made thousands of years ago, and then lost forever?

What if entire histories, scientific breakthroughs, literary masterpieces, and eyewitness accounts of the ancient world once existed, only to disappear into the flames of war, and the collapse of civilizations?

Join me for a fascinating journey into the world's lost libraries, from the legendary Library of Alexandria to the vanished collections of ancient empires whose treasures may be lost forever.

At the heart, stands the Library of Alexandria, the most famous library in history. Founded over two thousand years ago, it sought to gather all the knowledge of the known world. Scholars from across the Mediterranean came to study astronomy, mathematics, geography, medicine, philosophy, and literature. Yet one of history's greatest mysteries remains: what happened to this remarkable institution, and what priceless knowledge disappeared with it?

Was it destroyed in a single catastrophe, or did it slowly fade away over centuries from neglect?

Beyond Alexandria, we will explore a forgotten world of lost libraries and vanished collections stretching from Mesopotamia and ancient Egypt to medieval Europe, Baghdad, and China. Discover the remarkable stories of librarians, scholars, explorers, and rulers who dedicated their lives to preserving knowledge.

We will encounter lost books, missing histories, ancient scientific works, and literary treasures that survive today only as fragments.
This lecture is an exploration of one of history's most compelling questions: What have we forgotten?

And how libraries shaped civilization and why their loss continues to fascinate us centuries later. Whether you are a lover of history, literature, archaeology, or simply enjoy a good mystery, this special Lecture on the Go will leave you wondering. What secrets of the past may still lie hidden, just waiting to be rediscovered? Fascinating indeed!

Upcoming topics in the 2026 series:

\*Philosophy 1: Great Minds of the Western World: Goethe to Kant! - (2027)
\*Philosophy 2: Great Minds of the Eastern
World: Chuang Tzu to Dalai Lama - (2027)
Legacy of Triangle: How a New York Factory Scandal changed North America - (September 2027)

So book your plans now!

This event is for all levels and walkers, there are a few steps here and there to navigate, but mostly on one level. This event in a non-walking event.

The lecture begins on the steps of Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Bay Street and Queen Street West, and
has a ticket price of $20.00 per person, but **free with the yearly membership pass**.

**Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
