title: Meet New People | 50+ Board Games & After Dark Specials | Ages 25–45
description:
Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
As the year draws to a close, why not make room for some new faces and friendships? ❤️
Join Fast Friends at Stout Irish Pub for a professionally hosted social evening where guided conversations, rotations and themed connection rounds make meeting new people easier and more enjoyable — even if you're coming on your own.
And there's more to the evening! Stay for 50+ board games, drinks, food and Stout's After Dark Specials. 🎲🍻

🎟️ Book Early & Save: [https://toronto28thnov.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto28thnov.eventbrite.co.uk)
You can pay securely online with any debit or credit card through PayPal — no PayPal account required.
Advance tickets are cheaper and help us plan the right space and group size for a comfortable evening.
Early Bird: CAD $10 \| Regular: CAD $15 \| At the Door: CAD $20 cash

🤝 The Evening
7:00 PM — Welcome & Settle In
Meet your host, Kruttika, grab a drink and get comfortable.
Whether you've recently moved to Toronto or have lived here for years, it's a chance to step out, meet some new faces and enjoy a different kind of Saturday evening.
Coming alone? You're very welcome — many guests attend solo, and our host will help you settle in and get connected.
7:30–8:30 PM — Hosted Fast Friends
Meeting people doesn't have to mean approaching a room full of strangers and hoping a conversation takes off.
Our host guides you through short conversations and rotations, so you can meet a variety of people throughout the evening. You don't have to worry about who to approach or what to say next — the structure makes it easier to get involved and discover who you connect with.

✨ Themed Connection Rounds
We'll add interactive prompts and themed conversation challenges to help you discover shared interests, swap stories and find unexpected common ground.
From travel and food to music, hobbies and weekend adventures, these rounds help move conversations beyond the usual small talk.
🎲 8:30 PM onwards — 50+ Board Games & Socialising

Why end the evening just as you're getting to know people?
Stout has more than 50 board games available, giving you an easy way to keep socialising after the hosted rounds. Join a game, meet others around the table, share a few laughs, grab another drink or simply continue a conversation.
You don't need to be a board-game expert. It's all about having fun together and giving new connections more time to grow.

🍻 Stay for Stout's After Dark Specials
If you're planning to stay later, Stout's After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.
It's a great way to extend your evening, relax with the people you've met and enjoy more of Stout's lively pub atmosphere.

❤️ Why Come Along?
✔️ Meet 20+ new people in one evening
✔️ Professionally hosted conversations and rotations
✔️ Interactive themed rounds to spark better conversations
✔️ 50+ board games at Stout 🎲
✔️ Stout's After Dark Specials from 9–11 PM 🍻
✔️ Reserved space for our group
✔️ Relaxed Irish pub atmosphere
✔️ An opportunity to meet members from across our Toronto Meetup communities
✔️ Solo attendees welcome
✔️ Designed for ladies and gents aged 25–45
✔️ Friendship-focused — not a dating event

📍 Why Stout Irish Pub?
Located at 221 Carlton Street, Stout offers a relaxed, welcoming pub atmosphere with food, drinks and an impressive selection of more than 50 board games.
It's a great setting for an evening that starts with hosted conversations and continues with board games, laughter and more time to get to know the people you've met.

👥 Who Is It For?
You don't need to be new to Toronto, belong to an existing group or know anyone attending.
Whether you're looking to build a social circle, meet people beyond work, make friends after moving to the city or simply enjoy a different kind of Saturday night, you're welcome.
Come by yourself or bring a friend. We'll help make the introductions easier.

🌍 About Fast Friends
For over 10 years, Fast Friends has been bringing people together through professionally hosted social events in 30+ cities worldwide.
Our goal is simple: make meeting new people easier, more relaxed and more enjoyable.
Come for the conversations. Stay for the board games. Leave with new connections. ❤️
Come solo. We'll guide the experience. You make the connections. 🤝

title: ABCD Watches "The Gymnasts of Fisherman Colony" directed by Habiba Nosheen
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
You're invited to a screening at Hot Docs of ABCD Book Club member Habiba Nosheen's documentary ***[The Gymnasts of Fisherman Colony](https://www.thegymnastsoffishermancolony.com/)***. Register for the event and I'll send you a ***code for 20% off tickets***. We'll meet up beforehand, and anyone interested can join us for drinks afterwards.

*"The Gymnasts of Fisherman Colony is an intimate coming-of-age documentary by three-time Emmy Award–winning filmmaker Habiba Nosheen that follows three teenage girls in Pakistan, offering a rare and tender portrait of girlhood, joy, and play told through the eyes of young Pakistani girls navigating the margins of society.*
*At its core, The Gymnasts of Fisherman Colony is a story of hope and quiet defiance. Through the intimate journeys of three teenagers we witness as their passion for gymnastics begins to clash with deeply rooted expectations around what girls can and cannot do. The film follows their journey as they find themselves straddling two polar opposite worlds as they push to make space for themselves through gymnastics. The result is a lyrical and deeply human portrait of three young girls from a corner of the world we rarely see on screen. These are girls who dare to dream."* (from the [Hot Docs](https://boxoffice.hotdocs.ca/websales/pages/info.aspx?evtinfo=658891~cf285ddd-dacb-4f18-89b8-1252c6dcffa6&epguid=a2104450-7e47-4369-a17d-c247570c3939&mdy=11/28/2026&) website)

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre, 50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Hike with the Dancing King (aka Robin)- Hockley Valley
description:
These Boots Are Made for Hiking
**MeetUp Location: Hockley Valley PP/Bruce Trail Parking just off Hwy 7**

For those of you who join our parties, you know Robin is the the Dancing King! He also leads a wicked hike. Join Robin on the 14.2 km trail through the Hockley Valley.
This loop-to-loop trail brings you over rivers, wee waterfalls and bridges, winds and dines you through diverse forests filled with incredible varieties of fungus - you might even wonder if you just landed in British Columbia. And just when you get yourself used to piney forest goodness, you'll pop out into hilly meadows filled with wildflowers. Those 12 km deliver so many different landscapes, smells, sounds, an abandoned jalopy and pure joy. This hike is going to get your heart pumping and your body sweaty, but the trail is a mere minutes drive from Adamo Estate winery. So after traversing for 12km, a glass of dry crisp rose is the icing on the cake while sitting in Muskoka chairs overlooking the vineyards.
source: Meetup: These Boots Are Made for Hiking

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesday)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.

title: Christmas on the Historic Toronto Islands!
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

It's hard to imagine a better place than the Toronto Islands, as the big day approaches. Christmas on the islands was full of tradition, of skating on the frozen Toronto Bay, and sleigh rides between Ward's and Centre. And if it snows well so much the better. Let's take a look back at the Christmas season on the Islands.

It's about growing up in Toronto. About the ten minute ride over on the ferry boat, and the memories that have made Toronto a summertime and wintertime city. It's a stretch of land that is historic and fascinating, both geologically and socially as well. And a history that brings together the stories of Toronto from its founding.

The Gibraltar Point Lighthouse was constructed in 1809, and is one of the oldest structures in Toronto.

The peninsula was partially severed by a storm in 1852, which created a sandbar that was dangerously thin, and the peninsula became an island permanently by a violent storm that cut out the eastern channel, two hotels on the island were also destroyed. The modern history of the Islands' begins here!

The Islands' have three main parts, and all three have their historic elements, the most being the western most island named for the Hanlan family. A spectacular hotel, "The Ned Hanlan" was built and a regatta course dredged out of the western lagoon. An amusement park followed, and an airport after that!

It was also a residential enclave with most of the homes appearing on Ward's and Centre Islands. And the Christmas traditions began. A winter wonderland of lights and laughing children and some adults as well. Shall we explore the islands?

The tour begins and ends at the Jack Layton Ferry Terminal at the foot of Bay Street. We will meet **inside** the gates! And we will head over as a group, so tickets must be bought before! Please meet 10 minutes before the meetup time!

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person!

**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery, 1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: 2026 Mulan International Film Festival
location: Innis Town Hall, 2 Sussex Ave, Toronto, ON M5S 1J5, Canada
description:
From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen.


Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song.


Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame.


Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale.


Screening times vary by day.

OCAD University Senate Meeting

The next regular meeting of the OCAD University Senate is scheduled to take place on Monday, November 30, 2026 from 3:15 pm – 5:30 pm EDT. The Senate is responsible for the establishment and regulation of academic policy, standards and procedures at OCAD University. The Senate and its many committees are in charge of all matters pertaining to OCAD U academic resources, academic programming, academic strategic planning, student affairs and any other such matters relating to academic issues. More information can be found on the OCAD U Senate webpage . If you would like to attend as a guest, or if you have any questions, please contact David Wagschal, Quality Assurance Officer & Associate Senate Secretary at dwagschal@ocadu.ca . Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).

Screening times vary by day.

title: Curator's Talk: Time, Labour, and the Value of Beads
location: Ontario
description:
Date: Monday, November 30, 2026
Time: 7:00 pm – 8:00 pm (Doors @ 6:30 pm)
Location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St. W.
Tickets: $25 
Beads may be small and intricate, but their histories reveal powerful stories of identity, value, and status. In celebration of Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear Around the World, join Director & Senior Curator Elizabeth Semmelhack for an informative and illuminating exploration of beadwork traditions from around the world, and their role as markers of wealth, prestige, and cultural meaning. 
From royal adornment and ceremonial regalia to trade and personal expression, this lecture traces how beads have signaled belonging across time and place. At its core is the labour behind the work: the skilled craftsmanship, generational knowledge, and cultural practices embedded in every stitch. By centering time and labour, the talk challenges conventional ideas of value—asking what makes something “luxurious,” and who defines it. 
Through cross-cultural perspectives and historical insight, this talk reframes beadwork as more than decoration, as a powerful language of status, resilience, and artistry. 
BUY YOUR TICKETS  
Agenda
6:30 pm – Doors Open
7:00 pm – Lecture Begins
8:00 pm – Lecture Ends/Galleries Open
9:00 pm – Museum Closes 

ABOUT ELIZABETH SEMMELHACK: 
 
As Director and Senior Curator at the Bata Shoe Museum, Elizabeth applies her extensive cultural and art history background to guide the mission forward while exploring the multiple roles and meanings of footwear through innovative exhibitions. With over 30 exhibitions curated, Semmelhack has helped transform the Bata Shoe Museum into an internationally recognized center for footwear scholarship, revealing how shoes illuminate our understanding of diverse social, political, and cultural histories across time and geography. 
Named by FASHION Magazine as one of the world’s “top five game-changing fashion curators”, Semmelhack’s perspective and expertise have been featured in major publications, broadcasts, and television shows across the globe. She has authored nearly 30 articles and chapters as well as numerous books and catalogs, including Out of the Box: The Rise of Sneaker Culture (2015), which has sold over 30,000 copies worldwide. 

Please review our Terms and Conditions in advance and check in with Visitor Services upon arrival. Questions? Email us info@batashoemuseum.ca anytime.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesdays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

Research creates knowledge, but impact happens when knowledge is shared, understood, and used. This interactive session introduces graduate students to the fundamentals of Knowledge Mobilization (KMb) and explores how to move research beyond traditional academic audiences. Topics will include how to identify key audiences, develop effective knowledge-sharing strategies, build meaningful partnerships, and communicate research in ways that support social, community, policy, and professional impact. Whether you are just beginning your research journey or preparing for future careers inside or outside academia, this session will provide practical tools to help amplify the reach and relevance of your work.

title: [In]Security: Military Portraiture of Gertrude Kearns
location: Joan Goldfarb Study Centre, 275 Joan & Martin Goldfarb Centre for Fine Arts @ 86 Fine Arts Road, Toronto
description: [In] Security, evokes the tensions between protection and vulnerability, certainty and instability. Made between 2002 and 2026, these works are portraits of real people: Canadian Armed Forces senior officers at critical moments in Canada’s military history. They are also records of the systems around them. Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.

title: A Short History of Library Architecture in Toronto and Beyond
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, 1st floor
description:
Christopher Hume, the architecture critic and urban issues columnist of the Toronto Star, presents a short history of library architecture. He will be commenting on the structures and social relevance of monumental libraries from Paris, Boston, New York, with a focus on Toronto Public Libraries from around the city.
Hume is the recipient of 2009 The National Newspaper Award for journalism in architecture and urban affairs. His illustrious career at the Toronto Star earned him a President’s Award for Architectural Journalism from the Royal Architectural Institute of Canada. Hume's book, William James’ Toronto Views, won a Toronto Heritage Award in 2000 and in 2004 he received a Landscape Ontario award.

title: 2026 Mulan International Film Festival
location: Innis Town Hall, 2 Sussex Ave, Toronto, ON M5S 1J5, Canada
description:
From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen.


Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song.


Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: The lab of the future: How AI is changing the way we develop new materials
location: Online
description:
Register now! 
What if AI could help uncover new materials that improve drug delivery, support sustainable agriculture and address environmental challenges? 
By combining artificial intelligence, robotics and automated experimentation, self-driving laboratories are transforming the way new materials and chemical products are discovered. Join Professor Frank Gu (ChemE) as he shares how AI-powered research is accelerating innovation in areas such as drug delivery, agricultural technologies and water treatment, enabling researchers to identify promising solutions faster and more efficiently than ever before. 
Join us on December 2, 2026, at our monthly Skule™ Lunch & Learn. 

By registering for the Skule™ Lunch & Learn event, you could potentially earn Continuing Professional Development (CPD) credits. CPDs are essential for professional engineers and limited license holders to renew their licenses annually through the PEO PEAK Program. If you’re wondering whether this event offering qualifies you for CPD credits, click here to learn more. 

About the speaker
Professor Frank Gu
Professor Frank Gu is the Director of the Institute for Water Innovation, Co-Director, Formulation Self-Driving Lab, Acceleration Consortium and a professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering and Applied Chemistry, where he holds an NSERC Senior Industrial Research Chair in Nanotechnology Engineering. A leading nanotechnology engineer, Dr. Gu has advanced the development of functional nanomaterials with applications in healthcare and environmental sustainability. 
His research spans nanomedicine, drug delivery, AI-powered materials discovery and water treatment. He has helped develop innovative nanomaterials for treating industrial wastewater and advancing drug delivery for eye diseases. In 2015, he founded H2nanO Inc., a company that commercializes energy-efficient water treatment technologies for industrial applications. Throughout his career, Dr. Gu has mentored more than 200 students and research associates, published over 110 peer-reviewed papers, and holds more than 60 issued or pending patents.

Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.

title: DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit
location: Bendale, Auditorium (Basement)
description:
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit  teaches principles of air pressure and pneumatics to kids Ages 6 and up. Each child will get to take home one kit they build.
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit
Engages children in practical activities
Teaches principles of air pressure and pneumatics
Includes all components for easy assembly
Age: 5+
The
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit
is an engaging and educational assembly kit designed specifically for children between the ages of 5 to 12. This kit offers children the opportunity to participate in practical activities, while simultaneously observing the movement of a wooden horse, propelled by the simple push and pull of a syringe. This action illustrates the principles of air pressure and pneumatic systems in a fun and interactive way.
The kit includes all necessary components for the assembly of a pneumatic horse, such as pre-cut wooden pieces for the horse structure, a pair of syringes of different sizes, orange rubber rings that function as grippers, self-tapping screws, metal shafts of varying lengths, a small screwdriver, and a plastic tube. The assembly process does not require any soldering.
Registration Begins  on November  23rd 2026 at 10:00 A.M. Spaces are limited in this program.
The program will take place in the Auditorium located in the basement. Elevator on site. If you have any questions, please call Bendale Branch at 416-396-8910.

title: Tiny Titans: Insects Up Close | Book Launch & Panel Talk with Author & Photographer Dara Ojo
location: North York Central Library, Room 101 - 1st floor
description:
Discover the hidden world of arthropods through stunning macro photography — a visual journey celebrating their beauty, complexity, and essential role in our ecosystems.
Meet
Dara Ojo
, an award-winning macro photographer and conservation storyteller whose work brings the hidden world of arthropods into vivid relief. Ojo's book,
Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem
reveals the fascinating lives of insects, spiders, and other small creatures that quietly sustain life on Earth. Captured across Canada, Mexico, Costa Rica, and beyond, Dara Ojo’s photography highlights the intricate details and diversity of these often-overlooked species.
Ojo will be leading the conversation with:
Antonia Guidotti
,
a Collections Technician with a focus on Insects & Arachnids at the Royal Ontario Museum.
Lorraine Johnson
, author and native plant and ecological gardening advocate, bridging the connection between insects, plants, habitat and practical conservation action.
Dr. Sandra Rehan
, professor at York University and principal investigator of the Rehan Lab with a focus on wild bees, pollinator biology and conservation. Rehan's research explores the biology, behaviour and evolution of bees, with a particular interest in understanding and protecting native pollinators.
Dr. Laura Timms
, Senior Specialist of Natural Heritage Management at Credit Valley Conservation and Adjunct Professor with the Daniels Faculty’s Institute of Forestry and Conservation.
Join in this evening to celebrate macro photography and the intricate beauty and ecological importance of insects and spiders, creatures that quietly anchor global biodiversity, pollination, and climate resilience.
Free program. Register for a reminder.
***Doors open at 5:30 pm. At 6:00 pm, seating becomes first-come, first-served until capacity is reached.***
5:30 pm:
Doors open. Mingle and chat with fellow nature and environmental enthusiasts!
6:00 pm:
Presentation begins. Enjoy a highly visual presentation combining photography, science, conservation and storytelling, taking the audience behind the scenes of six years documenting tiny worlds across five continents and exploring why these overlooked species matter. A light, informal conversation with guest speakers will explore why arthropods are so essential to our ecosystems, with a discussion of challenges impacting local species, and how science, photography and art can work together to help people notice, understand and care about the natural world. An audience Q&A follows this discussion.
7:30 pm:
Book signing with books available for purchase.
***
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​
Questions? Please contact North York Central Library - Business, Science & Technology Department.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesdays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: National Day of Remembrance and Action on Violence Against Women
description:
December 6 is the National Day of Remembrance and Action on Violence Against Women, a time to remember the lives lost and acknowledge the ongoing impact of gender-based violence. As we reflect, we also reaffirm our collective responsibility to stand with survivors, raise awareness, and confront the deep-rooted norms that sustain violence and hate.​
York University will hold a memorial ceremony in honour of the 14 women killed at Polytechnique Montréal on December 6, 1989: Geneviève Bergeron, Hélène Colgan, Nathalie Croteau, Barbara Daigneault, Anne-Marie Edward, Maud Haviernick, Maryse Laganière, Maryse Leclair, Anne-Marie Lemay, Sonia Pelletier, Michèle Richard, Annie St-Arneault, Annie Turcotte, and Barbara Klucznik-Widajewicz.​
The event will take place at the Bergeron Centre for Engineering Excellence on Dec. 3, 2026, from 10 to 11:00 a.m. Community members at Glendon and Markham Campuses are encouraged to gather for the livestream at their respective locations: the Ballroom in Glendon Manor and room MK2050 at Markham. The memorial ceremony, along with other events planned for the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, aims to honour those who have been lost and inspire the community to take meaningful action and support those in need.​
In solidarity, please consider wearing a white ribbon as a symbol of your commitment to ending gender-based violence. Ribbons will be available at the memorial ceremony and live stream viewing locations on Dec. 3.

title: CAIS Talks with Ervin Sedjić
location: York Lanes 280N
description:
The Centre for Artificial Intelligence & Society presents:
CAIS Talks with Ervin Sedjić

Date: Thursday, December 3, 2026
Time: 11:00am-12:30pm EST
Location: York Lanes 280N

The Algorithmic Pulse: AI’s Quiet Revolution in Medicine
 
Abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) has captured the world’s imagination, promising to transform everything from our daily commutes to the future of healthcare. Yet, behind the hype lies a crucial question: How can AI actually empower us in our professional lives? In this talk, I will cut through the buzzwords to unpack the fundamentals of AI, exploring both its powerful capabilities and its limitations. We will then take a comprehensive tour of modern medicine, exploring how intelligent algorithms are revolutionizing diverse clinical domains. From parsing complex patterns in electronic health records and analyzing ECG rhythms to tracking gait dynamics and processing high-resolution medical imaging, we will see how data is reshaping diagnostics. Along the way, I will tackle the question on everyone’s mind: Will AI replace the clinician?

Bio:
Dr. Ervin Sejdić received B.E.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees in electrical engineering from the University of Western Ontario, London, Ontario, Canada in 2002 and 2008, respectively. From 2008 to 2010, he was a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Toronto with a cross-appointment at Bloorview Kids Rehab, Canada’s largest children’s rehabilitation teaching hospital.  From 2010 until 2011, he was a research fellow at Harvard Medical School with a cross-appointment at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. From 2011 until 2021, he was a faculty member at the University of Pittsburgh. In 2021, he joined the University of Toronto as a faculty member. He is also the Research Chair in Artificial Intelligence for Health Outcomes at North York General Hospital in Toronto. From his earliest exposure to research, he has been eager to contribute to the advancement of scientific knowledge through carefully executed experiments and ground-breaking published work. This has resulted in co-authoring over 150 publications. In February 2016, President Obama named Dr. Sejdić as a recipient of the Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers. In 2017, Dr. Sejdić was awarded the National Science Foundation CAREER Award. In 2018, he was awarded the Chancellor’s Distinguished Research Award at the University of Pittsburgh. Dr. Sejdić is the editor-in-chief of Biomedical Engineering Online. Dr. Sejdić’s passion for discovery and innovation drives his constant endeavors to connect advances in engineering to society’s most challenging problems. Hence, his research interests include biomedical signal processing, gait analysis, swallowing difficulties, advanced information systems in medicine, rehabilitation engineering, assistive technologies and anticipatory medical devices.

title: The Delicious and Surprising History of The Dining Room
location: Hillcrest, Auditorium
description:
John Ota presents​ and discusses his book,
The Dining Room : Exploring the Design of Twelve Iconic Rooms in Search of the Perfect Dining Experience.​
​(Random House, 2026).
Explore the stories behind twelve iconic dining rooms in homes around the world—from a Japanese samurai house to Claude Monet's brilliant yellow dining room to Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul to Jackie Kennedy’s White House—and travel through time in pursuit of the ultimate design.​
The Dining Room is an englightening and joyous celebration of history, culture and the art of dning. Presenter John Ota's charming observations of the surprising impact of dining rooms on our lives and the cherised moments we share within them will delight armchair travellers, history fanatics and interior design enthusiasts alike.

title: Youth Hub: Democracy Fitness - Compromise
location: Albion, Auditorium
description:
Develop and exercise the skills you need to be an active participant in everyday democracy in this fun, interactive session. Democracy Fitness expands traditional ideas of what democracy is by exploring how people participate in civic life, build understanding and work together.
In this session, we’ll exercise our Compromise muscles. In a democracy, we find solutions together. When we make room for each other's approaches, more people can accept the decisions. Through a 30-min series of short, interactive exercises, you'll find out how you prefer to make decisions, practice solving a problem with those who think like you, and practice compromising with those who might think differently. This workshop will strengthen your ability to engage in meaningful dialogue.
Generously supported by: McConnell Foundation

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.
Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle.
How to Joi
n a Learning Circle:
Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions.
Please sign up with a valid email address.
A valid TPL library card is required for online circles.
Attend all four sessions online via Zoom,
Thursdays December 3, 10, 17 from 5:30-8:30pm.
Registration is a two-step process. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration.

title: 2026 Mulan International Film Festival
location: Innis Town Hall, 2 Sussex Ave, Toronto, ON M5S 1J5, Canada
description:
From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen.


Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song.


Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame.


Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale.


Screening times vary by day.

title: 3D Design: SculptGL
location: Albert Campbell, 2nd Floor, Far back room
description:
Get started on the basics of using SculptGL, a browser-based 3D sculpting and design tool. In this class, you will:
Create a simple 3D sculpt using symmetry, masking, and clean-up tools, and export your model for sharing or 3D printing.
Learn how to navigate the SculptGL workspace, menus, and options (including camera orbit/pan/zoom controls and common view shortcuts).
Use essential sculpting tools such as Brush, Inflate, Smooth, Flatten, Crease, Drag/Move, plus Masking and Transform to shape and refine a model.
Add basic surface finish and color with vertex painting / material controls, then preview your model with different render options.
Prerequisites: Mouse and keyboarding skills required.

title: Learning Things You Love with AI
location: North York Central Library, eLearning Lab
description:
Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. A tutor explains things in the way you understand, asks you questions, and helps you choose what to learn next. Learn how to turn your goal into a specific, doable learning experiment: options not answers, with a practice that survives a bad day. Decide ahead of time how you'll know it's working: revise, or stop without guilt. You'll leave with a plan you actually want to try, and a sense for what AI should never decide for you.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.
About the AI Tools Used in This Program
This program includes activities that use agentic AI tools (listed below) on library laptops.
You do not need to create your own account for this program.
Participants are encouraged to follow the Resident’s guidance throughout sessions, which include best practices on using AI.

#### **What You’ll Learn**

25 and under PWYC! (25 tickets online, 25 tickets available at the door (pending capacity - must arrive by 8pm to claim)
Ticket link: http://bit.ly/SilkwormWL


On sale now!


Storied and influential American indie-rock band Silkworm comes back to Toronto for the first time in 26 years!


Formed in 1987, Silkworm is revered by those in the know. Relocating from Missoula, Montana to Seattle and eventually Chicago, the band has released nine acclaimed albums on iconic labels including Matador and Touch and Go Records. They disbanded in 2005 following drummer Michael Dahlquist tragic passing, and reunited in 2024 to honour their late friend and collaborator Steve Albini, joined by drummer Jeff Panall (Songs: Ohia, Mint Mile). Playing together as a quartet for the first time in 30 years proved both emotional and exhilarating, inspiring a long-awaited return to the stage.

The band's enduring legacy is celebrated in the documentary Couldn't You Wait: The Story of Silkworm and the forthcoming book Lay It Down in Full View.

For their historic return to Toronto, Silkworm will be joined by Fines, the songwriting project of Darcy Hancock. Many listeners will remember Hancock as a member of Vancouver’s indie-rock favourites, Ladyhawk, whose records and non-stop touring helped establish them as one of Canada's most beloved guitar bands of the 2000s.

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Migrantes
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Migrantes is a musical and narrative experience that explores migration as an inner journey — a movement of the soul as much as of the body.

Andrea Manzoni (piano) and Mauro Sigura (oud) create a space where different musical traditions meet and interact, becoming part of a broader reflection on cultural diversity, migration, and contemporary forms of artistic expression. The performance draws on the rich and diverse backgrounds of the two musicians, combining elements of European jazz, contemporary experimentation, and the evocative sounds of Arab-Ottoman music creating an original and compelling soundscape.

Through pulsating rhythms, improvisation, and the constant exchange between piano and oud, the audience is taken through a journey that transcends geographical and cultural boundaries. Migrantes invites audiences to not only listen, but to enter an immersive experience in which musical traditions encounter one another.

title: Computers for Beginners
location: McGregor Park
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: City Place and Toronto's Historic Rail Lands! (NEW FOR 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Before the soaring condominium towers, landscaped parks, trendy cafés and bustling streets of CityPlace, you would have found yourself standing in the middle of one of Toronto's busiest railway landscapes!

For generations, this was a world of locomotives, freight trains, railway workers, industrial buildings and miles of track stretching across the waterfront. These were the Railway Lands.

An enormous piece of Toronto's industrial heartland that helped keep the city moving and connected to the rest of Canada. But as the railways changed and their operations disappeared, an opportunity emerged: what would Toronto do with all this land?

The story of CityPlace is a story about ambition, controversy, urban planning and the ever-changing face of Toronto. From the grand redevelopment visions of the 1960s, the arrival of the CN Tower and SkyDome, to the plans that transformed these former railway yards into one of Canada's most recognizable residential communities, CityPlace has quite a story to tell.

We'll explore how an industrial wasteland became a forest of condominium towers, and how Toronto reconnected with its waterfront, and how an entirely new neighbourhood was created virtually from scratch.

Let's discover CityPlace, a new neighbourhood that many Torontonians know today in passing. A fascinating history overlooked. We'll look beyond the glass towers and modern architecture to uncover the railway history, the ambitious plans, the personalities and the decisions that shaped this corner of the city.

Toronto is constantly reinventing itself, but sometimes you have to look beneath the streets, and even beneath the buildings, to understand how it happened. Come and discover the remarkable transformation!

This walking tour begins at Toronto Public Library - Fort York Branch, at the corner of Bathurst Street and Fort York Blvd. The Bathurst Streetcar stops at the corner. We end at The Well at the corner of Spadina and Front.

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

title: Past & Present: Lost in Translation
location: Online-Only Virtual via YouTube
description:
Past & Present: Lost in Translation

Past & Present: Lost in Translation Friday, December 04, 1:00 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. Virtual Panel via YouTube Join Onsite Gallery for a thought-provoking virtual panel featuring Alize Zorlutuna, Richa Narvekar, Dedra McDermott and Tannis Nielsen exploring how artists draw on cultural traditions, ancestral knowledge, and diasporic ways of knowing to shape contemporary creative practices. The discussion will focus on how visual art, dance, design, storytelling, and material practices can reinterpret cultural knowledge while creating new relationships to memory, identity, land, material culture, and the more-than-human. The panelists will share how their practices engage with inherited traditions, not simply as forms to preserve, but as living sources for experimentation, reclamation, and new ways of understanding the present. Stay involved with a live Q&A session, moderated by Onsite Gallery’s Programs & Community Coordinator, Susan Jama . ASL Interpretation will be available. The panel is live-streamed via YouTube Visit Registration Page About the Panelists Images (left to right): Alize Zorlutuna photo by Farihah Aliyah Shaw. Richa Narvekar Alize Zorlutuna is a queer interdisciplinary artist, writer, and educator whose practice explores relationships between land, material culture, and the more-than-human through diasporic ways of knowing. Moving between Tkarónto and Anatolia has cultivated an attentiveness to sites of encounter, where bodies, geographies, and elemental forces meet in ongoing processes of negotiation and co-becoming. Drawing on material and relational traditions from the SWANA region, their work spans video, installation, ebru (Anatolian water marbling), ceramics, textiles, and participatory practice, bringing together diverse materials, methods, and geographies to consider place, memory, and relation. Richa Narvekar is an Architectural Designer and Visual Artist that is interested in the connect between Art, Architecture, Urban and Interior Design. She earned her Bachelors in Architecture at CEPT University, India and was a British Council scholar to the Masters in Architecture, Urban Design program at The Bartlett School of Architecture, London, UK. She is a registered Architect under the Council of Architecture, India and holds 15+ years of experience across India and Canada. Her practice, based out of Toronto, Canada and Goa, India is multidisciplinary, with a focus on projects in Interior Design. She has led several interior design and build projects as a Senior Designer for firms in the Greater Toronto Area. She is also involved with sustainable architectural projects and community focused art and urban initiatives in both Canada and India. Her work is centered on an exploration of vernacular, critical regionalist, decolonial and anti-capitalist approaches to material and ways of making. Images (left to right): Dedra McDermott photo by Christine Do. Tannis Nielsen and Susan Jama . Dedra McDermott is a Black artist-researcher, curator, producer, movement dramaturg, and cultural steward working at the intersection of choreographic performance, archival practice, and visual culture. Following a successful career as a professional contemporary dancer across stage and screen, two significant concussions in 2018 catalyzed a profound pivot toward creative leadership. Since then, Dedra has charted a rapid, wide-ranging trajectory, navigating a nimble transition from emerging to mid-career practice. Grounded by a multifaceted academic foundation (BFA ’16, MA ’20, MFA ’24), her cross-disciplinary work champions racialized artists navigating complex creative processes. As an evolving arts leader, she supports creators re-educating the public on global Indigeneity and Black diasporic histories across Latin America and the Caribbean. Dedra is one of the former Co-Executive Artistic Producers of DanceWorks (2023–25). During her tenure, she curated and produced over 15 live presentations and choreographic development programs, while leading access-based initiatives for hard-of-hearing and d/Deaf audiences alongside community partners like VibraFusionLab. As a cultural steward who values the art of gathering, Dedra works equitably to bring a diverse public together—creating the conditions for deeper cultural connection and appreciation. Tannis Nielsen (Red River Metis and Danish ancestry) has twenty-seven years of professional experience in the arts, cultural and community sectors, and seventeen years teaching practice at the post-secondary level. Tannis holds a Masters in Visual Studies Degree (M.V.S.- 2006) from the University of Toronto, an Art and Art History-Specialist Degree from U of T, as well as a Diploma in Art and Art History from Sheridan College, in Oakville, Ontario. Tannis’ research interests include: anti-colonial/anti-capitalist theory, Indigenous decolonization methodologies, Indigenous pedagogies/oral histories, Indigenous feminism, Indigenous arts activism(s), Indigenous governance/natural law(s), and the relative investigations between Indigenous science and quantum physics. As a visual artist Tannis’s practice includes: public art, drawing, painting, new media installation, sculpture and performance. While at OCAD-U Tannis has served as Chair on the Indigenous Education council, the Equity and Diversity Committee. The Aboriginal Engagement Committee at UBC-O and has sat as Advisor to the Toronto District School Board, a member of the Toronto Native Community History Project and is the past President of The Association for Native Development in the Performing and Visual Arts (A.N.D.P.V.A.), a national Native arts organization in service since 1972. Tannis currently teaches in the painting and drawing stream at OCAD-U About the Moderator Susan Jama is an art worker with over 6 years of experience leading community engagement and public arts programming with strong grassroots experience. She is the Programs and Community Coordinator at Onsite Gallery. Susan has worked with various institutions that approach heritage in a community-minded manner including Toronto Ward Museum (TWM) and Black Artists’ Networks in Dialogue Gallery & Cultural Centre (BAND). She graduated with a Masters of Museum Studies from University of Toronto and completed her Bachelor in Psychology & History at York University. She currently serves on the Museum Education Roundtable board as co-treasurer.

title: Book Launch: Chris Ware's The Acme Novelty Library #21
location: Lillian H. Smith
description:
Torontonians: You are cordially invited to join Chris Ware as he awkwardly acknowledges the release of THE ACME NOVELTY LIBRARY #21. Ware will be in conversation with fellow cartoonist Seth (Palookaville 25).
Books will be available for purchase from The Beguiling–the official bookseller for this event.
Chris Ware
is a writer and artist and has contributed graphic fiction and thirty-two covers to
The New Yorker
since 1999. He is the author of
Jimmy Corrigan: The Smartest Kid on Earth
, which won the Guardian First Book Award in 2001;
Building Stories
, which was chosen as a Top 10 fiction book by both
the Times
and
Time
in 2012; and
Rusty Brown
which was a finalist for the PEN/Jean Stein award and named among the
New York Times
’ top 100 Books of 2019. His work has been exhibited at the Hammer Museum, the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago, and the Whitney Museum of American Art, as well as at the Adam Baumgold Gallery in New York and the Galerie Martel in Paris. In 2021, Ware received the Grand Prix de la Ville d’Angoulême and a solo retrospective of his work was presented at the Centre Pompidou in 2022, traveling on to venues in Switzerland, Italy, Holland, and Spain, before making its only US appearance in May 2026 at the Billy Ireland Library and Museum in Columbus, Ohio.
Seth
is a cartoonist, designer, and collector. His books include
Wimbledon Green, George Sprott,
and
Clyde Fans
. He is currently working on a long graphic novel that will appear in the years to come. He lives in Guelph, Ontario with his beloved wife Tania and two cats (Albert and Arthur) in an old house he has pretentiously named “Inkwell’s End.” He was born in 1962 and is increasingly feeling lost in this modern world.
Praise for Chris Ware
"Chris Ware has built a career as a sort of astronaut exploring the nature of the consciousness."—
New York Times
“Maximalist and spare.”—
Washington Post
“Nobody chronicles lives of quiet desperation with the exacting meticulousness of Chris Ware.”—
NPR

TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE

\*\*Professor Emily Ogden shares her intimate inquiry into the shadowy life and compelling work of the definitive author of the macabre.

https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/27/books/review/darkness-becomes-bright-emily-ogden.html

***Since Edgar Allan Poe’s mysterious death in 1849, his stories and poems have captivated millions of readers around the world***. Nearly two centuries later, why do we continue to descend into the darkness of his imagination—and of the genres, from horror to crime, that he pioneered?

In Darkness Becomes Bright, Ogden plumbs the darkness within Poe and enters it alongside him. She interweaves stories from his mysterious and tragic life with those of his most famous readers and translators, showing us how Poe’s vision echoes across the generations, allowing us to make peace with our own flawed humanity.

Emily Ogden speaks with author and critic Naben Ruthnum about the brief life and immortal art of Edgar Allan Poe.

Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

A Meetup trip in December . . . what can be a better gift for the holidays?! Join our travelers group on a captivating 14-day journey through the heart of Southeast Asia as we explore the vibrant cultures and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam & Cambodia (Dec 04-18, 2026)

Movie info:

Forget peace on Earth and goodwill to all men. This Christmas, Santa is on someone's naughty list!

Christmas in London has taken a decidedly bloody turn. A mysterious killer with a serious grudge against Father Christmas is stalking the streets, brutally dispatching anyone unfortunate enough to be wearing a red suit and white beard. As the bodies pile up, Scotland Yard races to uncover the identity of the murderer before another unsuspecting Santa meets a particularly gruesome end. With the festive season fast approaching, it seems nobody dressed as jolly old Saint Nick is safe!

Released in 1984, Don't Open Till Christmas is a gloriously sleazy slice of British holiday horror, packed with outrageous murders, questionable decisions, and all the wonderfully bizarre excesses of 1980s exploitation cinema. Directed by and starring Edmund Purdom, with an appearance by cult horror favourite Caroline Munro, this delightfully trashy Christmas slasher offers plenty of gore, unintentional laughs, and festive mayhem. It's everything you could want from a Killer B Cinema Christmas screening, a little naughty, a lot bloody, and most definitely not suitable for the whole family!

Killer B Cinema invites you to celebrate the holidays the B-movie way. Just remember: whatever you do, DON'T OPEN TILL CHRISTMAS! Oh, and did I mention Caroline Munro?

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Silent Lake Loop
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**This adventure is sold out. Please [join the waitlist on our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/silent-lake-loop)**
**This adventure is exclusive to Explorer members.**
**We’ve wanted to hike this trail for years. There’s 15km of undeveloped shoreline with very few people around a beautiful looped trail. We finally have the opportunity to tackle it in this Explorer exclusive.**
The Shoreline Trail starts from the day use lot on a flat, easy path that eases the group in. From there it settles beside the water and stays close to it for the rest of the hike, with the lake appearing and disappearing through the trees.
The scenery shifts every few kilometres as the trail moves between low, shaded ground and higher, drier forest. Viewpoints along the way give us places to stop and look out over the water, and we’ll take a long lunch at one of them.
It’s a small group and a long trail, which means plenty of time to talk. By the time we reach lunch at the lookout, the conversation will have covered about as much ground as the trail.
Check the trip plan (available on the website after registration) for the details, including the meeting point, gear list, and timing for the day.
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Silent Lake Lookouts:** Most of the park’s lookout points are along this trail, with wide views across the water.
**Isolated Landscape:** A day with a trail entirely to yourself.
**Beaver Meadows:** The trail crosses open meadow flats where beavers have reshaped the landscape. It’s a good stretch for spotting birds and watching the light change
**Itinerary**
**06:30** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**10:00 - 16:00** \- Hike Shoreline trail
**16:00** \- Anticipated return to cars
**19:30** \- Anticipated return to Toronto
**Event cost: $65+HST. $60 optional transport also available. Join the waitlist [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/silent-lake-loop)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Design Your Own Mahjong Tiles Workshop
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
Design Your Own Mahjong Tiles Workshop            
                                
    



    
         
    




	

	


			
Events
	







	

	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Saturday December 5, 2026
10:00 am – 12:00 pm 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    In this hands-on workshop, participants will design and glaze a set of 4 ceramic Mahjong tiles using underglaze techniques. Guided by artist Joshua Lue Chee Kong, explore pattern-making, symbolism, and personal storytelling through clay. No experience needed. Just bring your stories, creativity, and inspiration! 
Then, join us on Wednesday December 16 from 6:00 – 8:00 pm for a Mahjong Social Night, where you can view the complete set of community-designed tiles, play a game of Mahjong, and take home your tiles. The tiles will be documented as part of the Mahjong Stories Archive, a collective archive of personal stories connected to Mahjong. 

                
                    
    

	




			

    
        
             
                
                    Your ticket includes one workshop and access to the Mahjong Social Night. 

                
                    
    



        
          
          
                        
               
                Gardiner Friends : $30
                                        
                        
               
                General : $35
                                        
                      

           
            
              Gardiner Friends, log in to access your discount.* 
Not a Gardiner Friend yet? Join now at the Friend level or above to save .

                                    SOLD OUT
                
                            
           
                
                
                    
                        
                    
                
                
          
          
        

	







    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    Important Information: 

                
                    
    



    
        
             
                
                    
Please ensure the course you choose works with your schedule. This class is non-refundable and non-transferrable, regardless of the reason for withdrawal.
By signing up for this class, participants are committing to abide by the Museum’s Code of Conduct, Ticketing Policy, and Studio Policy.

Gardiner Friends, please log in to access your discount. Gardiner Friends may only purchase adult clay classes at the discounted rate for membership card holders. 

                
                    
    



    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    Instructor
                    
                
                
                    Joshua Lue Chee Kong
                    
                
                
                    Joshua Lue Chee Kong is a multidisciplinary artist from Trinidad and Tobago based in Toronto. Working across ceramics, sculpture, digital media, and community-focused projects, he explores how objects carry personal history and cultural identities across geographical boundaries. His practice draws on nostalgia and transforms familiar forms into opportunities for storytelling, connection, and belonging. 
In 2026, Joshua co-founded DeNarrative Studio with Barry Ling to support people in telling their stories through art. Their Designing Your Own Mahjong Tiles workshop grew out of their own life experiences and familial memories surrounding mahjong tiles, using the tiles’ long history and physical form as a platform for others to express their stories.
