title: THE LIFE AND TIMES OF JANE FRANKLIN  (LECTURES)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

**Toronto History Walks is currently working on bringing Lectures on the Go to a permanent home for 2027. I will continue to update this site for information as to the venue. But for now we will still meet on the steps of Old City Hall until further notice.**

**This is the last Lecture on the Go for 2026!**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2027. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join us and learn about the world and keep active and warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life.

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

Jane Franklin was a prominent 19th-century British woman known for her remarkable energy, and influence, in exploration and colonial affairs during the Victorian era.

She is best remembered as the wife of John Franklin, the Royal Navy officer who led the ill-fated Franklin Expedition. After her husband disappeared in the Arctic in 1847, Jane Franklin became one of the most determined figures in the search for him. She funded expeditions, and lobbied the British government. She mobilized public attention for decades in an effort to uncover his fate and learn the truth.

But she wasn’t only defined by that search. Jane Franklin was also a widely travelled and intellectually curious woman who visited places like Tasmania (then Van Diemen’s Land), Greece, the Middle East, and Russia.

She also supported education, and science, often working behind the scenes to influence institutions like the Royal Geographical Society. You could say she became a kind of unofficial power broker in British exploration.

In this lecture, we’ll explore the life and times of Jane Franklin. in the new biography series of timely women and men who made the world.

Upcoming topics in the 2027 series:

\*Philosophy 1: Great Minds of the Western World: Goethe to Kant! - (January 2027)
\*Philosophy 2: Great Minds of the Eastern
World: Chuang Tzu to Dalai Lama - (January 2027)
Legacy of Triangle: How a New York Factory Scandal changed North America - (February 2027)
The History of Masculinity from the Industrial Revolution to the 21st Century! (March 2027)

**So book your plans now!**

This event is for all levels and walkers, there are a few steps here and there to navigate, but mostly on one level. This event in a non-walking event.

The lecture begins on the steps of Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Bay Street and Queen Street West, and
has a ticket price of $20.00 per person, but **free with the yearly membership pass**.

title: AI for Us: Shaping AI in Toronto
location: North York Central Library, Room 2/3
description:
Toronto is one of the biggest AI cities in the world. But what do the people here actually think about it and how do we want to shape its development and use?
A panel of experts, alongside our Innovator-in-Residence
Ryan Kelln
, who know AI from very different angles, unite for an open conversation about what AI is doing to this city, and what we want it to do instead. We'll talk about:
The human beings behind the machines: what drives the people who build AI, and what worries them.
Work, money, and meaning: what happens to jobs, creativity, and value when AI lands here.
Who gets to shape it and who's left out (both are our neighbours).
The stories we tell: how art, media, news, and everyday talk shape what we expect, fear, and hope for.
No pitches, no boosterism. Just an honest conversation about the ideas and stories shaping AI in this city, and what we want it to become.
Featuring:
Jerrold McGrath
, Cultural Programmer and Theorist, In the Meantime
Joseph Wilson
, Anthropologist & Author of Humans of AI: Understanding the Humans Behind the Machines
Owais Lightwala
, Assistant Professor, Performance at The Creative School at Toronto Metropolitan University, Director,
Chrysalis
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. description:
Join us for a fun-filled workshop on paper quilling and learn how to make amazing art with paper strips!
In the spirit of the holidays, join us for a creative and relaxing experience surrounded by the beauty of Toronto Botanical Garden! In this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn the art of paper quilling and create a stunning artwork from paper strips.
 
Perfect for beginners and craft lovers alike, this session will guide you step by step through rolling, shaping, and assembling paper strips into a masterpiece on a 5″x7″ canvas. Whether you’re coming with friends, family, or enjoying some creative “me time,” you’ll leave with a beautiful handmade piece and a new skill to cherish
 
All materials provided. Suitable for adults and children ages 10 and above.
 
Saturday, December 5, 2 to 4 p.m.
Public $50, TBG Members $45 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling, which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.

title: Landmarks 6: Gladstone Hotel to The Edgewater Hotel Via Gutta Percha
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Toronto is a city that hides its history in plain sight. Beneath the glass towers are layers of stories — grand hotels that vanished overnight, political scandals whispered through stone corridors, theatres that once glittered under gaslight, and laneways where the city first learned how to become a metropolis.

This new Toronto History Walks tour invites the walker to slow down, and see the city differently.

Let's return to a bygone era: late 1930s. Parkdale would already have had a long fascinating history behind it, but you would also be looking at a neighbourhood that was changing with the times. One of the most interesting examples was the Edgewater Hotel, built in 1939 at 14 Roncesvalles Avenue, at The Queensway.

It was built by Fred Hammer and became part of a very busy transportation hub, sitting beside the Sunnyside Bus Terminal. The building has survived, although the Edgewater name eventually disappeared and the hotel went through several incarnations. It is a wonderful reminder that Parkdale's history isn't just Victorian, there is twentieth-century history here as well.

And then we come to the Gladstone Hotel, which is one of those buildings that almost seem to have been watching the neighbourhood change. The hotel we see today dates from 1889 and was designed by Toronto architect George Martell Miller in the Richardsonian Romanesque style. Its location was absolutely perfect for business: it stood across from the Parkdale railway station, and was close to the Exhibition grounds. Travelling salesmen, railway workers, visitors to the CNE and commercial travellers could all find shelter here.

The original owner was Susanna Robinson, who was left a widow with thirteen children before construction of the hotel was completed.
The Gladstone tells us something important about Parkdale itself. For decades it was a working-class gathering place, and as the factories and industries changed, so did the fortunes of the hotel. The great tower once had a cupola that could be seen from a distance, but that disappeared in the 1940s. By the later twentieth century the hotel had fallen on hard times and had developed a much different reputation. Yet it never completely lost its role as a community gathering place.

Eventually it was restored and reinvented, becoming part of the artistic and cultural life of Queen Street West.

And finally, we get to one of the great industrial stories of old Parkdale — the Gutta Percha & Rubber Manufacturing Company. Established here in 1883 on West Lodge Avenue, the factory became one of the largest employers in the neighbourhood and, at its height, the largest rubber manufacturer in Canada. They made all sorts of rubber products — hose, belting, boots, footwear, mats and eventually products connected with the rapidly growing automobile industry.

The factory operated until 1960, when changing technology, synthetic rubber and competition finally brought its long Parkdale story to an end. Three places — the Edgewater, the Gladstone and Gutta Percha — give us three very different Parkdales: the Parkdale of travel and transportation, the Parkdale of hotels and community life, and the Parkdale of factories and working people. Put them together and you begin to see just how fascinating this neighbourhood really is.

This walking tour begins at The Gladstone Hotel at the northeast corner of Queen Street West and Gladstone Avenue, one block east of Dufferin Street. We end at the corner of Queen Street West and Roncesvalles Avenue.

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

title: Meet New People, 50+ Board Games & After Dark Specials | Ages 25–45
description:
Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
December is here, and it's a lovely time to get out, meet some new faces and make room for a few new connections before the year comes to an end. ❤️

Join us for a professionally hosted social evening where you don't have to worry about who to approach or how to get conversations started. Our host guides you through short conversations, rotations and interactive connection rounds, making it easy to meet different people and discover common interests in a relaxed, welcoming setting.

We're back at Stout Irish Pub in Cabbagetown — a relaxed Irish pub with food, drinks and 50+ board games, giving you plenty of ways to keep socialising after the hosted rounds.

🎟️ Book Early & Save: [https://toronto5thdec.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto5thdec.eventbrite.co.uk)
Early Bird: CAD $10
Regular: CAD $15
At the Door: CAD $20 cash — payable to the host.
Booking ahead helps us plan the right group size and venue space, and your ticket confirms your place.

🤝 What to Expect
7:00 PM — Welcome & Drinks
Meet your host, Faye, grab a drink and settle in.
Coming alone? You're in good company! Many guests attend solo, and we'll help you feel comfortable and get connected from the start.
7:30 PM — Fast Friends
Time to meet some new people!
You'll take part in a series of short, guided conversations, with rotations that give you the opportunity to meet different people throughout the evening. Our host keeps everything flowing, so you can simply relax and enjoy meeting others.
✨ Themed Connection Rounds
We'll also bring in interactive themed rounds and conversation prompts covering interests, experiences, travel, hobbies and more.
They're designed to help you move beyond introductions, find unexpected common ground and get conversations flowing naturally.
🎲 8:30 PM onwards — Board Games & Socialising
The hosted rounds may finish, but the evening doesn't have to!
Stout has 50+ board games available. Choose a game with the people you've met, join a group, grab another drink or simply continue chatting.
You don't need to be a board game enthusiast — they're just another fun way to break the ice and spend more time together.

🍻 Staying Later?
Make the most of Stout's After Dark Special, running from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.

❤️ Why Come Along?
✔️ Meet 15–25 new people in one evening
✔️ Professionally hosted conversations that make introductions easier
✔️ Rotations so you get to meet a variety of people
✔️ Interactive themed rounds to discover shared interests
✔️ 50+ board games to enjoy afterwards 🎲
✔️ Relaxed Irish pub atmosphere with food and drinks
✔️ Reserved space for our group
✔️ Solo attendees welcome
✔️ Plenty of time to continue socialising after the hosted rounds
✔️ Friendship-focused — not a dating event

👋 Who Is It For?
Whether you've recently moved to Toronto, have been living here for years, or simply want to bring some fresh faces into your social circle, you're welcome!
You don't need to know anyone beforehand or arrive with a group. Come solo, bring a friend or simply come ready to meet people and enjoy the evening.

🌍 About Fast Friends
For over 10 years, Fast Friends has been bringing people together through professionally hosted social events in 30+ cities worldwide.
Our goal is simple: make meeting new people easier, more relaxed and more enjoyable.
Come for the conversations. Stay for the games. Leave with new connections. ❤️
Come solo. We'll guide the experience. You make the connections. 🤝

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

description:
A Christmas Carol like you've never seen it before!

The critically acclaimed holiday comedy INVASION: CHRISTMAS CAROL returns to The Assembly Theatre in Toronto this December.

It starts with six actors performing Dickens' classic tale of Ebenezer Scrooge. But about five minutes into the show, a surprise guest "Invader" crashes the story as a character of their own creation. The cast has no idea who they're playing and must improvise their way through the chaos while somehow keeping Scrooge's journey toward redemption on track.

Different Invader. Different show. Every night.

This year's special guests include PRIYANKA (December 6), ANDREW PHUNG (December 10), and COLIN MOCHRIE (December 17), alongside a rotating lineup of surprise performers.

title: Niagara Falls on Foot
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/niagara-falls)**
**Most people who come to Niagara Falls stop at the railing. We’re going beyond the falls, to the part most visitors never see.**
We’ll start where everyone starts, on the path beside the falls. It’s busy, so we’ll take our time, find a good spot, and get the photos done before the crowds thicken.
Then we leave the crowds behind. A short drive away is the Niagara Glen Nature Reserve, a protected pocket of forest deep inside the gorge. We’ll take the stairways down to the river and hike a 6km loop along the Niagara River that ends at the Whirlpool. On the way we’ll wind through huge boulders scattered across the gorge floor, stopping for lunch on one of the flat spots in the reserve and moving at a pace that works for the group.
See the falls from above, then walk the river below as the gorge walls rise on either side. Both ends of the same river, in one day.
Check the trip plan for the details, including the meeting point, gear list, and timing for the day.
**Because this adventure includes multiple stops, taking our shared transport is mandatory. Transport is included in the cost of this adventure.**
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Niagara Falls:** The full weight of the Niagara River dropping over the edge, with the roar and spray carrying along the gorge rim.
**Boulder Fields:** Large boulders left behind as the Niagara River eroded through the gorge, now draped in mosses and ferns.
**The Niagara Whirlpool:** The river hits a bend in the gorge and has nowhere to go but around, spinning into a slow, churning circle.
**Itinerary**
**08:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**10:00 - 11:45** \- Walk the Niagara Falls path
**11:45 - 12:00** \- Drive to Niagara Glen
**12:00 - 15:30** \- Hike Niagara Glen and Whirlpool trails\, with a stop for lunch
**15:30 - 18:00** \- Drive back to Toronto
**Event cost: $120+HST. Transportation is included in the cost of the adventure. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/niagara-falls)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.

title: Christmas in Old Toronto! 1855 - The Railway Era (NEW FOR 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

**So what was it like in Toronto in 1855 at Christmas time? This tour is different from the first part - Christmas in 1833 York. If you can, try and take both tours, and compare the differences in 22 years of history! Toronto changed significantly between those years.**

Imagine spending Christmas in Toronto in 1855, when the city was still a relatively young place and the streets were a far cry from the Toronto we know today. There would be no electric Christmas lights, no department-store displays, no traffic jams of cars on the DVP. Instead, Toronto was a city of horse-drawn wagons, muddy streets, wood fires, gas lamps, small shops and busy markets. And the railways were on the way to Toronto.

Christmas was becoming increasingly popular as a family celebration, influenced by traditions coming from Britain, Ireland, Europe and the United States. For many, Christmas Day meant attending church, visiting relatives and friends, enjoying a special meal and taking a welcome break from everyday life, even if just for a day.

For children, Christmas could be magical, but it was a much simpler Christmas. Toys were homemade or relatively inexpensive, and a child's Christmas might include a wooden toy, a doll, some sweets, an orange, nuts or perhaps a book. There were no shopping malls or endless advertisements telling people what they needed to buy.

Toronto's shops and markets would nevertheless have been busy in the days before Christmas. The smell of roasting meat, baked goods, spices and coal fires would have filled the air, while church bells and carriages would have been part of the Christmas landscape. And for those who were poor, Christmas could be a very different experience, making charitable giving and church relief particularly important.

But perhaps the most fascinating thing about Christmas in 1855 is how close the holiday still was to the realities of nineteenth-century life. Toronto was a city of immigrants, workers, merchants, labourers, professionals and families living in very different circumstances. Some homes would have been warm and comfortable, while others would have been cold, and crowded. There were no modern hospitals, no antibiotics, no central heating and no easy way of escaping a harsh winter. Yet people celebrated, rich or poor.

They gathered around fireplaces, went to church, shared food, told stories and tried to make Christmas special. So when we walk through Toronto and imagine Christmas in 1855, we're not simply looking at an old-fashioned Christmas, we're stepping into a city where Christmas was beginning to take on many of the traditions we recognize today, but where life itself was more uncertain.

This tour explores old Toronto during the Christmas season of 1855. This walking tour is for all walking levels. The tour begins and ends at St. James Cathedral on King Street East at Church Street. A great way to kick off the season.

This tour has a ticketed price of $15.00.

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Forest Bathing at the Garden
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Connect with nature and join us for a guided forest therapy walk!
Discover the beauty of nature in winter through a guided outdoor forest bathing walk with certified forest therapy guide Laura Bincik. At a slow pace and in community with other participants and the environment, you will be guided by a series of invitations throughout the experience to awaken your senses and intentionally connect with nature in the present moment.
 
We will gather briefly indoors to prepare for the walk and consider the origin of forest bathing as well as some of the benefits of the practice. When we venture into the Toronto Botanical Gardens and cover approximately 1.5 km on paved pathways, lawns and bare ground, at times encountering uneven terrain, inclines and declines. We will be strolling, standing and sitting (if you wish to). Your comfort and safety are most important!
 
Please note: The surrounding Wilket Creek Ravine faced severe damage due to flooding and has unfortunately remained closed to the public until repairs can be made. The upcoming Forest Bathing Walk will not cross any closed trails into the ravine.
 
As this program occurs outdoors, please dress for the weather by wearing sturdy, insulated footwear, an insulated jacket, a hat, scarf and mittens. You may wish to bring a water bottle, sunglasses, walking poles and/or a folding stool for your comfort.
 
As the walk ends, we will gather and partake in a seasonal tea and snacks, and taste honey harvested at Toronto Botanical Garden.
 
In the event of severe weather or environmental conditions, TBG staff will make alternative arrangements to the program.
 
Washrooms are available onsite.
 
The program is suited for adults 18+. All participants must sign a liability waiver at the start of the program.
 
Sunday, December 6, 1 to 3 p.m.
Registration: Public $35, TBG Members $30 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Laura Bincik
Laura Bincik is a certified forest therapy guide with the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. Following a career that straddled health care and education, Laura discovered that her lifelong sense of awe for the natural world could be enriched and shared with others to enhance wellbeing. Laura feels a connection to the land and the wonder of being in nature from countless hours spent exploring Toronto ravines in all seasons. An active member of Nature and Forest Therapy Canada, Laura follows the growing research on the mental and physical health benefits of forest bathing and is expanding her practice by connecting with local, national, and international leaders in the field.

Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

**On Sunday, December 6th, join us for Our Holiday Dinner at 2026 Michelin Recommended Bar Eugenie.** The team behind this addition to Harbord Street’s increasingly epic food scene met while working for the Alo Food Group. Bar Eugenie is an ingredient-driven restaurant and bar that brings global flavours to the heart of Harbord Village. Their cozy, lively space is made for gathering—whether around our bar or at one of their intimately set tables. This neighborhood restaurant pays homage to Eugénie Brazier, the legendary French chef often referred to as the "mother of French cooking" and the first person to earn six Michelin Stars in 1933 (three each at two different restaurants). title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Funmilola Adessun
location: Mimico Centennial, Mezzanine
description:
Throughout the month of December, the works of artist Funmilola Adessun will be on display at Mimico Public library.
Funmilola Adessun is an architect and mixed-media artist, creating as byAjike--her alias and ode to joy, culture, and storytelling. Her work is a growing legacy: a celebration of memory, meaning, and what it feels like to belong. Inspired by the opulence, kinship, and spirited community of her Nigerian culture, Funmilola draws, paints, and sculpts with tactile techniques, energetic colours, and rich textures to express her perception of what happiness means in our world.
Theme: Root to Bloom Life is one big garden, and we are the Blossoms--Seeds popping, Children budding, Teens blooming, Adults Flowering, Ripening, Striving, Thriving--Then, we return to earth, Regenerating, Seeding, Budding, Blooming. We Blossom always, with our heads held high.
This exhibit is part of TPL's
Art Exhibit Space
program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighborhoods.
The exhibit can be viewed during Mimico library's opening hours.

title: Our Infinite and Inevitable Ends: Author Talk with A.D. Sui
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall (first floor)
description:
In this exciting author talk A.D. Sui will discuss their upcoming novel Our Infinite and Inevitable Ends, a sapphic cli-fi thriller, as well as science fiction's role in today's rapidly politically and technologically changing world. Question and answer period to follow.
This sapphic cli-fi thriller is a love letter to hope in the bleakest of times, combining the multiverse-bending drama of This Is How You Lose the Time War with the cat-and-mouse chase of Killing Eve.
On a near-future Earth devastated by climate change, Dr. Cassandra Barlowe is right where she wants to be: working on an island of floating trash in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, as far away from Dr. Yana Gulsvig as possible. Cas’s research on plastic-dissolving fungi is undervalued and underfunded, thanks to the invention of deleria, a drug that allows glimpses into different timelines. For the average user, it’s a way to view lost loved ones or experience a different life, but it also offers a glimpse into worlds where humanity has solved its many global crises. Now, most science funding is dedicated to trawling these different timelines, searching for a reality with the solution to the climate devastation.
But when Yana — the world’s leading expert on deleria and Cassandra’s ex-lover — is killed in a mysterious explosion in the hub of deleria research, taking the hope of reversing climate change with her, Cas is arrested on charges of domestic terrorism. Cas must delve through timelines to piece together what happened, while watching other versions of herself and Yana live out the life they could have had — happier, more in love. As brutal government agents close in and her addiction to deleria grows, Cas has to make a choice: live in the spiraling branches of reality, seeking closure for Yana’s death until the drug shatters her mind, or live in the now, even if that means embracing her own damaged self and fighting, however hopelessly, for her own future and that of humanity.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesdays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

description:
Students get up close and personal with an eclectic group of authors while earning course credit through LA&PS’ Canadian Writers in Person (AP/CLTR 1953 6.0A) course. You’ll explore the contemporary work of renowned authors, while having the unique opportunity to engage with them in a dialogue about their work.
Readings are free and open to members of the public and to members of the York community not enrolled in the course.
Our lineups consist of a unique selection of emerging and established Canadian writers, whose writing explores a broad range of topics, and a variety of geographical and cultural landscapes. Featuring seasoned and emerging poets and fiction writers, the series highlights Canada’s ever-growing literary talent.
December 8, 2026 – I Remember Lights
In the summer of 1967, Montreal is buzzing with Expo 67—and for a young man new to the city, love and possibility feel endless, even when being queer is still criminalized. A decade later, the notorious 1977 police raid on the Truxx gay bar forces him to confront the bitter choice between happiness and safety.
Award-winning poet Ben Ladouceur’s debut novel I Remember Lights is an intimate, unforgettable portrait of queer joy, desire, and resilience in pre-liberation Montreal.

title: Dec 8 - How to Let Long-tail Guide Your 3D Annotation Workshop
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join us on Dec 8 for the “How to Let Long-tail Guide Your 3D Annotation” workshop with [Eric Hofesmann](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eric-hofesmann/).

**Date, Time and Location**

Dec 08, 2026
9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/how-to-let-long-tail-guide-your-3d-annotation-december-8-2026)**

Autonomous driving models rarely fail on the common case. They fail on the long-tail: the pedestrian stepping out from behind a parked truck or a construction zone that matches nothing in the training set. Each of those moments lives in synchronized multi-sensor data, made up of a LiDAR sweep, a ring of cameras, a timestamp, and a calibration. Fixing one means finding it, labeling it in 3D, and proving the next model handles it.

In this live session, we will take long-tail driving scenarios from discovery to 3D labels to evaluation, and make the case that 3D ground truth should be built where your data lives, not exported away from it.

description: [In] Security, evokes the tensions between protection and vulnerability, certainty and instability. Made between 2002 and 2026, these works are portraits of real people: Canadian Armed Forces senior officers at critical moments in Canada’s military history. They are also records of the systems around them. Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.

title: Logic and Philosophy of Science Group (Gordon Belot, Michigan)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Logic and Philosophy of Science Research Group is pleased to welcome as its guest speaker Gordon Belot, the Lawrence Sklar Collegiate Professor of Philosophy at the University of Michigan. Professor Belot’s primary interests are in philosophy of physics, philosophy of science, metaphysics, and epistemology. His most recent book, Accelerating Expansion: Philosophy and Physics with a Positive Cosmological Constant, explores some of the philosophical consequences of modern cosmology, focusing on the significance of the discovery of the accelerating expansion of the universe for our understanding of time, geometry, and physics. 
Talk Title
Computable Epistemology—An Idiosyncratic Primer 
Talk Abstract
Some morals. (a) In some settings, there is no such thing as an optimal method for learning (so someone who tells you there is a unique rational response to any body of evidence may be telling you something strange). (b) In some settings, induction-unfriendly scenarios are common (and do not require demonic fine-tuning). (c) In some settings, computable learners pay a price for following intuitively reasonable strategies (like relying on the simplest hypothesis consistent with their data). (d) In some settings, computable learners pay no price for being Bayesian—but only if they are willing to use priors inconsistent with their background knowledge.

Birds are woven into the fabric of Christmas traditions, serving as powerful symbols of hope, renewal, and warmth during the winter months. Their presence during the holidays, whether through festive ornaments, songs, or sightings at feeders, recalls ancient lore that connects birds with messages of love and positivity. By inviting birds into our lives and honoring them through tradition, we not only support these treasured visitors but also embrace the spirit of Christmas—one of generosity, harmony, and the celebration of nature’s enduring beauty. Jim Mackiewicz is the owner of Wild Birds Unlimited and has been helping customers with backyard bird feeding and connecting to nature for 25 years.

title: Free/PWYC Double Feature You've Got Mail + Winter Village (Distillery District)
description:
Experience Toronto
**Note: I recommend obtaining your ticket as soon as possible, as there are a limited number of seats**

**On Tuesday, December 8th, see** **Soulpepper's Double Feature** **You've Got Mail and Shop Around the Corner, plus get free, skip-the-line entry into the famous Winter Village at The Distillery District**. Be part of **Soulpepper's** **first dedicated Civic Programming lineup** rooted in a simple belief: arts spaces should also be public spaces, where people can experience culture, exchange ideas and connect, with or without a ticket. All seats are general addminssion. **Purchase your Free/PWYC ticket for You've Got Mail and Shop Around the Corner on Tuesday, December 8th at 7pm.**

**Shop Around the Corner (1940):** Two employees at a gift shop can barely stand one another, without realizing that they are falling in love through the post as each other’s anonymous pen pal.

**You’ve Got Mail (1998):** A boutique bookshop owner and a corporate chain store owner who despise each other in real life unwittingly fall in love over the Internet.

**Costa Rica’s Río Celeste Chocolate Waterfall**
Snack on chocolate-drizzled pineapple and banana treats, then step through an augmented reality portal to explore Costa Rica’s natural beauty.

**Santa’s Village at Soulpepper**
Inspired by Soulpepper Theatre’s production of “Parfumerie,” this whimsical Christmas world takes over the theatre atrium. Step into Santa’s Village with twinkling lights, displays, a vintage-inspired letter-writing station, specialty hot chocolates and, of course, Santa and his elves.

**Festive food and drinks**
With more than 50 vendors and outdoor bars, the Distillery Winter Village is a true foodie destination. New this year: Prince St. Pizza, Carousel Bakery, Sweet Crumble, Potato Bar and Peacock Bakehouse. Chef’s Lane returns following a strong debut last year, with four acclaimed chefs: Michael Angeloni, Afrim Pristine, Taylor Wells and Arush Vardhan Singh.

**Naughty or Nice Bar at Pure Spirits Courtyard** — one of the village’s signature outdoor bars — now updated with 50,000 white-and-blue holiday lights and a long communal table.

**COST**
Regular: Pay What You Can $0/ 15/ 20
Seats are general admission.

Meetup Organizer Fee: $5

Ticket Policy: All sales are final.

**SIGNING-UP**

* **RSVP, confirming if you will join for Winter Village only, or Winter Village and the Movies**
* **[Purchase](https://my.soulpepper.ca/16473/16483) your Free/ PWYC ticket for Tuesday December 8th at 7pm, and post you have your ticket in the Comment section. I will then move you to attending.**
* Members can also show up at the Theatre at event start time with their ticket in hand.

RSVPs close 2 days prior, hoping there will still be tickets. Cancellations may result in a No Show and impact future attendance.

A reminder will be sent the day before with my cell and reminder details where to meet and when.

**Meet me for the Winter Village at: 5:45pm in front of Young Centre for the Performing Arts in the Distillery District at 50 Tankhouse Lane.**
We will wait 5 mins.

**Meet me for the show at: 6:30pm in the line for the Garland Cabaret inside the Young Centre for the Performing Arts in the Distillery District at 50 Tankhouse Lane**

Once we have grabbed our seats, we can take turns buying food inside the Theatre - sandwiches, salads, pastries, beverages..

**Show Starts**: **7pm**

You've Got Mail Length: 2 hours
Shop around the Corner Length: 1 hour 37 mins

**After: meet at the same spot to chat about the show before heading home**

Enjoy and please post your comments in the Event after!

title: In Depth Sewing Intro - Dec 8 [Tuesdays - 6 week program]
location: TTLMakerspace, 192 Spadina Ave., Toronto, ON
description:
LEARN TO SEW 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Suitable for beginners. This class goes over the basics of operating a sewing machine, cutting and sewing garments, and basic pattern alterations. 
 
 
 The main project for this class is an apron custom fit to YOU. A typical first project is a tote bag,but we’ve chosen to have our students make an apron as it covers the same skills while also teaching basic tailoring and fitting. The goal of this class is to provide students with the basic skills associated with sewing, understanding patterns, and textiles, while promoting confidence and shifting the mindset of your everyday clothing as things that suit your needs and body, rather than things to simply wear. 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 This class will also explore clothing repairs and minor alterations like hemming, altering
necklines, adding pockets, etc. Students are encouraged to bring in items they wish to alter or repair. 
 
 
 Materials and equipment for all projects are provided with the course. 
 
 

 
 Schedule 
6 weeks, Tuesdays 6pm to 9pm 
 
 

 
 
 Outcomes 
 At the end of the course you will have achieved the following goals: 
 
 
- Proficiency with operating a sewing machine safely 

- Understanding of fabric types, their uses, how to prep them for sewing, and how to cut fabric 

- Comfort with taking measurements of the body and how to apply them to a pattern 

- Knowledge of basic pattern alterations and how to adjust existing garments to fit you better 

- Understanding of how to transfer patterns to fabric so that space is used as efficiently as possible 

- Understanding of pinning and ironing techniques 

- Familiarity with basic sewing techniques including seams, hemming, hand stitching,
applying pockets, fasteners including buttons, zippers, snaps, and ties, as well as
different stitch uses for different techniques and materials

- Basic repairs like fixing holes, torn seams, holes in pockets, adding patches

- Basic alterations like adjusting hems, changing necklines, switching out buttons or other fasteners

title: Collective Body
location: Off Campus Koffler Arts, Koffler301, 180 Shaw St., Toronto
description:
Collective Body

About the Exhibition Presented as part of OCAD University’s 150th Anniversary Program, Collective Body is a multidisciplinary project by Gülay Alpay, selected and awarded for support through the anniversary program. Bringing together installation, performance, wearable art, photography, and experimental 16mm film, the exhibition explores inclusivity, connection, collective identity, and shared responsibility. Rooted in the belief that art can bring people together, Collective Body invites OCAD U students, faculty, alumni, and staff to participate in a shared creative experience that celebrates community, collaboration, and belonging. At the heart of the exhibition is a large-scale wearable dress that functions as both a sculptural installation and a living artwork. Activated through movement and collective participation, the dress becomes a symbol of unity, carrying individual memories, emotions, and experiences within a shared body. The exhibition also features behind-the-scenes photographs documenting the project's creative development, alongside an experimental 16mm short film that explores the relationship between the body, movement, and collective consciousness. Artist: Gülay Alpay Curatorial Advisor: Dr. Kahawhitha Leah Shenandoah, Acting Chair, Indigenous Visual Culture (INVC), OCAD University Project Coordinator: Ece Ugrasiz Photography & Filmmaking: Shako Opening Day: 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m., Dec. 9, 2026

title: [In]Security: Military Portraiture of Gertrude Kearns
location: Joan Goldfarb Study Centre, 275 Joan & Martin Goldfarb Centre for Fine Arts @ 86 Fine Arts Road, Toronto
description: [In] Security, evokes the tensions between protection and vulnerability, certainty and instability. Made between 2002 and 2026, these works are portraits of real people: Canadian Armed Forces senior officers at critical moments in Canada’s military history. They are also records of the systems around them. Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.

title: Pop-up Performance: Empire of Wild with the Canadian Opera Company
location: Northern District, Main Foyer
description:
From your bookshelf to the stage, enjoy an informal musical performance of Empire of Wild, a new Canadian opera making its world premiere at the
Canadian Opera Company (COC)
this season. Based on the bestselling novel by Cherie Dimaline, the opera is composed by Métis composer Ian Cusson.
The performance features artists of the Canadian Opera Company Ensemble Studio in excerpts of the opera.
The story centres on the character of Joan, a tenacious woman who seeks to rescue her husband from the grips of the rougarou, a werewolf-like creature often described in stories passed down over generations. Part conversation and part performance, this event showcases the breadth and power of Métis storytelling.
Register for a reminder. Performance starts at 12:35 pm in the main foyer of the branch. Experience this performance as you enter the branch. Limited seats. Stay after the performance to mingle with fellow attendees to chat about the music.
This program is produced by Canadian Opera Company (COC).
Personnel:
Emma Pennell, soprano
Ariana Maubach, mezzo-soprano
Ben Wallace, baritone
Kimly Wang, piano
Repertoire:
Cecile’s Aria “You Poor Man”
Heiser’s Aria “I Never Wanted to Share This”
Joan’s Aria “My Prayer is Small”
(All from Empire of Wild by Cherie Dimaline/Ian Cusson).

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesdays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Dec 10 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Dec 10, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-december-10-2026)**

**Your mAP is fine. Your slices are not. Finding the images that actually matter**

A single mAP can look acceptable while one slice is unusable, small objects, occlusion, or a confused class. I will run a pretrained detector on a few hundred public images (COCO-style, not a production crawl), report the headline metric, then break the same run by slice and walk through the worst samples.

The claim is modest: you do not need a million images or a trained-from-scratch model to see what the mean is hiding, and you cannot relabel everything, so the next labeling budget should follow those slices. No employer data and no confidential dashboards.

*About the Speaker*

[Amandeep Jiddewar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amanfj/) is a Machine Learning Engineer at Pinterest, with prior work in U.S. manufacturing analytics (CertainTeed / Saint-Gobain) and marketplace allocation (QuinStreet). Emory Goizueta MSBA (2019), Kaggle Expert. This talk is in his personal capacity and does not represent his current or prior employers.

**Production AI Agents: Tool Use, Evaluation, Guardrails and Observability**

Building an AI agent is easy. Knowing whether it is behaving reliably in production is much harder. This session explores how to evaluate agents that use tools and external systems, including tool-call validation, tracing, observability, failure analysis, guardrails, permissions, and human review.

Attendees will learn practical patterns for understanding not just what an agent answered, but why it acted and whether the action was safe.

*About the Speaker*

[Akshay Talathi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/akshaytalathi/) is a Vice President at Goldman Sachs with over 10 years of experience building large-scale, cloud-native, and distributed systems across financial services and technology. His current focus is GenAI and agentic AI, including production AI agents, MCP, enterprise integrations, guardrails, observability, and reliable AI-driven workflows.

**From Virtual Worlds to Physical AI: Building Simulation Pipelines That Survive the Real World**

Robots are moving beyond perception systems that only detect and classify objects toward systems that must understand a scene, learn behaviors, and act in the physical world. In this talk, I’ll show a practical Physical AI workflow using OpenUSD, BowerBot, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to build a robot’s virtual world, including its body, cameras, sensors, and environment.

We’ll explore how demonstrations and reinforcement learning can teach behaviors in simulation, how vision and sensor data become observations for a robot policy, and what needs to match when transferring that behavior to real hardware. The demo follows a small robot from a simulated environment toward a real-world task, exposing both the power and the limitations of sim-to-real.

The goal is to make the path from pixels to actions concrete for computer vision and machine learning practitioners.

*About the Speaker*

[Arturo Morales Rangel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arturo-morales-rangel) is the founder of Binary Core LLC, a Physical AI engineering company working across simulation, perception, robot learning, and deployment.

**Prompting Video-Language Models in Production: Lessons from Enterprise Video Tagging and Evaluation**

Video-language models can now describe, tag and answer questions about long-form video, but production results depend heavily on prompt design and evaluation. This talk shares field lessons from deploying such models for media, news, streaming and sports organizations, including how to structure prompts for consistent, schema-bound outputs across hours of footage.

On one sports video-tagging project, consolidating the prompt definitions cut estimated processing cost about 3x, and about 90% of the originally reported issues were later resolved through prompting alone. I'll also walk through building evaluation frameworks for video outputs, including for hard domains like egocentric video, and what changes when migrating between model versions.

Attendees will leave with reusable prompt patterns and an evaluation checklist they can apply to their own video pipelines.

*About the Speaker*

[Yash Gugale](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yashgugale/) is a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at TwelveLabs in New York, integrating video foundation models (Marengo for embeddings and search, Pegasus for video-language understanding) for media, news, streaming and sports customers. He previously spent about six years in video streaming engineering at Peloton and Samsung TV Plus, and holds an MS in Computer Graphics Technology from Purdue.

Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.

title: Aesthetics Reading Group (Alexandra King, Simon Fraser University)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Aesthetics Reading Group is pleased to welcome as guest speaker Alexandra King, associate professor in the Department of Philosophy at Simon Fraser University. Currently, she is thinking through what aesthetic normativity looks like: the shape it takes, its parallels and interactions with other varieties of normativity (like the moral and epistemic), and whether it can be said to exist at all. Within aesthetics, she is also interested in an assortment of issues, including subtlety, high and low art, aesthetic/artistic agency, and applied arts. She also owns, runs, and regularly writes for the aesthetics and philosophy of art blog Aesthetics for Birds, which aims to make concepts and arguments in academic aesthetics accessible to a wide, public audience. 
Talk Title
What Is the Aesthetic? 
Talk Abstract
Talk of aesthetics – including among other things talk of aesthetic reasons and value, aesthetic practices, and aesthetic agency – is on the rise recently. These discussions aim to acknowledge the ways aesthetics can inform such debates and be informed by them. But it often remains unclear what, exactly, makes a value or reason or practice aesthetic, especially once we distinguish the aesthetic from the artistic. To sidestep this difficulty, a recent trend in aesthetics is to explicitly set aside the talk’s titular question, claiming that such a question needn’t be answered before proceeding. This talk challenges that tendency, arguing that we need a more precise conception of the subject matter at hand if we are to make real progress in giving such accounts. I propose and defend a view on which the aesthetic has to do with sensation, not narrowly restricted to sense perception, but construed more broadly to include mental imagery as well as feeling and emotion, ideation, comprehension, and understanding. I then examine which conclusions this framework licenses us to draw about aesthetic reasons and value, practices, and agency.

title: How to 10x Your DevOps with AI (Without Deleting Production)
description:
Toronto Enterprise DevOps User Group
Autopilot made flying safer, not because the autopilot is perfect, but because of the instruments, checklists, and feedback around it. AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor are no different. Too many teams are betting on better models and longer prompts, when what agents actually need is the boring stuff DevOps has preached for years: fast feedback, deterministic checks, and tight controls.

An AI coding tool reportedly deleted and recreated an AWS environment. Another wiped a production database during a code freeze. Skipping the checks in "YOLO mode" is fast, right up until it isn't. This talk is about the alternative: doubling down on DevOps in the age of AI, so teams can move faster with agents inside locked-down enterprise environments, without betting production on a prompt. When developers with AI commit faster than ever, the pipeline becomes the bottleneck. We'll look at how to unblock them with fast CI/CD in GitHub Actions and on-demand cloud environments. Then we'll get practical: how to 10x your delivery with modern AI tooling, including Claude Code, voice-driven development, remote access, and running agents in parallel.

You'll leave with:
\- Real takeaways for going fast and safe with AI agents\, from GitHub Actions pipelines to cloud environments
\- How to 10x your DevOps workflow with Claude Code\, voice\, and remote access

*Come at 5:30 pm have some pizza and chat for a bit. The presentation starts at 6:00 pm.*

title: Ghost Stories of Toronto: Modern Phantoms
description:
As Toronto has grown into a major metropolis, its ghost stories have grown along with it. Many of our city's most bone-chilling tales were born out of that rapid evolution — and the sense of unease it has often caused. We'll conclude this series of talks with author Adam Bunch by exploring ghost stories from Toronto's more recent past. We'll take the subway with the spectre believed to haunt the TTC, set sail with the ghost ship of Etobicoke Creek, and meet the demon said to have terrorized one of Canada's most famous folk singers.
About this event's guest:
Adam Bunch
Read More:
The Toronto Book of Love
The Toronto Book of the Dead
About this series:
You can learn a lot about Toronto through its ghost stories. Whether you believe in the supernatural or not, the tales we tell about spirits and spectres illuminate the true history of the city. They're often tied to dramatic stories of death and disaster, to fascinating historic sites, and to pivotal moments that helped shape our communities. In this series of talks by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore Toronto's past through tales of ghosts, séances and hauntings. Whether it's phantom horses from the War of 1812, the strange prime minister who believed in the occult, or the ghost who was arrested by the Toronto Police Morality Squad, these supernatural stories have a lot to teach us about the history of the place we call home.

title: Early Modern Philosophy Research Interest Group (Andreea Mihali, Wilfrid Laurier)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Early Modern Philosophy Research Interest Group is pleased to welcome as its guest speaker Andreea Mihali (Wilfrid Laurier University) who is an expert in critical thinking, informal logic and argumentation theory, modern philosophy (Descartes to Kant) and visual and musical arguments. 
Talk Title
Descartes’ Omissions 
Talk Abstract
In the Meditations Descartes insists that readers closely follow the example and meditating steps set out in this text (AT VII, 10; CSM II, 8). Given this emphasis on the right order of reasons, it is at least prima facie surprising to also find the following remarks in the Second Replies: “Moreover there are many truths which although it is vital to be aware of them – this method [analysis] often scarcely mentions since they are transparently clear to anyone who gives them his attention” (AT VII, 156; CSM II, 110 – emphasis added).  
A careful reading of Descartes’ works shows that such remarks regarding things left out of Descartes’ actual text are far from being unique. This paper aims to classify Descartes’ omissions, to inquire into what these omissions tell us about Descartes’ approach and to make some preliminary remarks about the light these omissions shed on his explicit statements and theses. 
After discussing and backing up with textual evidence seven criteria of classification of omissions (content-relatedness, scope, means of identification, deliberateness, motivation, purpose and who is expected to remedy these omissions), I will apply them to Descartes’ published works. This application will show that Descartes’ account of the progression of his published works in the Preface to the French Principles (progression from the Discourse and the three accompanying Essays, through the Meditations, to the Principles – Latin and French), this progression in effect also tracks omissions and corresponding additions.

title: Film Screening: ᑕᐅᑐᒃᑕᕗᒃ / Tautuktavuk / What We See
location: Malvern, Community Room
description:
Join us to watch ᑕᐅᑐᒃᑕᕗᒃ / Tautuktavuk / What We See in Inuktitut with English Subtitles.
The film screening will include an 82 minute film and a 20 minute pre-recorded Q&A (102 minutes total).
Blurring the line between narrative and non-fiction, Uyarak and her eldest sister Saqpinak, embark on a difficult healing journey after a traumatic event that reminds them of the importance of community, culture, and family.
Feel free to drop in, no registration required. Registering will send you a reminder before the event.
SYNOPSIS: After experiencing a traumatic event in Igloolik (an Inuit hamlet in Foxe Basin, Qikiqtaaluk Region in Nunavut), Uyarak leaves her community and family in Nunavut to live in Montréal. When Covid-19 lockdowns close off the Canadian Arctic from the rest of the world, Uyarak is further separated from her closest friend, eldest sister, Saqpinak. This extreme situation blurs the lines of both the fictional lives of the sisters, and the non-fiction lives of the film’s directors, Lucy Tulugarjuk and Carol Kunnuk, who play the sisters. The film becomes a series of vignettes of heartache and healing – both in the dramatic based-on-true-events narrative, and the lived reality of these characters and creators. Uyarak doesn’t remember much about one terrible night of domestic violence, but Saqpinak does. Through Zoom calls, Uyarak talks about healing from years of trauma and abuse, and how the counselling sessions she goes to, and other cultural reconnections, are helping her heal. At the same time, Saqpinak is raising a family and hosting live shows about her community. Things are difficult at home – Saqpinak herself is experiencing domestic abuse at home but is waiting to talk about this to Uyarak when she can get home. When Covid-19 restrictions ease, Uyarak is finally able to travel home to Igloolik. At home, she embarks on a deeper healing journey visiting with family and elders, in town, and out on the land. Uyarak and Saqpinak share more stories and support one another in their short time together before Uyarak must return to Montréal.
ABOUT THE CO-DIRECTORS: Lucy Tulugarjuk is an award-winning actor, creative performer, and the Executive Director of Nunavut Independent Television Network (NITV). NITV created Canada’s first 24/7 Inuit language television station, Uvagut TV. Lucy is the co-writer, director of Tia and Piujuq, and assistant director for Zacharias Kunuk’s, One Day in the Life of Noah Piugattuk. In addition to her work in film and television, Lucy is a skilled Inuktitut translator. Carol Kunnuk is a filmmaker working in independent television and film with Isuma for over 25 years as a writer, camera operator, production supervisor, assistant director, actor, and editor. Her personal work includes the short, Being Prepared (NFB), and creator/director of the documentary, Attagatuluk. Carol currently directs and produces Welcome to my Qammaq, a weekly live television show broadcasting across Canada on Uvagut TV.

title: Nerikomi with Eiko Maeda | Nov 14 & 15 2026 | Dupont
location: 300 Campbell Avenue, Unit 115 Join us for a two-day workshop with ceramic artist Eiko Maeda, exploring the traditional Japanese technique of Nerikomi. Unlike surface decoration, Nerikomi builds pattern directly into the clay body itself, layering, stacking, and folding differently coloured clays until intricate designs run through the material from edge to edge. Over two days, you'll learn to prepare and condition coloured clays, build your own pattern blocks and work through four distinct pattern designs, each resulting in a finished ceramic piece approximately 15 cm in diameter. Eiko will guide you through every stage, from initial slab to shaped, refined form. This workshop is open to makers at all levels. No prior experience with Nerikomi is required, though some familiarity with hand-building is an asset. ABOUT EIKO MAEDA Eiko Maeda trained in Japanese lacquer at Joshibi University of Art and Design in Tokyo before discovering ceramics after relocating to Canada. She has spent over a decade developing and teaching her Nerikomi practice from her studio in Ontario, and has been recognized by the Ontario Arts Council and the Toronto Outdoor Art Fair. In 2026, her work was exhibited in Taipei, Taiwan. PLEASE NOTE Firing is included in the registration fee. Finished works will be available for pick-up approximately 3–4 weeks after the workshop concludes. You will be notified by email when your pieces are ready. All Specialty tools will be available for usage with the option to purchase your tools at the end of the course., Toronto, ON

title: Muskoka Highlights Hike
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/muskoka-highlights)**
**Muskoka’s best-known views and best-loved trails, packed into one day out of the city.**
We meet in Toronto and ride out together, so no one is stuck behind a wheel after a day on the trails. First stop is Hardy Lake Provincial Park, where we walk the 7km loop at an easy pace. Expect a rugged shoreline path with tree roots and patches of bare rock, and the lake in view through the trees.
After the lake, we drive to Huckleberry Rock. The trail is short, but it climbs steadily, and the trees open up to a wide slab of granite with Lake Muskoka spread out below. Locals have been coming up here for over a century, and it’s easy to see why. We’ll take our time at the top.
The day finishes in Bracebridge. You’ll have time to walk the main street, explore cute cafes and bookstores to find something hot to eat or drink, and stretch your legs before the ride home. Lastly, we will check out Bracebridge falls before heading home.
The idea is simple: see what Muskoka does best, from a lakeside trail to a big open view to a small town worth wandering. We take care of the planning and the driving, so all you need to do is show up and enjoy it.
Check the trip plan for the details, including the meeting point, gear list, and timing for the day.
**Because this adventure includes multiple stops, taking our shared transport is mandatory. Transport is included in the cost of this adventure.**
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Hardy Lake Boardwalk:** A wooden walkway over the water on the lake loop, and one of the most photographed spots in the park.
**Huckleberry Rock Lookout:** A short climb up to an open clearing with sweeping views across Lake Muskoka and the forest beyond.
**Explore Bracebridge:** A small town on the Muskoka River, with local shops, cafés, and places to eat.
**Itinerary**
**08:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**10:30 - 14:00** \- Hike Hardy Lake trail with a stop for lunch along the way
**14:00 - 14:30** \- Drive to Huckleberry Rock
**14:30 - 15:00** \- Hike to Huckleberry Rock viewpoint
**15:00 - 15:20** \- Drive to Bracebridge
**15:20 - 16:30** \- Explore Bracebridge
**19:00** \- Anticipated return to Toronto
**Event cost: $120+HST. Transportation is included in the cost of the adventure. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/muskoka-highlights)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

During the week of Digital International Rights Days, take part in a full-day hackathon where you'll work in a team to imagine and design a software prototype that advances digital rights, then experiment with AI-assisted coding to build it. Explore AI tools and discover how they can help build or maintain software that serves communities. Apps for your community, by your community.
Please bring your own computer. No coding experience is required, but participants should have mouse, keyboarding and internet skills.

must register individually

title: Cooking with Spirit: Stories, Flavours, and Traditions from Indigenous Fusion Cuisine
location: Riverdale, Program Room 1
description:
In this talk, Chef David Wolfman will take the audience on a culinary and cultural journey through the pages of his cookbook,
Cooking With the Wolfman
. Drawing from the traditions of the Xaxli’p First Nation and his decades of professional culinary expertise, David will share stories behind the making of select recipes an explore how Indigenous foods connect us to the land, to community, and to sustainable living. Participants will also learn how cooking can be an act of reconciliation and cultural preservation.
At the end and of the program, David will lead a Q&A session and share food samples with attendees.
Registration Required.
David Wolfman, from Xaxli’p First Nation, has reshaped Canada's gastronomic landscape and global perceptions of Indigenous and North American cuisine. David was the first of many to have an Indigenous catering enterprise in Toronto. Outside of the kitchen, Chef Wolfman shares his love of food, family and friendship through education. He leads workshops on Indigenous culinary practices, cultural tourism, and economical family food budgeting. He has done so at youth conferences, business conventions, and through his role as a Culinary Arts professor at George Brown College. Chef Wolfman was also an executive producer and host of "Cooking with the Wolfman" on APTN from 1999 to 2017, where he shared Indigenous Fusion foods to viewers across Canada. Chef Wolfman lives in Toronto and enjoys being walked by his Boston Terrier.

description:

Les réseaux d’ornements imaginés par Gustav Klimt concoururent ainsi à magnifier ses modèles tout en préservant leur sensibilité. Quant aux aplats de couleur avec lesquels Henri Matisse ou André Derain architecturent leurs autoportraits, ils traduisent leur vie intérieure avec plus d’intensité encore. Autant de recherches qui ouvrent la voie à l’art contemporain.
Cette conférence vous est proposée par Gilles Genty, historien de l’art, en partenariat avec l’
Alliance française de Toronto
.

title: Songs of My Mother: A Celebration of African Women Concert
location: The Redwood, 1300 Gerrard St E, Toronto, ON M4L 1Y7, Canada
description:
Batuki Music Society presents Songs of My Mother: A Celebration of African Women at the Redwood Theatre on Saturday December 12th at 8 pm. Doors open at 7 pm.

Three electrifying vocalists and a dancer with roots on the African continent will honour the role of women and mothers in carrying on musical traditions.

Songs of My Mother: A Celebration of African Women, curated by Batuki Music Society will showcase diverse stories and musical styles from different regions of sub-Saharan Africa. Featured will be JUNO Award winners, South African-born Lorraine Klaasen and Malian-born Djely Tapa, also on the line-up is Melat Mengesha, winner of the Balageru (Ethiopian Idol) and Guinea-born dancer Mabinty Sylla. These women share their unique talents in a showcase of musical diversity and artistic excellence, supported by an ensemble of accomplished musicians from Toronto and Montreal.

This presentation shines a light on female singers and their significance in African customs, rituals and ceremonies. The first words or language that a child hears from their mother are often shared in song. This introduction to sound and words through song is a very common element in the bonding process between a mother and her newborn in most African cultures. Though singing is not solely done by women in most African societies, it is true that the female voice is ever present and sometimes is not given a prominent role that it deserves. Women are often discouraged from assuming leading roles, especially as bandleaders.

More than just an unforgettable evening of music and storytelling, Songs of My Mother aims to inspire mothers, daughters, grandmothers, sisters, and aunts to stand together and celebrate themselves as major contributors to the arts and the community.

title: The Music Gallery & The Ministry of Phonic Services presents Devin DiSanto, Anne-F Jacques, Shadow Pattern + Installation by Tümmler Studio
location: Friends House, 60 Lowther Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 1C7, Canada
description:
Join us at Friends House for an evening of exploratory sound art performance, in a triple-bill bringing together distinct builders of the form—Devin DiSanto, Anne-F Jacques, and Shadow Pattern, featuring installation art by Izzy Mink of Tümmler Studio.

Stringing together sonic elements of the everyday into ideations and completions of tasks, Devin DiSanto visits from New York, pushing the conceptual bounds of how electroacoustic sounds are created and performed.

We are also joined by the acute material tinkerings of Anne-F Jacques (Montréal) and the paint-stripped tape ripples of Shadow Pattern (Hamilton), for a night of three subtle solo sets bridging active listening with experimental performance.

As a textural complement to the live sets, the evening will also feature the installation ‘Persistent Feeder’, by Izzy Mink of Tümmler Studio.

Co-presented and curated by the Ministry of Phonic Services, a Toronto-based concert presenter and experimental record label.

If cost is a barrier, please reach out to us at sara@musicgallery.org mailto:sara@musicgallery.org to reserve a lower-priced PWYC ticket at the door. No one will be turned away for lack of funds (NOTAFLOF).
