title: Survivalist Series: Firecraft Level 1
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fire-craft-intro-5)**
***Discover the ancient art of safely creating and maintaining fire without lighters or matches!***
For thousands of years, fire has been our greatest ally for warmth, safety, cooking, and survival. But in the wild, fire doesn’t come easy. It takes knowledge, patience, and the right technique.
We are back for another installment of this popular course to teach you the beautiful art of fire. You’ll begin to master the craft with hands-on guidance from our expert firecraft instructor - guide Kyle.
You'll be shown and encouraged to practice:
1\. Ferrocerium rod techniques with multiple tinders
2\. Traditional flint & steel fire lighting
3\. How to reliably start an effective fire
This course will give you the foundation to create fire anywhere, anytime.
**Included:** Your own high-quality ferro rod to take home and keep the fire burning wherever you go.
**Need a knife?** You'll be using a knife throughout the day, so a fixed-blade knife is essential. If you don't have one, you can purchase a high quality Mora knife during your check out. Please note that a knife is required for this course!
**Who It’s For:** This course is for beginners and intermediate survivalists alike. Bring your curiosity, a willingness to learn, and a love of getting outside. This is an amazing opportunity not only to learn from our expert, but it's a fun, practical lesson at a uniquely low price.
**About this series:** The Survivalist Series is an expert-led set of courses designed to develop applicable and life-saving skills in the outdoors. Keep your eyes peeled for more courses on many other topics coming soon!
**Due to the cost of parking at Bronte Creek, WU transport is recommended for this course.**
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Ancient techniques:** Learn unique firecraft techniques from long ago that do not need matches or a lighter.
**Survivalist skills training:** Develop essential skills to survive and thrive in the wild.
**Fire kit included:** Every participant gets this kit including a ferro rod and variety of tinders.
**Itinerary**
**10:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**11:00** \- Arrive at course location
**11:00 - 16:00** \- Introduction to fire craft course
**16:00 - 17:00** \- Drive back to Toronto
**Event cost: $95+HST. $50 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fire-craft-intro-5)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***
**“Se Habla”** is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Mondays and Wednesday)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: Afternoon Book Club
location: Woodside Square, Program room
description:
Join us on the following Monday afternoons to discuss books in a friendly and social atmosphere: September 14th, October 19th, November 9th, and December 14th.
This month we will be reading
The MANIAC
by Benjamin Labatut.
The MANIAC
is a 2023 novel by Chilean author Benjamin Labatut, and his first in English (compared to his usual Spanish). It is a fictionalized biography of polymath John von Neumann interwoven with tripartite narratives exploring the intersection of human genius, rationality, and artificial intelligence. Told via oral-history style from peers, wives, and colleagues, Labatut attempts to decipher core themes of reason and madness, the edge of progress, and the loss of the sacred. While a spiritual sequel to
When We Cease to Understand the World
,
no prior knowledge of science or technology is needed to appreciate Labatut's polymathic portrait of von Neumann.
Participants can borrow a copy of the book from the Woodside Square branch upon registration.

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: Dying of Whiteness
location: Toronto Reference Library, Discussion Room, 3rd Floor
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
December's book is
Dying of Whiteness: How the Politics of Racial Resentment Is Killing America's Heartland
by Jonathan Metzl, Professor of Sociology and Psychiatry at Vanderbilt University. Copies of the book are available in print,
eBook
&
eAudiobook
format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"In the era of Donald Trump, many lower and middle class white Americans are drawn to politicians who pledge to make their lives great again. But as
Dying of Whiteness
shows, the policies that result actually place white Americans at ever-greater risk of sickness and death. Physician Jonathan M. Metzl's quest to understand the health implications of "backlash governance" leads him across America's heartland. Interviewing a range of everyday Americans, he examines how racial resentment has fueled progun laws in Missouri, resistance to the Affordable Care Act in Tennessee, and cuts to schools and social services in Kansas. And he shows these policies' costs: increasing deaths by gun suicide, falling life expectancies, and rising dropout rates. White Americans, Metzl argues, must reject the racial hierarchies that promise to aid them but in fact lead the nation to demise."
Drop in. No registration required.

title: Above the Fire by Michael O'Donnell
description:
Post-Apocalyptic Book Club - Toronto Chapter
It's our last PABC meetup of 2026!

This time we'll be reading *Above the Fire* by Michael O'Donnell. Here's the blurb:

Laboring under a shared loss, a father and son set out on a late-season backpacking trip through the mountains of New Hampshire. They find beauty and solidarity in the outdoors, making friends along the way and falling into the rhythms of an expedition. But when war breaks out during their hike, they are forced to withdraw even further into the backcountry.

Surviving an alpine winter by themselves, father and son must endure the elements, the solitude, and the ever-present danger of outsiders. As their isolation intensifies, their bond with each other grows more fierce. From their mountain refuge they must confront the perils of a changed world until they are forced to decide whether--and how--to rejoin society.

title: From Interview Jitters to Interview Confidence: Navigating In-Person, Virtual and AI-Powered Interviews
description:
Interview formats are evolving, but the ability to communicate your experience, value and potential with confidence remains essential. This practical webinar will help job seekers prepare for in-person, virtual and increasingly common AI-powered interviews.
Participants will learn how to manage interview anxiety, structure clear and compelling responses, communicate effectively on camera and adapt their approach to different interview formats. We will also explore what employers and recruiters assess during interviews, common mistakes to avoid, and how candidates can remain authentic and human throughout a technology-enabled hiring process.
Attendees will leave with practical strategies to approach their next interview with greater clarity, preparation and confidence.
Speaker Bio
- Wagisha Singh is a Talent Acquisition Specialist with over six years of experience recruiting across Canada and the United States. She has partnered with organizations ranging from growing businesses to large national employers, hiring talent across logistics, transportation, supply chain, skilled trades, healthcare, accounting and finance, operations, and leadership roles.
This program is part of TPL's Career Coaches in Residence and is generously supported by our lead donor Azrieli Foundation along with supporting donors Fidelity Canada, Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter and
The William and Nona Heaslip Foundation.
For more information, please visit
tpl.ca/careercoach

title: Integrated Course Design Workshop (Online, Dec. 15 & Jan. 19, 10am-12pm)
location: Online (Zoom)
description:
Designing a course can be overwhelming!  Whether you need motivation to get started, want concrete strategies to structure your curriculum, or are seeking a community of engaged instructors to connect with, the integrated course design workshop is for you. 
Guided by Fink’s model of Integrated Course Design and Universal Design for Learning (UDL), session 1 will focus on using completely constructed course learning outcomes to generate ideas for course assessments. 
Session 2 will consist of small-group problem solving where each participant will have time to share an aspect of their course design they are working through with opportunity to receive feedback or suggestions from group members.
Register through YULearn (requires Passport York sign-in) using our registration form ( https://yulearn.yorku.ca/local/yulearn/learning_opportunity.php?id=2264 ).

You've asked an AI chatbot questions. But there's another kind of AI that doesn't just answer: it acts.
In this demo-driven talk with our Innovator-in-Residence,

title: ABCD Reads Exit Party by Emily St. John Mandel
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***[Exit Party](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4792123)*** by Emily St. John Mandel (author of ***Station Eleven***).
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/5182568441053184) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"From the bestselling author of Station Eleven, Exit Party is Emily St. John Mandel’s epic new story of crimes committed and loves lost across worlds and decades.
2031\. America is at war with itself\, but for the first time in weeks there is some hope: the Republic of California has been declared\, the curfew in Los Angeles is lifted\, and everyone in the city is going to a party\.
Ari, newly released from prison, arrives with her friend Gloria just as a fragile new era begins. But there are people at the party who shouldn’t be there. Something is very wrong...
Years later, living a different life in Paris, Ari remains haunted by that night. Whatever happened at the party fractured her sense of reality – and may hold the key to a very different world.
Freedom and surveillance, art and survival, love and loss in a broken world: Exit Party is the electrifying new novel from Emily St. John Mandel." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/241683548-exit-party?ac=1&from_search=true&qid=8V5Hrtzu0U&rank=1))

"A novel of doubles, shadow worlds, and fractured timelines as a man disappears from a glittering Los Angeles party, and a woman—a gunrunner, an art collector, an operative of the State—searches for answers." (from [BookMarks.reviews](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/exit-party/))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Sven Beckert: A Global History of Capitalism
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL and Toronto Metropolitan University present historian Sven Beckert in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
As the Laird Bell Professor of History at Harvard University and co-chair of the university's Program on the Study of Capitalism, Sven Beckert has spent his career tracing how a single economic system came to structure nearly every aspect of modern life, how we work, how we think about ourselves and others, and how we organize our politics.
In
Capitalism: A Global History
, Beckert reveals that capitalism was born global, corresponding at no point to an idealized dream of free markets; from the outset, state-backed institutions, imperial expansion, and coercion shaped its dynamics as much as innovation and exchange did. Along the way, capitalism has both expanded political voice for some and violently foreclosed it for others, entangled from its origins with slavery, colonialism, and profound inequality.
How do we distinguish between capitalism's capacity to generate genuine prosperity and its tendency to concentrate power in ways that undermine democratic institutions? What can nearly a thousand years of capitalist history teach us about the conditions under which economic systems support, rather than erode, democratic life? And as we confront what many call a crisis of late-stage capitalism, what possibilities remain for reimagining an economic order more compatible with democratic values?
Join one of the world's foremost historians of capitalism for an essential conversation about the deep entanglement of markets and democracy, and what history suggests about the road ahead.
Question and answer session and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this Event's Guests:
Sven Beckert
Sanjay Ruparelia
Read More:
Capitalism
Empire of Cotton
***
This event is part of our
On Civil Society
series, where we host local and international authors, activists and academics in conversation about the most critical topics of our time. Generously supported by the McConnell Foundation and also by Chris M. Reid.
***
About the series:
On the Frontlines of Democracy
is a public lecture series to analyze the trajectory of democracy in the twenty-first century.
In every region, the prospects of democracy face serious challenges, old and new. Can we protect constitutional rights and renew collective self-rule in an era of popular mistrust, severe partisanship and resurgent nationalism? Can they reduce inequalities of power, wealth and status, defend deep diversity and confront climate change in the new digital age? Can we develop innovative strategies to revitalize civic engagement, empower public institutions and resist autocratic threats? And what can we offer, learn and do to promote the prospects of democracy in our increasingly post-western global order?

location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your AI didn't need the internet at all: no subscription, no one recording what you type?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln

We'll compare a small local model against a powerful cloud model and plain search: what each gets right, what each costs, and what the privacy trade-offs really are. You'll leave with a decision sheet for your own hardware, an installation recipe, and an honest look at what "open" really means when it comes to AI.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

title: HPV and Cancer: What Everyone Should Know and What We Can Prevent
description:
Can HPV show up years after you were exposed? Does a positive HPV test mean cancer? Can you still benefit from vaccination as an adult?
Join Dr. Amanda Selk, obstetrician-gynaecologist at Women’s College Hospital and Professor at the University of Toronto, for an accessible conversation about HPV, a common virus that can affect people of all genders. Discover how HPV can cause cancer - and how vaccination, screening and the treatment of precancer can prevent disease. Dr. Selk will explain what has changed in Ontario and what it means for you and your family.
What to Expect:
Understanding HPV:
How it spreads, how it can remain undetectable for years, and why a positive test does not necessarily mean a recent infection
The Cancer Connection:
How HPV can lead to cervical and other cancers, and why prevention matters for people of all genders
Screening in Ontario:
Why HPV testing has replaced the Pap test for routine cervical screening, when to get screened, and who should discuss anal screening
Vaccination at Different Ages:
What we know about safety and effectiveness, why school-based vaccination matters, and who may benefit as an adult
The presentation will be followed by time for questions and discussion.
About the Presenter:
Dr. Amanda Selk is an obstetrician-gynaecologist at Women’s College Hospital and a Professor at the University of Toronto. She leads the Colposcopy Program at Women’s College Hospital and specializes in HPV-related disease, cervical cancer prevention and vulvar conditions. She is a past president of the Society of Canadian Colposcopists and serves on the board of the International Federation for Cancer Prevention and Colposcopy. An experienced clinician, researcher and educator, she helps patients and the public make informed decisions about their health.
About the Series
Bridging Minds: Health & Science Conversations is a partnership between the Toronto Public Library and Women’s College Hospital. Through monthly discussions led by experts from across different clinical areas and scientific disciplines, this series provides attendees with the opportunity to engage directly with our topics and speakers and empowers communities to navigate health and science topics confidently, inspiring a future of informed decision-making.
Learn more:
https://www.womenscollegehospital.ca/bridging-minds/

title: Rapp Lecture on Contemporary Art: Lotus L. Kang and Ebony L. Haynes (Free)
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
( WINNER of the 2026 Sobey Art Award )

*The Rapp Lecture on Contemporary Art features distinguished international leaders in the contemporary art world, including artists, curators, critics, and scholars. The program was established in 2009 in honour of Carol and Morton Rapp.*

***PLEASE reserve your own FREE ticket*** in advance at the AGO link below.

**Join artist Lotus L. Kang and curator Ebony L. Haynes as they discuss Kang’s multi-disciplinary creative practice. They’ll explore how Kang uses unstable and light-sensitive materials to consider the relationship between the body and its environments, and how Haynes’ groundbreaking work leading New York’s 52 Walker Gallery led to them working together.**

Lotus Kang is also short-listed for the upcoming Sobey Art Award. We'll visit her works at the National Gallery in Ottawa--on our upcoming trip.

https://www.gallery.ca/whats-on/sobey-art-award

**Lotus L. Kang** is a New York-based artist whose practice spans sculpture, photography, and site-responsive installation. Recent solo exhibitions include the Bvlgari Pavilion at the 61st Venice Biennale, Frye Art Museum, 52 Walker, and Chisenhale Gallery. Her work has also been featured in the Whitney Biennial, Shanghai Biennial, and New Museum Triennial, and is held in major museum collections including the Art Gallery of Ontario, Stedelijk Museum, Whitney Museum of American Art, The Guggenheim Museum, and Museum of Modern Art, New York.

3 mins intro..

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NK00tdA5Qas

**Ebony L. Haynes** is a New York-based curator and is the Global Head of Curatorial Projects at David Zwirner. She previously led the gallery’s 52 Walker space in Tribeca, NY. Haynes sits on the boards of Artists Space (New York), Topical Cream, and the New Art Dealers Alliance. She also runs Black Art Sessions: an online school that offers free professional practice classes to Black students worldwide.

**Reserve your own FREE ticket here:**

https://ago.ca/events/rapp-lecture-contemporary-art-lotus-l.-kang-and-ebony-l.-haynes

Note--this ticket gets you into the AGO (for FREE) from 6pm onwards.

title: Sedai Youth Creator Lab Showcase
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
For the past 2 years, the JCCC has been working on enhancing the accessibility of our Sedai Oral History Collection through long term preservation, outreach workshops on Oral History techniques and through activation of our existing interviews. The capstone project of this Japanese Canadian Legacies Society funded project is our Sedai Youth Creator Lab. Six youth have been working with three mentors and JCCC staff, to collect and edit oral histories in 3 amazing short documentaries. Join us on December 16, 2026 as we screen these documentaries for you for the first time. The evening will include 3 short documentaries and a panel discussion with our Youth and Mentors. A celebratory Reception will be held after the panel discussion. This evening event will be a celebration of both the work of our Sedai Youth Creator Lab and our larger Sedai Project as we wrap up this amazing grant work. We hope that you are able to join us as we celebrate this amazing project. When: December 16, 2026 Doors Open: 6:00pm Screenings will begin promptly at 7:00pm Where: Kobayashi Hall at the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre Registration is highly recommended. Register

title: The Delicious and Surprising History of The Dining Room: Author Talk with John Ota
location: Deer Park, Room 204
description:
John Ota presents​ and discusses his book
The Dining Room
.
Explore the stories behind twelve iconic dining rooms in homes around the world—from a Japanese samurai house to Claude Monet's brilliant yellow dining room to Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul to Jackie Kennedy’s White House—and travel through time in pursuit of the ultimate design.​
The Dining Room is an enlightening and joyous celebration of history, culture and the art of dining. Presenter John Ota's charming observations of the surprising impact of dining rooms on our lives and the cherished moments we share within them will delight armchair travelers, history fanatics and interior design enthusiasts alike.
John Ota has been involved with architecture and design since 1978, with degrees from Columbia University, the University of Toronto and the University of British Columbia. His bestselling book
The Kitchen
was a 2021 Taste Canada Awards finalist and a 2021 Paris Gourmand Cookbook finalist in the book design category. After working in architecture in Toronto, New York, and Vancouver, and as lead on multiple Ontario Ministry of Culture projects, John now loves to travel the world visiting historic houses, cooking regional food, and meeting people of all backgrounds.

description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: How Do AIs "Think"? And Why They Get Things Wrong
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
How does a machine actually "think"? Explore the history and latest developments of machine learning.
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, we'll dig into what's really going on inside AI systems: how they decide what matters in your question, where their training data comes from (and who's missing from it), and how hidden instructions can sneak into content and hijack an AI. Develop an intuitive understanding of how AIs "think" without the math. We'll talk about how AIs remember, how they don't and how they are both similar and different to humans. And we'll ask the question underneath it all: is there anyone home inside the machine?
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.
Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle.

title: Coding with Python II
location: Highland Creek, Program Room
description:
Python is an open source programming language that is used for creating web applications, web content, mathematics and system scripting. In this second Python session we will leverage everything we learned about loops and blocks in part one to create our very own functions. We'll take a look at how to approach function design, how to allow users to enter data into functions through arguments, and how to get our functions to return results. We will also introduce some new data structures which, unlike variables, can hold more than one piece of data at a time.
This class is for beginners but assumes you have a basic understanding of Python or have attended Coding with Python I.
Registration will start 2 weeks before this class. Computers will be provided.

Georges Som
, médiateur culturel, nous essayerons de comprendre les enjeux de ces scènes, de découvrir leurs sens et de partager nos sentiments sur leurs auteurs et autrices. En attendant Godot
de Samuel Beckett. Deux vagabonds, Vladimir et Estragon, se retrouvent sur une route de campagne, près d'un arbre, à la tombée de la nuit. Est-ce bien le jour et l'heure pour attendre Godot. Arrivent Pozzo, un homme autoritaire, le propriétaire des lieux, avec un Knouk, un sous homme tenu en laisse.

title: Internet Horror Classics on Film: Backrooms
description:
In this final instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series Internet Horror Classics on Film, actor Erin Mick and critic Michael LaPointe join host Adam Nayman to discuss Kane Parsons' debut film, Backrooms, which bends the liminal spaces that have haunted the internet for years into a mesmerizing horror film.
About this event's guests:
Erin Mick
is an actor and writer based in Toronto. Her doctoral research centers on contemporary horror cinema, with particular interest in emergent modes of fan/viewer engagement, as well as horror's relationship to and mobilization of notions of trauma and collective memory. Erin also works as an actor, and is a writer of horror fiction.
Michael LaPointe
is a novelist, critic, journalist and producer in Toronto, Canada. He has published a novel with Random House Canada, written for The New Yorker, The Atlantic, and The Paris Review, and produced series for BBC Radio 4. He is a regular contributor to the Times Literary Supplement. His second novel, Ruby Red, will be released in spring 2027.
Adam Nayman
is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. He is a regular contributor to The Ringer, a lecturer at the University of Toronto's Cinema Studies Institute, and he has written on film for The New Yorker and The New York Times.
Read more:
The Creep

Become a page-turner by joining the Between the Lines Book Club! Here, we embark on a new chapter with every read, diving into a world of endless possibilities. From gripping thrillers to heartwarming coming-of-age tales, or a sprinkle of fantasy adventures, there's something for everyone. Whether you're a die-hard fan of one genre or love mixing things up, you'll find a place here to discuss, share, and connect with fellow readers. Friday November 16: A Gentleman in Moscow by Amor Towles
Set in Moscow in 1922,
A Gentleman in Moscow
by Amor Towles follows Count Alexander Rostov, a refined Russian aristocrat sentenced by a Bolshevik tribunal to house arrest in the grand Metropol Hotel, where he must spend the rest of his life confined within its walls. As the world outside undergoes dramatic political and social change, the Count gradually transforms his restricted circumstances into a life rich with unexpected friendships, meaningful encounters, and quiet adventures. From navigating the hotel's intricate social world to forming a particularly meaningful bond with a young girl named Nina, Rostov discovers new perspectives on love, loyalty, personal growth, and the passage of time. Elegant, witty, and deeply moving, the novel explores the nature of freedom, the importance of human connection, and the possibility of finding purpose and beauty even when life takes an unexpected turn.

The purpose of this event is to meet up to play heavier / longer board games, and have fun while doing it! We will start off small and if there is sufficient interest we will add capacity for future events.

You are welcome to bring your own games to the event, or use the games in the library at the location.

**Scheduling details:**
\- If you have a specific game that you would like to post for\, feel free to do so in comments\. In your post\, include the name of the game\, number of players needed for the game\, whether you are offering a teach or not\, and the start time \(please try to start before noon if possible\)\.
\- If you would like to join a specific game that has already been posted\, feel free to comment on it confirming your participation\. Make sure you have noted the details posted by the host\.
\- You are of course also welcome to organize / join games onsite on the day itself\, assuming sufficient players / tables are available

**Rules around COVID:**
\- Given this is a public event\, we respectfully ask that only i\) fully vaccinated individuals\, and ii\) those not exhibiting any COVID symptoms\, participate\. This requirement may change in the future based on provincial guidelines and group requirements

**Available Amenities:**
\- Food and drinks are available on\-site\, you can see a detailed menu [here](https://theguildhouse.ca/pages/menu). **Outside food and drinks are not allowed by the Guild House.**
\- There is an on\-site game library\, and use of it is covered within the admission fee\.

**Admission Fee:**
\- There is a $10 fee charged by the establishment for use of space\. Payments are to be made directly to the establishment at the time of entry and not to the organizer

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

title: Winter Solstice Night Hike
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**This adventure is sold out. Please [join the waitlist on our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/solstice-night-hike)**
**This adventure is exclusive to Explorer members.**
**The longest nights of the year are a good time to experience a true adventure.**
We’ll start after dark at the main lot and head out on the Beaver Dam Trail, then link into sections of the Bruce Trail and the Hilton Falls Side Trail. It’s a full 21km, half marathon distance, so it suits people who are comfortable moving at a steady pace for hours in the cold.
Everyone hikes by headlamp. Somewhere along the route we’ll find a quiet stretch, switch them all off, and give our eyes a few minutes to adjust. If the sky cooperates, there will be stars. If it doesn’t, you still get the silence of a winter forest at night.
We’ll also pass the falls and the old mill ruins on the way through. Bring a thermos, dress for standing still as well as moving, and expect to finish tired, cold-cheeked and very awake.
Check the trip plan for the details, including the meeting point, gear list, and timing for the day.
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Hiking After Dark:** Your view shrinks to the beam of your headlamp, and you hear more than you see. It’s the same trail we hike by day, covered at night.
**Half Marathon Distance:** 21km with 201 m of elevation gain, in winter conditions and by headlamp.
**Headlamps Off:** A planned stop where the whole group switches off and waits for our eyes to adjust. Weather permitting, it’s the best chance on the route to see stars.
**Itinerary**
**21:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**22:00** \- Arrive at the trailhead
**22:00 - 06:30** \- Hike trail overnight
**06:30 - 07:30** \- Drive back to Toronto
**Event cost: $60+HST. $40 optional transport also available. Join the waitlist [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/solstice-night-hike)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Mission of Gravity - Hal Clement
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi everybody,

Back for another team investigating an alien planet. This time we have a true classic, Hal Clement's seminal 1954 gritty sci fi novel, *Missions of Gravity*. This one has been on the list for a while and I'm so glad it was on theme enough to get on the survey.

Book of the Month
*Mission of Gravity* \- Hal Clement \(1954\)

From a good review on Skiffy.ca, "Originally serialized in 1953 in the magazine *[Astounding Science Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analog_Science_Fiction_and_Fact)*, the tale was published in book form the following year. Decades later, it was awarded a [Retro Hugo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Award#Retro_Hugos), for excellence in SF’s pioneering era.

*Mission of Gravity* is an archetypal example of what the kids call “hard science fiction”, a subgenre in which the characters within the SF story solve physical problems with physical –largely technological– means. The science tends to be solid, even the speculative science, and the rules are intensely consistent within the boundaries of the story."

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

title: Virtual: The Nutcracker from The National Ballet of Japan (Tokyo)
description:
Experience Toronto
On **Sunday December 20th,** **see The Nutcracker from The National Ballet of Japan in Tokyo.** On Christmas Eve, Clara receives a mysterious Nutcracker from her godfather Drosselmeyer and is drawn into a magical world filled with toy soldiers, giant mice and enchanting adventures. After bravely helping the Nutcracker during a fantastical battle, Clara journeys with him to the Kingdom of Sweets, where she is celebrated with dazzling dances. But was Clara’s magical adventure only a dream, or was there something real behind the mystery of the Nutcracker Prince?

*The Nutcracker* was composed by Tchaikovsky in 1892 for the Mariinsky Theatre in St Petersburg. The ballet is based on a story inspired by E.T.A. Hoffmann’s *The Nutcracker and the Mouse King*, later adapted into a lighter version by Alexandre Dumas. For their 2025/2026 season, The National Ballet of Japan has asked the award-winning English choreographer Will Tuckett to create an original new production of Tchaikovsky’s much loved ballet. Together with the creative team of widely recognised artists including the designer Colin Richmond, his Nutcracker is full of the authentic beauty of classical ballet in a sweet and colourful world full of humour - a joy at any time of year.

**COST**
Free

🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

📩 **CONTACT:** Terry (Organizer)
💸 **E-transfer:** [tmg8@wealthsimple.me](mailto:tmg8@wealthsimple.me)

🔗 **Stay Connected & Join Us:**

📸 Instagram: [https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel](https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel)

📅 Meetup: [https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel)

💬 WhatsApp Group Chat: [https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7](https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7)

📘 Facebook: [https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel](https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel)

👉 **See what’s coming up and RSVP on our calendar:**
[https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar)

🛡️ **Community Guidelines:**
Toronto Babel is a welcoming, inclusive, and safe space for everyone. Our events focus on language exchange, cultural sharing, and friendship — **not for dating or matchmaking.** Harassment and inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated. If you experience or witness anything concerning, please let an organizer know so we can help.

Come for the conversations, stay for the community! 🌎💬❤️

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs. 
Register in advance for this meeting:
Meeting Registration – Zoom

Please use the map provided on the event page also.

title: Pet Shop Boys - a Toronto Tribute Day
location: Cat's Cradle Sports and Spirits, 1245 St Clair Ave W, Toronto, ON M6E 1B8, Canada
description:
We'll run through ALL the bigs hit a in a crazy fun-filled two hours! SATURDAY / Boxing Day.

Early show - 3pm! FREE.


Immerse yourself in the BIG SCREEN / BIG SOUND fun + join a whole pub full of other Pet Shop Boys fans! FANTASTIC food and drink specials.


PET SHOPS BOYS VIDEO TRIBUTE DAY – BOXING DAY IN TORONTO!

Boxing Day just got legendary!


VIDEO SONG LIST:



Top 15 Pet Shop Boys Songs (by popularity/streams + chart success)

  1. West End Girls (1985/86) — Their breakthrough; UK #1 and US #1. Iconic synth-pop with hip-hop and literary influences.
  2. Always on My Mind (1987) — Cover of the Elvis classic that became their Christmas #1 in the UK.
  3. It’s a Sin (1987) — UK #1; dramatic, theatrical anthem about guilt and Catholic upbringing.
  4. Go West (1993) — Village People cover; UK #2. Anthemic and frequently used in sports contexts.
  5. Domino Dancing (1988) — Latin-tinged dance-pop; UK #7. Marked the end of their early “imperial phase” of #1s.
  6. What Have I Done to Deserve This? (with Dusty Springfield) (1987) — UK #2; classic duet.
  7. New York City Boy (1999) — UK #14; later-period disco-pop hit.

 14. Left to My Own Devices (1988) — UK #4; orchestral, camp, and self-reflective.

title: Water Marbling Bookmarks Workshop
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Immerse yourself in the mesmerizing world of water marbling — an ancient technique of floating pigments on water and transferring them onto paper to create intricate, fluid designs.

Practiced for centuries across the Islamic world, particularly in regions such as Türkiye, Iran, and the Indian subcontinent, water marbling has been used to adorn calligraphy, manuscripts, and decorative papers. In this introductory workshop, you will explore its rich history and cultural significance while mastering traditional tools and methods to produce a variety of classic patterns. Guided step-by-step, you will create between five and eight unique marbled bookmarks to take home — each a one-of-a-kind reflection of colour, movement, and your own creative expression.

title: Festival Select: Sorcerer (William Friedkin, 1977)
location: North York Central Library, Room 101
description:
Join the Society and Recreation department of the North York Central Library for monthly screenings of fiction and non-fiction films that push the boundaries of the medium. This month we are showing William Friedkin's
Sorcerer
(1977).
Synopsis (The Criterion Collection): A hallucinatory journey into the heart of darkness, William Friedkin’s pulse-pounding reimagining of the suspense classic
The Wages of Fear
was dismissed upon its release, only to be recognized decades later as one of the New Hollywood’s boldest auteur statements. In a remote Latin American village, four desperate fugitives—a New Jersey gangster (Roy Scheider), a Mexican assassin (Francisco Rabal), an unscrupulous Parisian businessman (Bruno Cremer), and an Arab terrorist (Amidou)—take on a doomed mission: transporting two trucks full of highly explosive nitroglycerin through the treacherous jungle. Aided by Tangerine Dream’s otherworldly synth score, Friedkin turns each bump in the road into a tour de force of cold-sweat tension—conjuring a hauntingly nihilistic vision of a world ruled by chance and fate.
No registration required.

title: Screen Scaries: Black Christmas, Bob Clark (1974)
location: Lillian H. Smith, B/C
description:
Get your spook on with this month's scary movie screening of
Black Christmas
(1974), directed by Bob Clark.
A prototype of the American slasher,
Black Christmas
wears its Giallo influences on its sleeve and sets a blueprint for genre films like John Carpenter's
Halloween
(1977). Shot in Toronto, the film follows a group of sorority girls over their winter break as they are harassed by a series of disturbing phone calls.
Black Christmas
has a running time of 1 hour and 37 minutes, and is rated R.
There will be a short introduction to the film followed by the screening, which will be accompanied by closed captions.
The next Screen Scaries will be:

Ring
(1998, Japan) Hideo Nakata. Runtime: 1h35m; Rating: PG

title: The Birth of Modern Forensics – 1910-1940
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, 1st floor
description:
​The Birth of Modern Forensics explores the science of early-twentieth-century forensics, how it changed and expanded. It explores the social context in which these changes occurred. Not every law enforcement agent welcomed the presence of interlopers, of the fame they received for “solving” a crime. The success and perseverance on the part of the first forensic scientists ushered in a new era and changed criminal investigations forever.
This program is being presented by Kerry Cathers, author of
A Writer's Guide to Nineteenth-century Murder by Arsenic
, who runs research resource websites
A Curiosity of Crime
and
Bandit’s Roost
for authors of historical detective fiction (1800-1940)
Registration is encouraged, and we welcome drop-in customers until capacity is reached.

Learn how patterns and motifs have been used for centuries across the Islamic world, and experiment with tools and textures to bring your vision to life. You’ll leave with a one-of-a-kind creation that blends traditional inspiration with your own creativity.

description:

Working with copper, participants will learn simple yet effective techniques to shape and decorate metal surfaces. Guided by our Museum Educators, you’ll design and create your own embossed bookmark, exploring how artists across the Islamic world have transformed metal into objects of both beauty and function for centuries.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: DAYDREAMS NYE
location: The Jama, 961 College St, Toronto, ON M6H 1A6, Canada
description:
DAYDREAMS returns this New Year’s Eve, bringing together Chicago’s Mark Grusane and hometown hero DJ Dirty Dale for a night where music leads, time disappears, and the dreams we’ve carried become the world we create.

MARK GRUSANE (Chicago)

A Chicago treasure whose relationship with the dancefloor stretches back to the ‘80s, Mark Grusane is a lifelong digger, producer, and co-founder of the legendary Mr. Peabody Records. With an encyclopedic knowledge of house, disco, and the musical worlds beyond, Mark has a rare instinct for what makes people move. His selections weave together obscure discoveries, timeless grooves, and unexpected diversions, creating deeply emotional journeys guided by a lifetime of musical curiosity and passion.

DIRTY DALE (Toronto)

A fixture in Toronto’s underground house community for over 25 years, Dirty Dale brings a dancer’s sensibility and a deep love for the groove to everything he plays. Rooted in the city’s soulful house tradition, his sound moves through deep, jazzy, Afro-influenced, and disco rhythms, blending forgotten gems with contemporary cuts. His selections reflect a lifetime spent on both sides of the decks and an enduring devotion to the dancefloor.

DAYDREAMS

There’s something so beautiful about a room full of people surrendering to the same rhythm. Strangers become friends, time slips away, and for a few hours, nothing matters but the music and the people sharing it.

Come dance and daydream with us as we conjure a future rooted in harmony, soulful connection, and the profound power of love. 💫✨❤️

title: Water Marbling Bookmarks Workshop
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Immerse yourself in the mesmerizing world of water marbling — an ancient technique of floating pigments on water and transferring them onto paper to create intricate, fluid designs.

Practiced for centuries across the Islamic world, particularly in regions such as Türkiye, Iran, and the Indian subcontinent, water marbling has been used to adorn calligraphy, manuscripts, and decorative papers. In this introductory workshop, you will explore its rich history and cultural significance while mastering traditional tools and methods to produce a variety of classic patterns. Guided step-by-step, you will create between five and eight unique marbled bookmarks to take home — each a one-of-a-kind reflection of colour, movement, and your own creative expression.

description:

title: Clayming Love
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:

Events
	







	

	

	


				







	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Monday January 4, 2027
6:00 pm – 8:00 pm
 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    For ages 18+ 
Are you ready? Are you open? Are you willing? 
“The awareness in our hands is alive and continuous. The feeling of our lives will be awake in our fingers. We befriend the clay. The clay befriends us.” — M.C. Richards 
The sense of touch cannot happen anywhere but the here and now. Touch is immediate. Through exploration with clay we will recognize how we can be stuck because we have not looked deeply enough into the nature of our experience. 
Guided by a Zen Buddhist practitioner and registered art therapist, engage in clay exercises designed to call attention to habits of belief, judgments, and the stories we tell ourselves. With self-compassion, we will create possibilities to loosen their hold on us by working with the malleability of clay. 
At the end of the workshop we return the clay to its original form, letting go of what was created and ready to begin anew. 
This workshop welcomes everyone, whether you are new to or familiar with clay, breath, and presence.

                    Suzanne Thomson is ceramic artist, registered psychotherapist, and art therapist with over 30 years of experience integrating these practices to facilitate healing, community building and social transformation work. As a practitioner of Zen Buddhism with training in contemplative arts, sensorimotor psychotherapy, narrative therapy, and trauma-informed approaches she offers psychotherapy, clinical supervision, and has taught at the Toronto Art Therapy Institute and the University of Toronto. title: Adult Afternoon Movie - Nouvelle Vague (2025)
location: Riverdale, Program  Room 1
description:
It's 1959, a young Jean-Luc Godard (Guillaume Marbeck) is the only one among his film-critic peers at Cahiers du cinéma not to have made a feature film. Determined to put his revolutionary cinematic ideas into practice, he brings his small crew and two stars an eager unknown named Jean-Paul Belmondo (Aubry Dullin) and wary Hollywood expat Jean Seberg (Zoey Deutch) onto the streets of Paris to shoot Breathless, an adventure in unfettered creativity that would soon upend the way movies are made. title: ABCD Reads American Hagwon by Min Jin Lee
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads [American Hagwon](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4792135) by Min Jin Lee (author of [Pachinko](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C3448477))
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/6718256866656256) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"In schools and churches, hotel rooms and nail salons, law firms and fried-fish shops; in cramped, dingy apartments and luxury, gated communities, the men, women, and children in American Hagwon struggle to find satisfaction and meaning in a world that seems to grow less forgiving with each passing year. Once comfortably middle class in Korea, John and Helen Koh and their three children, Bo, DH, and Mido, find their lives upended, first by a shocking betrayal by John's oldest friend, then by the 1997 Asian financial crisis." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/american-hagwon/))

"At last, the National Book Award finalist and NYT bestselling author of Pachinko returns with a breathtaking contemporary epic: Min Jin Lee has written a masterpiece by turns sweeping and intimate, one that reckons with ambition and moderation, lust and loyalty, personal dreams and familial duty." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/245886309-american-hagwon))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

description:
TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Floral Design Program: Classic Design Fundamentals 2
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
In this follow-up to Classic Design Fundamentals 1, you will enrich your understanding of traditional design.
Enrich your understanding of traditional design, a style which is used in contemporary settings with sophistication. You will gain deeper knowledge of both plant material and design. You will learn colour theory: the importance of colour and how to create different colour harmonies. You will explore the concept and importance of asymmetry in a design and how this can be used to great effect. Discover a new design style each week: a hand-tied bouquet, a vertical line design, a Hogarth Curve and an asymmetrical mass design.
 
Course fees do not include flowers or supplies. Students are encouraged to find a local flower shop or grocery store to purchase their flowers. A materials list will be emailed prior to the start of each class.
 
Learn more about our Certificate in Floral Design
 
Prerequisites: Classic Design Fundamentals 1.
 
Thursday, January 7, 14, 27 and 28, 6 to 9 p.m.
Public $245, Members $195 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Margaret Betts
Marg Betts is a floral design judge with accreditation to judge and instruct the craft. Her passions are gardening, plants and her love for creating floral artistry. She is a recent past President of the Garden Club of Toronto and has also been the Chair of the Toronto Flower Show at Canada Blooms.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program, please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.

title: Launch Your Career Plan for MASc, PhD, and PDFs
location: Galbraith Building – GB202 @ 35 St. George Street, Toronto, ON
description:
Launch Your Career Plan is an initiative by the Institute for Studies in Transdisciplinary Engineering Education & Practice (ISTEP) to support MASc and PhD students and Postdocs to launch their career planning early in their studies. This event will guide you to critically reflect on career opportunities and equip you with strategies and tools to explore your unique career aspirations. You will leave this event with tailored resources to dive deeper into the specific career pathways that interest you.   
At this event, you will:   

Learn about parallel planning for further graduate studies, academia, and industry careers  


Use labour market data and networking tools to discover diverse academic and industry opportunities  


Listen to a panel of alumni who have completed further graduate studies, are working in industry, or obtained a professorship  


Create a plan to explore your specific career aspirations  

This event is open to all MASc, PhDs and PDFs. We welcome students who have a clear idea of their career trajectory as well as those who are exploring their next career move. It is highly recommended that all MASc, PhDs, and PDFs students attend this event near the beginning of their studies or postdoc journey.

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: On Tyranny & On Freedom
location: Toronto Reference Library, Discussion Room, 3rd Floor
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
January's books are
On Tyranny: Twenty Lessons From the Twentieth Century
and
On Freedom
by historian Timothy Snyder. Copies of the books are available in print, eBook and eAudiobook format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"In
On Tyranny
,
Holocaust historian Timothy Snyder draws from the darkest hours of the twentieth century--the rise of Hitler and Stalin--to provide hope for the twenty-first. As he writes, "Americans are no wiser than the Europeans who saw democracy yield to fascism, Nazism and communism. Our one advantage is that we might learn from their experience."
In
On Freedom,
Snyder argues that "we have lost sight of what Freedom mean, and this is leading us into crisis. Too many of us look at freedom as the absence of state power: We think we’re free if we can do and say as we please, and protect ourselves from government overreach. But true freedom isn’t so much freedom from as freedom to—the freedom to thrive, to take risks for futures we choose by working together. Freedom is the value that makes all other values possible."
Drop in. No registration required.

title: Applied Qualitative Research: A Practical Guide for Graduate Student Researchers
location: Live on Zoom @ Zoom
description:
Are you interested in gaining an understanding of how to design, conduct, and present applied qualitative research? If so, these online workshops are for you! While this series is particularly intended for graduate students, FGS additionally invites and warmly welcomes graduate faculty including supervisors and committee members, as well as research staff, and postdocs. Feel free to come to one, two or all of them! Workshops will be delivered virtually and will be recorded. Registration is required.
Facilitated by Dr. Karen Campbell, RN, PhD ( https://www.linkedin.com/in/kcamp232/?originalSubdomain=ca ), Assistant Professor, School of Nursing, York University. Dr. Campbell’s program of research focuses on the intersections of women’s health with physical and social geography. She has taught graduate-level courses in qualitative research and designed and conducted multiple applied qualitative research projects using a broad range of study designs and approaches to analysis.
Hosted by Associate Dean, Academic, Dr. Cheryl van Daalen-Smith, RN, PhD
Webinar One: A Guide to Applied Qualitative Research
This webinar provides graduate students, supervisors, and researchers with a practical foundation in applied qualitative research. Participants will explore key qualitative methodologies, research design considerations, data collection strategies, and approaches to generating rigorous and meaningful findings.
When: Tuesday, January 12, 2027 from 11:00 a.m.-12:15 p.m.
Location: Zoom
*Registration is required | RSVP Link
Webinar Two: Coding Qualitative Data
This webinar introduces the principles and practices of qualitative data coding, from developing initial codes to identifying patterns and themes. Through practical examples, participants will learn strategies for organizing, analyzing, and interpreting qualitative data in a systematic and transparent manner.
When: Tuesday, February 9, 2027 from 11:00 a.m.-12:15 p.m.
Location: Zoom
*Registration is required | RSVP Link
Webinar Three: Generative AI in Qualitative Data Analysis 
This webinar examines the emerging role of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in qualitative research and data analysis. Participants will explore opportunities, limitations, ethical considerations, and practical applications of GenAI tools to support coding, theme development, data synthesis, and research productivity while maintaining methodological rigor.
When: Tuesday, March 9, 2027 from 11:00 a.m.-12:15 p.m.
Location: Zoom
*Registration is required | RSVP Link

About David Leopold
Sifu David Leopold has been practicing, studying, researching and teaching martial and healing arts since 1994.
In 1999, Sifu David achieved his black belt in Shaolin Kung Fu. Since 1999, Sifu David has received numerous certifications in Tachi and weapon forms, and seven Qigong routines. In 2009, Sifu David received his Usui Reiki master certification from the Naturopathic School of Medicine in Toronto.
In 2012, Sifu David travelled to China to compete in the International Wushi Competition in Shanghai. He brought home two gold and a bronze medal.
By combining all these modalities and experiences, Sifu David brings a unique style of teaching that includes technique, philosophy and practicality. Sifu David’s approach to teaching is relaxed and he believes tai chi and qigong practice should be useful in everyday life and enjoyable to do.
Sifu David has a passion for martial and healing arts. His holistic approach to wellness includes physical, emotional, spiritual and nutritional well-being. Sifu David continues to improve his skills as a practitioner, teacher/mentor, and he hopes to teach for the rest of his life.
Sifu David’s words of wisdom:
“To be a master of what you do, you must first be a master unto yourself.”

title: Jan 14 - MCP, Agents and Skills Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Jan 14, 2027
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/mcp-agents-skills-meetup-january-14-2027)**

**From Demo to Production: Testing, Scaling and Securing AI Agents with Spring AI**

Your agent works perfectly in the demo. Then in production it gives a wrong answer and nobody can tell why, token costs spike, it slows to a crawl under load, and it calls a tool the user was never allowed to use. Building an agent is the easy part; the real work is running it like any other production service: tested, observable, scalable and secure.

Spring AI lets you do that with the Spring idioms and tooling you already know. This code-first session grows one example step by step. We start with a simple ChatClient, add advisors, memory and RAG, comparing the options Spring AI offers for each, and then let the agent act through tool calling and MCP.

Then come the production questions:

* Testing: we catch regressions with LLM-as-judge evaluators and typed decision models like Jev for fast, cheap verdicts.
* Observability: we add Micrometer traces, logs and token usage across model and tool calls.
* Scaling: we compare options for handling more concurrent users, from self-hosting to a managed runtime such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
* Security: we use Spring Security to authenticate users and make sure only the MCP tools they're allowed to use ever get called. You'll leave with reusable Spring patterns for agents that reason and act, and the discipline to test, observe, scale and secure them in production.

*About the Speaker*

[Andrei Shakirin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andrei-shakirin/) is a Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services and a former Pivotal Labs engineer, specializing in the design of highly scalable systems and generative AI applications. He is an active committer to several Spring and Apache open-source projects, contributor into MCP java SDK and a regular speaker at technical conferences.

**From Model Evals to System Evals: Evaluating Agents, Harnesses, and the Evaluators Themselves**

Every team shipping agents is quietly standing up two systems: the agent harness that plans, retrieves, calls tools, and edits code — and the evaluation harness that decides whether any of it can be trusted. Most teams only evaluate the first one's final output.

That is not enough. An agent can produce a correct answer through an unreliable, wasteful, or out-of-policy execution path, and outcome-only checks will pass it. This talk argues for evaluating the whole agent system: execution trajectories — tool correctness, evidence and grounding, state handling, policy compliance, and efficiency — alongside final outcomes, using deterministic specification checks an agent cannot game, model-based judges, and human-calibrated benchmarks.

We separate capability evaluations from regression evaluations so harness or model changes can be gated in CI. Then we turn the lens around: the evaluators themselves need evaluating — LLM judge calibration, disagreement analysis, and where human review still belongs.

Attendees leave with a production checklist for gating agent, model, and harness changes on system-level evidence instead of final answers.

*About the Speaker*

[Dipen Chawla](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dipen-chawla-bb4a49bb/) is an AI engineer and researcher working on agentic AI systems and their evaluation, including agent memory and clinical diagnostic reasoning work at Microsoft, and data platform engineering at Walmart and S&P Global.

**Leading an Army of AI Agents**

Our AI coding agents now pick up tasks, follow team playbooks, open pull requests and wait for review. This firsthand engineering case study follows more than ten agents running in parallel and shows how briefs, shared context and verification loops keep their work reviewable.
It covers the failure modes too: confident wrong turns, incomplete verification, review bottlenecks and the attention required from human leaders.
Attendees will learn a practical task-to-PR workflow, how to make trust conditional on evidence, and which measures expose the costs hidden by faster output. The focus is on agent workflow and operating discipline, with concrete engineering examples rather than a product pitch.

*About the Speaker*

[John Adib](https://www.linkedin.com/in/MrAdib) is a London-based engineering manager at Zapp, a former CTO and two-time founder with 18+ years of software experience.

Agents in Action: Putting AI Agents to Work on Visual AI Data

What should an AI agent remember, and what should it forget? In this talk, we’ll explore the Voxel51 agent through the lens of memory, examining how retaining the right context and incorporating feedback can help agents improve over time. Through examples from visual AI workflows, we’ll discuss what’s worth remembering, from dataset context and user preferences to corrections and successful approaches, and when to update or discard information that becomes outdated. We’ll also explore how feedback and evaluation can help us determine whether an agent is making better decisions, offering practical insights for building agents that become more useful with experience.

*About the Speaker*

[Adonai Vera](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adonai-vera/) is a Machine Learning Engineer and DevRel at Voxel51 with over 7 years of experience building computer vision and machine learning models using TensorFlow, Docker, and OpenCV.
