title: Botanical Printed Notebook and Prints
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of creating a customized notebook and prints!
Using the process of linocut, you’ll create a custom printed Japanese notebook and 4 fine art prints. From designing your image, through to carving and printing, our instructor will demonstrate linocut techniques and provide individual guidance. By the end of the workshop you’ll leave with 1 unique botanical-themed notebook, 4 original prints and new printmaking skills. Beginners welcome.
 
You can create anything, so please bring photos, sketches and designs for reference and inspiration. Your image needs to measure 4×6 inches. If you’re stuck for ideas, pressed leaves will be available.
 
Making art can be messy, please wear old clothes or an apron. Materials included.
 
Each student will receive:
 


1 Japanese notebook
1 block of soft-cut lino
4 sheets of toned art paper
Black printmaking ink


Saturday, January 16, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $80, TBG Members $70 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine-inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: 藍 ai - A life of creativity in Indigo by Sachiko Watanabe Opening Reception
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Artist Talk Sachiko Watanabe will share the story of ai (indigo), from growing plants to making dye material, demonstrating the traditional tools and techniques used to transform indigo plants into dye. Through her artwork and personal experiences, she will discuss the various indigo dyeing methods, her deep connection with nature, her lifestyle and the role that love and care play in her creative practice. The presentation will include: An introduction to the cultivation of indigo, the preparation of natural dye, and the artistic process behind her work. A video presentation showcasing her life, practice and creative journey. A Q&A session with the audience. Exhibition info Artist bio: Sachiko Watanabe (渡辺幸子) was born in 1977 in Ehime Prefecture, Japan. After studying textile design at Musashino Art University in Tokyo, she encountered natural indigo dye at the Iyo Kasuri Centre in Ehime. This encounter marked the beginning of a practice that has continued for more than 20 years. Sachiko later moved to Onomichi, Hiroshima, where she developed her work with indigo. Today, she grows her own indigo plants on Mukaishima, an island off the coast of Onomichi. She combines her harvest with sukumo, traditionally fermented indigo leaves from Tokushima Prefecture, to create her own natural dye. Living in a traditional Japanese house, where she also exhibits and sells her work, Sachiko continues to work closely with indigo each day. Through her textiles, she hopes to share its quiet beauty and to remind us of the natural world that surrounds and embraces us. Her exhibitions include Indigo in Our Daily Lives (2019), Indigo, Simultaneously (2021), Indigo in Winter (2021), Indigo in Darkness (2022), and Intaking Indigo (2024) Photo: © Toshinori Tanaka

title: 藍 ai - A life of creativity in Indigo by Sachiko Watanabe
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
For over twenty years, Sachiko Watanabe has lived with indigo — growing it, fermenting it, dyeing with it, and shaping her days around its rhythms. Traveling from her home in Japan, she brings this quiet, deeply personal practice to the JCCC for the first time. Rooted in one of Japan's oldest natural dyeing traditions, natural indigo sukumo fermentation, this exhibition invites you to slow down and step into her world — to see, touch, and feel the colour of a life shaped by patience, land, and time. Join us in welcoming her to Toronto. About the Exhibition The exhibition follows the full life cycle of indigo — from seed to sukumo, from vat to fabric, from field to everyday life. Visitors will encounter: The Making of Sukumo — a year-long journey through sowing, transplanting, harvesting, drying, and fermenting indigo leaves Shades of Indigo — a study of the many named hues within the indigo spectrum, from pale aijiro(藍白) to deep kachi-iro(搗色) Textiles & Objects — a curated collection of dyed khadi, cotton, linen, hemp, and wool pieces, shaped by Sachiko's hand Everyday Indigo — an invitation to touch, smell, and wrap yourself in indigo cloth Living with Indigo — a reflection on more than twelve years spent in an old farmhouse, where growing, fermenting, and dyeing indigo have become inseparable from daily life Opening Reception & Artist Talk Please join us on January 16 at 2pm More Info Workshops Details coming soon! Artist bio: Sachiko Watanabe (渡辺幸子) was born in 1977 in Ehime Prefecture, Japan. After studying textile design at Musashino Art University in Tokyo, she encountered natural indigo dye at the Iyo Kasuri Centre in Ehime. This encounter marked the beginning of a practice that has continued for more than 20 years. Sachiko later moved to Onomichi, Hiroshima, where she developed her work with indigo. Today, she grows her own indigo plants on Mukaishima, an island off the coast of Onomichi. She combines her harvest with sukumo, traditionally fermented indigo leaves from Tokushima Prefecture, to create her own natural dye. Living in a traditional Japanese house, where she also exhibits and sells her work, Sachiko continues to work closely with indigo each day. Through her textiles, she hopes to share its quiet beauty and to remind us of the natural world that surrounds and embraces us. title: ABCD Reads The End of Everything by M. John Harrison
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads [The End of Everything](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4802129) by M. John Harrison, winner of the [2026 Booker Prize](https://thebookerprizes.com/the-booker-library/prize-years/2026).

([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/6285142977675264) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"Phillip Tennent makes his living at the tideline, collecting artifacts that wash up from the Channel. It's been years since the crisis changed everything, but its exact nature remains obscure. Government barely functions, the seas are full of new creatures, an entire continent has been mislaid. It feels like the end. Now Phillip has fished out of the water an object he can't keep. A creature that keeps changing. An artifact he must take inland, before it destroys everything he thinks he knows." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/the-end-of-everything/))

"The End of Everything is a slyly satirical and unsettling post-apocalyptic adventure into the limits of human understanding from the peerless master of contemporary fiction." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/245886309-american-hagwon))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Ethical Research Decision-Making: Building Professional Judgment Across Career Paths
location: Live on Zoom @ Zoom
description:
This workshop is designed for graduate students and postdoctoral scholars who want to strengthen their ability to navigate ethical challenges in research and professional practice. While responsible conduct of research is often presented through policies and regulations, researchers frequently encounter situations where the “right” course of action is not immediately clear. These complex scenarios require thoughtful judgment, critical reflection, and the ability to articulate and defend ethical decisions.
By the end of the workshop, participants will have greater confidence in navigating ethically challenging situations and a stronger foundation for responsible leadership in research and professional environments. The skills developed are relevant across disciplines and career paths, supporting participants in becoming thoughtful, reflective, and ethically grounded professionals.

title: Belonging: A Sense of Place : 6-Week Art Therapy Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Avenue East, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee, for a six-week closed art therapy group for adults!
Belonging: A Sense of Place invites participants to slow down, connect with nature, and explore their inner world through creative expression. Each session includes a brief meditation, gentle check-in, nature-inspired art-making, and optional sharing.
 
Across the six weeks, the garden becomes both a setting and a metaphor for exploring themes of memory, identity, place, belonging, relationship, and what makes somewhere feel like “home.” Each session introduces a distinct theme while contributing to an overarching exploration of belonging and our relationship with the natural world.
 
As a closed group, participants are invited to attend all six sessions. The continuity of the series offers opportunities to build trust, develop connections, and deepen reflection as the sessions unfold.
 
The group is facilitated by Mahja Kabir, an artist and art therapy trainee who creates gentle, creative spaces that support reflection, care, growth, and connection. Art therapy uses the creative process as a way to explore emotions, experiences, relationships, and self-awareness, with no emphasis on artistic skill or producing a finished artwork.
 
Wednesdays, January 20 through February 24, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. (six sessions).
Public $120, TBG Members $90 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.

title: Jan 21 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Jan 21, 2027
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-january-21-2027)**

**Verifier-Gated Generative Tutoring: When the LLM Writes Lessons but Never Decides Mastery**

Adaptive tutors increasingly let LLMs both generate content and decide mastery — a risky coupling. dino.study separates those roles: models draft interactive lessons under verifier gates, while deterministic Python BKT + FSRS tracks mastery and review timing. I'll show the production architecture (Expo app + Bun API + Postgres prerequisite graphs), cost (\~$0.04/lesson), and an honest LLM-simulated N=30/arm dry-run that is not a human peer-reviewed study.

The talk is code-forward with a live demo. Aimed at ML/CV practitioners curious about evaluation, mastery modeling, and shipping educational AI.

*About the Speaker*

[Animesh Alang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/animesh-alang-232713132) is a UCSC Computer Engineering junior building dino.study. He founded SlugAI, serves as President of CruzHacks, and was Cloud Track winner at NVIDIA Hack-a-Claw.

**Building CAD for Machine Intelligence: The Future of AI-Driven Engineering**

What does it take to build AI systems that can reason about geometry, design mechanical parts, and automate engineering workflows? In this talk, we introduce Quartz, a CAD system built for machine intelligence, and explore how high-performance geometry execution, reinforcement learning, and massively parallel environments enable AI agents to learn engineering through design and iteration.

We demonstrate how AI can create and modify complex assemblies while preserving editable CAD histories, and share our vision for the future of AI-driven engineering.

*About the Speaker*

[Debao Huang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/debao-huang/) is currently a Research Scientist at Spectral Labs, where he develops AI-native CAD systems and foundation models for automating engineering design. He obtained his Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from The Ohio State University.

**Does 70% Mean 70%? Building an Honest Tennis Win-Probability Engine**

When a model says a tennis player has a 70% chance to win, does that player win 70% of the time? I built Tiebreak, a win-probability engine trained on about 900,000 ATP matches that layers surface-adjusted Elo, a point-by-point Markov chain and gradient boosting, updating live as a match unfolds.

Early versions looked better than they were because the same match leaked into both training and test data, and I show exactly how I caught it with a chronological, match-level split. Reliability diagrams then show where the model is calibrated and where it is overconfident.

Attendees leave with a practical checklist for building and honestly evaluating any ML model that outputs probabilities.

*About the Speaker*

[Krrish Ghindani](https://www.linkedin.com/in/krrishghindani/) is a Data Science junior at the University of San Francisco on a full merit scholarship and leads USF's Data Science team at national competitions (1st place).

**Can an Open-Weight Model Power a Physical AI Agent? Serving Gemma 4 on Google TPUs with Voxel51**

In this session, we'll deploy Google's Gemma 4 on Cloud TPUs using vLLM-TorchTPU and connect it to the Voxel51 Agent. Through a live demo and inference benchmarks, we'll explore how open-weight models can support Physical AI workflows, examining latency, throughput, and the infrastructure tradeoffs behind building reliable AI agents.

*About the Speaker*

[Adonai Vera](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adonai-vera/) is a Machine Learning Engineer and DevRel at Voxel51 with over 7 years of experience building computer vision and machine learning models using TensorFlow, Docker, and OpenCV.

title: Aimi Kobayashi Piano Recital
location: Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
description:
Experience an unforgettable evening with acclaimed Japanese pianist Aimi Kobayashi, celebrated for her “perfect technique, a light touch, fast and virtuoso” playing. A Fourth Prize winner at the 18th International Chopin Piano Competition, Kobayashi has captivated audiences around the world with her exceptional artistry, expressive depth, and extraordinary musicality. From her early beginnings at the age of three to performances with leading orchestras across Japan and Europe, she has established herself as one of Japan’s most sought-after pianists of her generation. Her distinguished career includes performances with the Orchestra of the Eighteenth Century, Moscow Virtuosi, Yomiuri Nippon Symphony Orchestra, Japan Philharmonic Orchestra, New Japan Philharmonic, Tonhalle-Orchester Zürich, Tokyo Symphony Orchestra, and Münchner Philharmoniker. Her recordings for Warner Classics feature works by Bach, Beethoven, Chopin, Liszt, and her latest album, Schubert (2024). Join us for an inspiring evening of piano artistry as Aimi Kobayashi brings her remarkable talent and passion to the stage. Concert Program: Beethoven: Bagatelles, Op. 126 Chopin: Nocturne in F major, Op. 15, No. 1 Chopin: Mazurka in F minor, Op. 68, No. 4 Chopin: Ballade No. 1 in G minor, Op. 23 Schubert: Piano Sonata No. 20 in A major, D. 959 *Concert program subject to change. title: Investing 101: What you need to know
location: Hillcrest, Auditorium
description:
Whether you are starting out or learning more about your current investments, this seminar will help you make sense of the complex world of investing. We will cover the three asset classes: stocks, bonds, and cash plus simple ways to get started with investing. In this easy-to-understand seminar, Teri will set out the advantages of each of the three major tax-sheltered investing plans for Canadians: Tax-Free Savings Accounts (TFSAs), Registered Retirement Savings Plans (RRSPs) and the new First Home Savings Accounts (FHSAs).
Presented by Teri Courchene, BA, MA, MEd, CSC
Teri earned master’s degrees in economics and in education.  In her earlier career as an economist, she was Director of Economic Research at a major bank. In her second career, Teri taught at her own small Montessori school for 10 years, then switched to tutoring students in math. In her third career, she taught investing for 5 years at the University of Toronto School of Continuing Studies.
Registration is encouraged
. Drop-ins are welcome until capacity is reached.

location: Hillcrest, Auditorium
description:
Due to Hillcrest Library closure on July 27, this event will be postponed until January 2027.
In Montreal, at the dawn of the 20th century, a poor boy falls in love with a girl whose sorrow turns into pearls. He sells them to a ruthless pawnbroker, who hungers for more. Tempted by greed, the boy must choose between love and fortune. The choice could damn his soul.
The 2026 Oscar® Winner for Best Animated Short Film from the acclaimed team of Chris Lavis and Maciek Szczerbowski. This meticulously crafted film is a testament to the magic of stop-motion animation. With handmade puppets, mesmerizing narration by Colm Feore and a haunting score by Patrick Watson,
The Girl Who Cried Pearls
is a timeless parable of desire, deception and the price of innocence. (25 minutes)
Also screening from the same Oscar winning team with be
Higglety Pigglety Pop! or There Must Be More to Life
. This live-action/animated adaptation of Maurice Sendak's book features the voices of Meryl Streep and Forest Whitaker.
The story follows Jennie the terrier's suspenseful and unexpectedly moving journey to gain new experiences and realize her dream of becoming the star of the World Mother Goose Theatre. (23 minutes)
Films courtesy of the National Film Board of Canada (NFB).

title: Jan 27 - Physical AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup: Purpose-Built Robots
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join us for the Physical AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup series focused on robotics use cases. In this session we will focus on purpose-built robots.

**Date, Time and Location**

Jan 27, 2027
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/physical-ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-purpose-built-robots-january-27-2027)**

**Building a Home Health Robot for Family Caregiving**

Home health is one of the most personal places a robot can work, and one of the least explored. Jacob will share how Rhem Labs is building a purpose-built tabletop robot and family app that help households keep track of health readings and daily routines, so changes in a loved one's health can be spotted earlier.

He will talk about what his own family's caregiving experience taught him about the problem, the design choices that come with building for older adults and caregivers, and how a robot earns trust in someone's home. Attendees will hear how a focused, single-purpose robot can make a real difference in everyday care.

*About the Speaker*

[Jacob Shen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jacobshenn/) is founder and CEO of Rhem Labs, a Y Combinator company building Rhem, a tabletop robot for home health. After years of caring for relatives at home, he set out to build a robot and family app that track health readings and daily routines so families can spot changes earlier.

**Closing the Loop Between Sensing and Action in Surgical Robotics**

Some of the hardest robotics problems live inside the human body, where space is tight, visibility is limited and every millimeter counts. Ali will share how Mosaic Intelligence Labs is building purpose-built surgical robots that pair sensing catheters with robotic control to reduce reliance on X-ray guidance. She will explain why today's instruments lack a real feedback loop between what they sense and how they act, and how closing that loop opens the door to safer, more precise procedures. The talk will also cover what it takes to design a robot for a single, high-stakes job and the lessons that carry over to purpose-built robots in other fields.

*About the Speaker*

[Ali Mackanic](https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-kight/) is co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Mosaic Intelligence Labs, a San Francisco company building sensing surgical robots. Her team is developing sensing catheters and robotic controls designed to reduce reliance on X-ray guidance during procedures, giving surgical instruments a real feedback loop between what they sense and how they act.

**Purpose-Built for People: The Invisible Metrics of Robot Adoption**

Your robot works. Accuracy is 0.1 mm, uptime is 24/7, the demo was flawless. Six months later, it sits switched off in a corner of the plant.

Robotics projects rarely fail on engineering metrics. They fail on the ones nobody measures: how much operators trust the robot, how a single bug is perceived, whether the robot solves the real bottleneck. Purpose-built robots have an edge here: designed around operators' real pain points, they start with trust instead of fighting for it.

Drawing on deployments in mining, oil and gas, manufacturing and pharma, Hugo Turlet walks through a real ROI breakdown, from OEE to adoption, and shows which hidden factors purpose-built design can move. Attendees will leave with a short list of invisible metrics, how to measure them, and how purpose-built design can move them.

*About the Speaker*

[Hugo Turlet](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hugo-turlet/) is a robotics engineer who leads the robotics practice at Osedea, a Montreal innovation firm. His strength is translation: he turns field needs into technical requirements, and those requirements into business models that work. A regular robotics and AI columnist on Montreal radio and an open-source contributor to Hugging Face, he works to make robotics accessible to everyone.

**Motivation and Challenges in working with Multimodal Timeseries Data**

Physical AI is having its moment, with many companies and research teams focussed on this space. But working with physical AI data means wrestling with high cardinality, complex, non-synced, multi sensor streams that are hard to explore, align and curate. In this talk, we will break down the challenges that come with multimodal time series data, and then look at the research directions this industry is pursuing, the ones that are unlocked when you can actually work with your data effectively.

*About the Speaker*

[Prerna Dhareshwar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/prernamd/) is a Machine Learning Engineer at Voxel51, where she helps customers leverage Voxel51 to accelerate dataset curation, model development, and evaluation in real-world AI workflows.

**Faster Physical AI Development with CoreWeave**

Building robots and autonomous systems means training on huge multimodal datasets, running simulation at scale, and iterating on models quickly. In this short session, CoreWeave's Head of Physical AI shares how teams are building their physical AI infrastructure today, where the bottlenecks are, and what is coming next to make it easier to go from data to deployed models.

*About the Speaker*

[Matt Shaffer](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shaffermatthew/) is a founder and research scientist, I have spent the last decade bridging the gap between frontier research and commercial reality. With a background spanning $44M+ in fundraising, product strategy, customer discovery, research, engineering, hiring, executive operations, and technical leadership, I have built and led distributed organizations to deliver AI-powered robotics across industries.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

The Board Games event is a fun, sociable and charitable event

***ALCOHOL IS PROHIBITED AND WE HAVE A ZERO TOLERANCE POLICY ON THIS - there are no second chances**

Presented by D. Grant Campbell, author of "Surviving Dementia Care: The Realities of Caregiving" (University of Toronto Press, 2026).
Please note the author will be available after the event to sign copies of his book.
Please register online.

This time we'll be reading *I Cheerfully Refuse* by Leif Enger. Here's the blurb:

Set in a not-too-distant America, *I Cheerfully Refuse* is the tale of Rainy, an aspiring musician setting sail on Lake Superior in search of his departed, deeply beloved, bookselling wife. An endearing bear of an Orphean narrator, he seeks refuge in the harbors, fogs, and remote islands of the inland sea. After encountering lunatic storms and rising corpses from the warming depths, he eventually lands to find an increasingly desperate and illiterate people, a malignant billionaire ruling class, a crumbled infrastructure, and a lawless society. As his guileless nature begins to make an inadvertent rebel of him, Rainy’s private quest for the love of his life grows into something wider and wilder, sweeping up friends and foes alike in his wake.

description:
The Faculty of Graduate Studies is hosting a session entitled Digital Research Tools for Doctoral Success. Join us!
Doctoral research involves managing complex projects, vast amounts of information, and evolving workflows. The right digital tools can help researchers work more efficiently, stay organized, and make the research process more manageable. This session explores practical tools and strategies for citation management, note-taking, collaboration, writing, project planning, and organizing your research workflow. Participants will learn how digital approaches can support effective research practices and help develop sustainable systems for navigating the demands of advanced scholarship.

description:
TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

location: S. Walter Stewart, Auditorium
description:

Afterwards, join us for a 30-minute Stay and Play activity session where children can explore sensory bins, and adults can connect with other parents and caregivers, and discover helpful resources.
These programs are specifically designed to be welcoming to neurodivergent children, including autistic children and those with sensory processing differences. The programs will take place inside S. Walter Stewart Auditorium, with access to the Sensory Room. This program is a neurodivergent positive space.
Registrants will receive a Venue Guide describing accessibility features, sensory accommodations, and further details a few weeks before the program.
For more information, please call 416-396-3975 to speak with the Children’s Librarian.

TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE

William is an expert on his Persian wife Tara: her mother, her culture, her turn-ons. Yet their marriage is collapsing fast. So he plans one last BIG surprise with the help of his infinitely patient colleague Shahriar – who is desperate for a favour of his own. https://tarragontheatre.com/plays/tarragon-season-26-27/call-me-by-my-cousins-name/

title: Dystopia Nonfiction Book Club: Regime Change
location: Toronto Reference Library, Discussion Room, 3rd Floor
description:
Join us each month to discuss issues in politics and society, and explore how powerful forces are exploiting our world and dystopian imaginings are becoming present-day realities.
February's book is
Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump
by journalists Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan. Copies of the books are available in print, eBook and Audiobook CD format. Book club attendees are encouraged to read the book in advance of the meeting.
"Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan bring us behind the scenes of a presidency that has transformed the culture, turned the Justice Department into an agent of retribution against the President's enemies and the office itself into a brazen vehicle for profit. They reveal a second term propelled by a historical irony that Trump himself has come to understand: that the indictments, the convictions, the assassination attempts, and four years of exile made him not weaker but far more powerful, more vengeful, and more willing to gamble than any President in modern history... It is also the story of something American journalists are more accustomed to chronicling in distant capitals than in their own: a President who has fundamentally altered the nature of the office he holds—and, with it, how the rest of the world understands American power."
Drop in. No registration required.

title: Feb 10 - Physical AI Meetup: Robot Brains and Models
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join us for the Physical AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup series focused on robotics use cases. In this session we will focus on robot brains and models.

**Date, Time and Location**

Feb 10, 2027
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/physical-ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-robot-brains-and-models-february-10-2027)**

**Physical AI That Adapts**

Every vision model is trained on a snapshot of the world, but robots are deployed into one that keeps changing: lighting shifts, friction drifts, objects move, actuators wear. Today the fix is a slow loop of collecting new data, retraining, validating and redeploying, which can take weeks or months. In this talk, we show how Lazy Dynamics’ LazyInfer closes that gap by treating perception, parameter learning and control as one Bayesian inference problem that runs on the device, inside the control loop.

*About the Speaker*

[Bart van Erp](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bart-van-erp/) is CTO at Lazy Dynamics. He has a background in Electrical Engineering and a PhD in the field of probabilistic machine learning.

**Robotic World Models: Cloud Versus On-Edge**

Cloud-hosted robotic world models can draw on substantial compute, while on-edge models promise local, low-latency inference; choosing between them depends on the reliability of their predictions. We examine this question through a from-scratch, gradient-verified reproduction of the proprioceptive Robotic World Model for ANYmal D, using recorded robot trajectories and CPU resources. Autoregressive training reproduces the model's long-horizon advantage over teacher forcing, while ensemble disagreement tracks the ordering of prediction errors but substantially underestimates their magnitude. On the released checkpoint's training episodes, disagreement is 33.4 times smaller than realized error at the method's 100-step rollout horizon, making it a useful ranking signal but not a calibrated error bar.

*About the Speaker*

Joyjeet Singh is an independent researcher in physics-informed machine learning and the sole author of three arXiv preprints on implicit-reasoning models, world-model reproducibility, and the planning objectives used over learned latent dynamics.

**Faster Physical AI Development with CoreWeave**

Robot brains are getting bigger. Vision language action models, world models and foundation policies all demand large training runs, fast experimentation and serving that keeps up with real robots. In this session, Narendra Kumar Vadapalli, Senior Specialist Field Engineer at CoreWeave, walks through how physical AI teams are building the infrastructure behind these models today. Drawing on his work helping customers design and scale AI platforms on Kubernetes, he will cover how teams organize multimodal training data, run distributed training and simulation side by side, and move models from experiment to deployment without rebuilding their stack each time. Attendees will leave with practical patterns for scaling robot learning workloads and a look at what is coming next.

*About the Speaker*

[Narendra Kumar Vadapalli](https://www.linkedin.com/in/narenandu/) is a Senior Specialist Field Engineer at CoreWeave, where he has helped customers design and scale AI infrastructure since 2024.

**Robot Brains and Models with Voxel51**

*About the Speaker*

[Brent Griffin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brent-griffin-0b6325b5/) is a Principal Machine Learning Scientist at Voxel51, specializing in low-cost learning on unstructured data at scale. He previously built and led the perception group at Agility Robotics and was an assistant research scientist at the University of Michigan, working at the intersection of computer vision, control, and robot learning.

It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. description:

Award winning guitarist, Rez Abbasi ( https://www.reztone.com/ ) is featured as part of the Department of Music’s 2026-2027 Oscar Peterson Jazz Artist-in-Residence.
The following session is free and open to the public.
Date: Thursday, February 11
Time: 12:30 – 1:30 p.m.
Location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall
Free Admission
REZ ABBASI
Guitarist, composer, author and 2021 Guggenheim Fellow, Rez Abbasi is among a rare
breed of artists that continue to push boundaries from within the traditions he has
embraced. Consistently placing on DownBeat magazine’s International Critics Poll in
Guitar alongside luminaries Bill Frisell and Pat Metheny since 2014, Abbasi continues to
forge new ground with his multi-dimensional projects.
“Abbasi is living, breathing proof that jazz music can be as vital and boundary-pushing as
ever.” AllAboutJazz.com.
Born in Karachi, Pakistan, migrating to Southern California at the age of four, schooled
at the University of Southern California and the Manhattan School of Music in jazz and
classical music, along with a pilgrimage in India under the guidance of master
percussionist, Ustad Alla Rakha, Abbasi is a vivid synthesis of all the above stated
influences and genres.
“Mr. Abbasi succeeded in making some fairly cerebral intricacies feel intuitive and
touched by a higher purpose.” – New York Times
The Oscar Peterson Jazz Artist-in-Residence is made possible by a grant from the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities.

title: Learn to Grow Native Plants From Seed: Sowing In a Winter Wonderland
location: Cliffcrest
description:
Who says you can’t grow a garden in the winter? Winter sowing is an easy and inexpensive way to start native seeds. Through this simple method of sowing seeds during the colder months, you can plan your garden to support butterflies, bees and birds.
In this workshop, learn how surprisingly easy it is to grow native wildflowers from seed if we follow nature’s lead by embracing the cold!
In this presentation, Dorte Windmuller, a Butterflyway Ranger of the David Suzuki Foundation, will lead a hands-on experience of seed cleaning and packing. Participants can take some seed packets home for your garden or balcony.
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile
Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​

title: Thailand Sea Side Discovery: Bangkok, Phuket and Krabi Island
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
Join us for an unforgettable 10-day Meetup adventure through Thailand, blending culture, temples, islands, beaches, and relaxed free time. This trip is a true Meetup - designed for those who want to travel the world and explore exotic destinations like Thailand, but don’t want to do it alone. We are traveling as a group, while still enjoying flexibility and optional experiences.
This journey blends the energy of Bangkok, the tropical beauty of Phuket, and the laid-back charm of Krabi, creating the perfect balance of culture, nature, and downtime. We will explore iconic temples, cruise through stunning islands, relax on white-sand beaches, and enjoy free time to wander, shop, or simply slow down and soak it all in.

**Trip Highlights**
• Bangkok City & Temple Tour
• Optional Ayutthaya Day Trip
• Flight to Phuket included
• Phi Phi Islands Tour
• Big Buddha Visit
• Scenic drive from Phuket to Krabi
• 4 Island Hopping Tour with Picnic

**Who is this trip for**
✔ Solo travelers who don’t want to travel alone
✔ People who want structure without feeling rushed
✔ Travelers who enjoy a mix of sightseeing and free time
✔ Anyone who wants to experience Thailand with a fun, supportive group

This adventure is ideal for solo travelers, friends, couples and even families, who want the comfort of a group while keeping the experience fun and social.

The best way to see what it's like is to check the gallery with past pix from our previous trip: https://photos.app.goo.gl/qXfrs5zQp5rULNvb9

For a detailed Day By Day itinerary [Click Here](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8) to fill out the form and receive information.

**Land Tour cost $2997 per person, double occupancy (we match roommates for those willing to share and save).**
**If you want your own room: Solo occupancy $3867**

**The only way to secure your spot for this meetup is a $325 deposit that is refundable up to 90 days before departure.**
**[Click here for secure deposit link](https://www.paypal.com/instantcommerce/checkout/4K9UHVSFEL8UA)**

When you make a deposit be sure to fill out this [ATTENDEE’S FORM](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScjUyrsruOGiQWnWgqn-hiNuIpheVNCkYkavtNyYNsAnn0tZA/viewform).
As mentioned, . . . the cost is $2997. This is for the "Land" portion only. **International airfare is not included.** This gives you the flexibility to have a flight with timing that works best for you. Or to use points/miles.
Ekaterina can also help arrange your airfare.
To contact her for more info, [CLICK HERE](https://www.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=14363992) [to send her a message.](https://secure.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=14363992)

**What is included in the cost:**
✔ Meet & greet upon arrival at the airport
✔ 3 Nights in Bangkok
✔ 3 Nights in Phuket
✔ 3 Nights in Krabi
✔ Accommodation with daily breakfast as mention
✔ Airfare from Bangkok to Phuket
✔Transfer services in private air-conditioned vehicle
✔English speaking guide throughout program
✔Entrance fees, other boat fees where applicable
✔ Meals as listed in the program
✔Bottled water on coach during transfer
✔ Airport arrival and departure transfers in Bangkok
✔ Airport arrival transfer in Phuket (one time together for the group)
✔ Airport departure transfers in Krabi
✔ Road transfer from Phuket to Krabi

**What is not included:**

* International Airfare
* Meals not mentioned in the itinerary
* Visa
* Early check-in and late check-out
* Tips, drinks, personal expenses and others
* Travel insurance

Want more info?
[Click Here to fill out our info request form](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)
OR
RSVP to the event with your email to receive additional info.
OR
[CLICK HERE to send me a message](https://secure.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=14363992)
Whatever is easiest for you!

Still have questions?
We do a Q & A Zoom once a month.
[CLICK HERE for our Q & A Zoom](https://www.meetup.com/moretoexplore/events/296044209/). RSVP on that event to get a reminder for the zoom.

We believe in good, decent social. This event is cross posted to several other groups and the number of RSVPs on each is not reflective. We have a set of sister groups where we post our local free, local/regional camping, and our overseas events too.

title: Language Exchange & Social Event @ Madison Ave Pub by Toronto Babel
description:
TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

📩 **CONTACT:** Terry (Organizer)
💸 **E-transfer:** [tmg8@wealthsimple.me](mailto:tmg8@wealthsimple.me)

🔗 **Stay Connected & Join Us:**

📸 Instagram: [https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel](https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel)

📅 Meetup: [https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel)

💬 WhatsApp Group Chat: [https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7](https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7)

📘 Facebook: [https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel](https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel)

👉 **See what’s coming up and RSVP on our calendar:**
[https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar)

🛡️ **Community Guidelines:**
Toronto Babel is a welcoming, inclusive, and safe space for everyone. Our events focus on language exchange, cultural sharing, and friendship — **not for dating or matchmaking.** Harassment and inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated. If you experience or witness anything concerning, please let an organizer know so we can help.

Come for the conversations, stay for the community! 🌎💬❤️

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Get the Jump on Spring 2027
location: ON
description:
Where the Plant People Meet



Shake off the winter blues and start the countdown to spring at Toronto Botanical Garden’s much-loved Get the Jump on Spring one-day garden extravaganza. Whether you’re a seasoned gardener, a curious beginner, or simply dreaming of warmer days, this annual event brings together plant lovers, expert growers, and local makers for a joyful, inspiration-packed kickoff to spring. 



Saturday, February 20, 2027, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.FREE Admission. $2 suggested minimum donation 







What to Expect













Plant Community Connections 



Meet fellow plant enthusiasts, swap stories, ask questions, and connect with horticultural societies, plant and seed vendors, local makers, and other community groups dedicated to gardening, nature, and sustainable living. 









Over 40 Local Makers & Eco-Vendors



Discover unique houseplants, organic seed vendors, botanical-inspired products, garden accessories, natural wellness items, and artisan goods from over 40 local makers and growers. 









Interested in Participating in 2027




APPLICATIONS FOR VENDOR SPACES IS NOW OPEN














Visit the Plant Doctor



Have questions about the health or care of your indoor plant(s)? Looking for help on how to repot your plant? Bring in your plant(s) or a photo, and our horticulturists will provide you with an on-the-spot assessment and treatment. Examples of services offered include: Pruning, repotting, leaf cleaning and pest removal. 



Please note: If your plant is HEAVILY infested with pests, you should keep it at home and only bring in a photo. This service is ideal for small or young plants. We will not be able to help you unload/load your plant. 









Free Plant & Seed Swap



Bring as many plants as you wish to trade. If there isn’t anything of interest on the table when you arrive, add your plant(s) and take a ticket to redeem later when you see something new you’d like to try.  



Drop by the Weston Family Library, which houses our Seed Library. You can borrow seeds for FREE! If you have extra seeds, package and label them to add to our seed library collection. There will be a seed library assistant to assist you with your selections and contributions. 















Seasonal Plants & Seed Sales



Shop a curated selection of seeds, unique plants, and specialty offerings from trusted growers—perfect for getting a head start on your garden plans. Drop by the Garden Shop to learn more about our new online plant shop with at-home delivery, pre-order early-blooming hellebores, and sample a flight of local Ontario honey. 









Pop up Plant Cafe



Recharge with a coffee, tea, or freshly baked cookie, square, or scone. Gluten-free, Dairy-free & nut-free options available. Bistro seating is available. Operated by Daniel et Daniel. 















Free Garden Chats



Grow your gardening confidence with interactive sessions in the Weston Family Library led by the Toronto Master Gardeners. No registration required. 









Free Family Fun



Bring the whole family along! Kids can enjoy a drop-in, plant-themed craft to take home or, if you prefer a quiet moment, roast marshmallow over the outdoor firepit or simply relax together and cuddle with a book in our cozy indoor corners. 














Ways you can make this event more sustainable




TBG will have waste stations for reuseable, recyclable and compostable materials with hands-on volunteers to assist.



Bring your water bottle and take advantage of our complimentary water station, bring your mug, plate, or cutlery.



You are encouraged to bring your reusable bags or boxes to carry your seeds, plants, or garden-related treasures home.









How to get there



Click here for directions and parking information.

title: Global Philosophy Research Interest Group Talk (Jeannie Miller, University of Toronto)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Global Philosophy Research Interest Group is delighted to welcome as guest speaker Jeannie Miller, an associate professor in the Department of Near and Middle Eastern Studies at the University of Toronto. Her book, The Quibbler: Al-Jahiz’s Equivocations in Kitab al-Hayawan and Beyond is a study of the Arabic writings of al-Jahiz, a foundational 9th-century author and analyzes al-Jahiz’s literary style and unique voice as a performative demonstration of good thinking, according to his definition. She is currently working on several interconnected studies of the reception and afterlife of Abbasid texts in premodern Islamicate contexts, using manuscripts as evidence. How were these texts read before the modernizing movements of the 19th and 20th centuries and the advent of a modern notion of “literature”?

title: Galapagos Islands Expedition ~ Untouched Nature in all its Splendor! Small Group
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
***It's a Meetup . . . in the Galápagos!!***

**This Meetup Event is for the nature lovers, for the curious explorers and the adventurers who want to experience nature in all its splendor & diversity.**

The Galápagos Islands are a volcanic archipelago in the Pacific Ocean, considered one of the world's foremost destinations for wildlife-viewing. It's a place where lizards swim, birds walk, and humans — for once — don't take center stage. In 1835 a 26-year-old Charles Darwin introduced the Galápagos Islands to the world with his theory of evolution.

As amazing as you think the Galápagos Islands would be, they exceed all expectations of our group in 2023 and 2025! That sea lion above in our group photo is not a prop! It was very real, ready to play and pose for a picture. You can see sea lions, giant lizards and many other exotic and friendly creatures, waddling on the streets, playing in the sand or just chilling (sun bathing) on a bench!

***We will explore and experience:***

* The famous Galapagos penguin and blue footed boobies. Swim with sea turtles and sea lions.
* Tortuga Bay Beach for swimming, snorkeling, kayaking or surfing with unique marine life.
* Get close and personal with the giant tortoises roaming in their natural habitat
* Explore the Tintoreras islet, home of the white tip sharks and its shark tunnel.
* Visit the Charles Darwin Station, to observe giant tortoises and their babies and learn about this majestic animal.
* Snorkeling around the shore of the Tijeretas Bay
* Boat ride to Kicker Rock with snorkeling
* Sailing to Santa Cruz Island.
* Sail to Isabela Island, the largest of the archipelago.
* Boat tour to Tuneles De Cabo Rosa, a formation of series of above ocean arches, creating an unique snorkeling experience.
* Explore cavernous underground Lava Tunnels.
* Tour the Galapagos rainforest habitat
* San Cristobal Island with visit to the Interpretation Center
* Visit to Los Gemelos, a haven for bird watchers!
* Visit Sierra Negra and Chico Volcano. A 10-mile challenging hike (for those who are interested)
* El Trapiche to see the old methods of extracting cane juice, roasting coffee beans and techniques of distillery.
* Quito with a full day tour and visit to the Equator line
* Visit to the town of Puerto Baquerizo Moreno.

***Land Tour cost US$4650 per person, double occupancy***
***(we match roommates for those wishing to share)***
***Solo occupancy additional US$990***
**\*\*\*Airfare not included\*\*\***

We have a second departure with the same itinerary: March 16-26, 2027
**[Click here to go to the event](https://www.meetup.com/moretoexplore/events/312009746/)**

· Galapagos National Park entrance fee
· Isabela island entrance fee
· All transportation during the tour
· 24/7 assistance in the islands
· Airport Transfers to hotel. (in – out)

WHAT IS NOT INCLUDED:

* Airfare to Galapagos (unless booking the group fare from LA)

* Tips

title: Language Exchange & Social Event @ Madison Ave Pub by Toronto Babel
description:
TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

📩 **CONTACT:** Terry (Organizer)
💸 **E-transfer:** [tmg8@wealthsimple.me](mailto:tmg8@wealthsimple.me)

🔗 **Stay Connected & Join Us:**

📸 Instagram: [https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel](https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel)

📅 Meetup: [https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel)

💬 WhatsApp Group Chat: [https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7](https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7)

📘 Facebook: [https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel](https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel)

👉 **See what’s coming up and RSVP on our calendar:**
[https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar)

🛡️ **Community Guidelines:**
Toronto Babel is a welcoming, inclusive, and safe space for everyone. Our events focus on language exchange, cultural sharing, and friendship — **not for dating or matchmaking.** Harassment and inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated. If you experience or witness anything concerning, please let an organizer know so we can help.

Come for the conversations, stay for the community! 🌎💬❤️

title: Postgres Conference 2027: Celebrating 20 Years of Community & Innovation! 🐘🎉
description:
Toronto Postgres
Join us as Postgres Conference turns 20! We are marking two decades of community-driven database excellence by gathering developers, DBAs, architects, and maintainers from around the globe who build, manage, and scale Postgres in production.

**📍 Venue:** San Jose Marriott, San Jose, California
📅 **Dates:** Apr 21, 2027 – Apr 23, 2027

**Two Decades of Real-World Engineering**
Reaching this milestone is a testament to the strength and resilience of open source engineering. Our community continues to push data systems forward, from core protocol advancements and a thriving extension ecosystem to autovacuum tuning, vector workloads, high availability, and data security.

## **Interested in Speaking? 📢**

Help shape our 20th anniversary program! We invite practitioners, researchers, and community members to submit speaker proposals. Share your hard-won production lessons, architecture strategies, security and compliance insights, post-mortems, or technical benchmarks with our global audience.

## **Conference Tracks**

Our comprehensive, multi-day, multi-track program offers deep technical sessions and holistic professional growth:

* **Essentials:** Fundamental concepts, best practices, and foundational knowledge for new and growing Postgres users, including secure configuration and access control basics..
* **Dev:** Application design, ORMs, query optimization, advanced SQL features, and secure coding practices such as preventing SQL injection and using row-level security.
* **Ops:** High availability, replication, backup & recovery, performance tuning, and infrastructure management, along with hardening, encryption, auditing, and compliance.
* **Extensions:** Extending Postgres functionality, custom extension development, and ecosystem integration, plus security tooling like pgaudit and extension supply chain safety.
* **AI:** Vector embeddings, pgvector, LLM integration, AI-driven data pipelines, data sovereignty, governance, and protecting sensitive data used in AI workloads.
* **Professional Development & Wellness:** Career growth, engineering leadership, mental health, and maintaining work-life balance.
* **Life & Fun:** Community stories, creative technical pursuits, and social networking activities.

**How to Submit Your Proposal**
Ready to share your knowledge with the Postgres community? Submit your proposal at [https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027/program/proposals/new](https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027/program/proposals/new)

**Visit the official conference portal to learn more about Postgres Conference 2027:**
**👉 [https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027 ](https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027)**

**Questions?**
Reach out via [organizers@postgresconf.org](mailto:organizers@postgresconf.org) with any general questions or guidance regarding your proposal.

**Interested in Sponsoring?**
Visit the sponsorship page at [https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027/sponsorships](https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027/sponsorships)
